articles.title: Potassium-Competitive Acid Blockers in GERD and Helicobacter pylori Infection: The Emerging Role of Fexuprazan.
articles.abstract: The pharmacological control of gastric acid secretion has evolved substantially over the past five decades, yet clinically important limitations remain with delayed-release proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), including delayed onset of action, meal dependency, nocturnal acid breakthrough, and variable intragastric pH control. Potassium-competitive acid blockers (P-CABs) represent a major advance in antisecretory therapy by providing rapid, potent, sustained, and meal-independent inhibition of the gastric H+,K+-ATPase through a reversible mechanism of action. Among currently available P-CABs, fexuprazan is a relatively recent agent for which an expanding body of pharmacological and clinical evidence has become available. This review critically examines its pharmacology, experimental biology, and clinical efficacy, with particular emphasis on gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and Helicobacter pylori infection. Randomized controlled trials and real-world studies demonstrate that fexuprazan is non-inferior to esomeprazole in healing erosive esophagitis, with evidence of rapid symptom improvement, effective nocturnal symptom control, and greater dosing flexibility. Emerging data also suggest potential benefit in extra-esophageal manifestations of GERD. Experimental studies indicate anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and epithelial barrier-protective properties, although their clinical relevance remains to be established. In H. pylori infection, the profound and sustained intragastric pH elevation achieved with P-CABs may enhance eradication therapy, and fexuprazan-based triple, quadruple, and dual regimens have shown promising efficacy and tolerability. Overall, current evidence indicates that fexuprazan is an effective and well-tolerated P-CAB that may overcome some of the limitations of conventional PPIs, while ongoing comparative and long-term studies will further define its place in the management of acid-related disorders.

articles.title: Mitochondrial Transplantation as a Therapeutic Strategy: From Energy Replacement to Metabolic and Immune Reprogramming.
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction drives diseases, including ischemia-reperfusion injury, neurodegenerative disorders, cardiovascular disease, metabolic syndrome, and inflammation. Conventional mitochondria-targeted strategies offer only partial rescue and are insufficient for severe, irreversible damage. Mitochondrial transplantation (MT)-the delivery of exogenously isolated functional mitochondria to injured cells-has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy that directly restores mitochondrial bioenergetic function and may subsequently modify the tissue microenvironment. This Review examines the entire MT pipeline, from mitochondrial source selection, isolation and preservation, to in vivo delivery strategies. We critically examine the multiple mechanisms underlying MT's therapeutic efficacy, including cellular uptake and intracellular integration, energy restoration and metabolic reprogramming, redox rebalancing, remodeling of mitochondrial quality control (fusion/fission, mitophagy, biogenesis), and immunomodulation. We summarize preclinical and clinical applications across multiple organ systems-heart, nervous system, liver, kidney, lung, skeletal muscle, retina-as well as in oncology and aging. We analyze five major translational bottlenecks: the lack of standardized manufacturing protocols, undefined dose-response relationships, immunogenicity and long-term safety uncertainties, the decisive impact of mitochondrial heterogeneity, and regulatory ambiguity. We outline future directions-mechanistic deepening, engineered target delivery, individualized mitochondrial medicine, combinatorial regimens, and a phased clinical roadmap. MT is not merely energy supplementation; it may reshape cellular metabolism, quality control networks, and immune microenvironments, representing a shift from pharmacological modulation of mitochondrial function toward organelle replacement strategies. Despite challenges, these advances may facilitate individualized mitochondrial therapies as a proposed future direction.

articles.title: Biosimilar Development Considerations for Therapeutic Proteins With Limited Systemic Exposure: A Landscape Analysis and Pathway Evaluation.
articles.abstract: Biosimilar development for therapeutic proteins (TPs) with limited systemic exposure presents distinct challenges, as the new paradigm based on comparative analytical assessments plus pharmacokinetic similarity without a comparative efficacy study (CES) is inapplicable. Of 19 TPs with limited systemic exposure, 15 are well-characterized, of which 12 have at least one CES-feasible indication. The remaining 3 may require alternative strategies, including pharmacodynamic (PD) biomarker approaches or optimized CES designs, underscoring the need for proactive regulatory engagement.

articles.title: Ritlecitinib lipid microsphere development and model-facilitated determination of regional gastrointestinal delivery in healthy volunteers.
articles.abstract: Colonic drug delivery has the potential to provide therapeutic benefit for diseases like Ulcerative Colitis (UC) and Crohn's disease (CD) by elevating local drug concentrations while minimizing adverse effects associated with systemic exposure. Achieving colonic drug delivery requires deliberate formulation development optimally supported by Physiologically Based Biopharmaceutics Models (PBBMs) that may predict colonocyte exposure and drug concentration in the colon lumen. In this study, ritlecitinib (Litfulo™), a covalent inhibitor of JAK3 and TEC family kinases, was incorporated into modified release (MR) lipid microsphere formulations to achieve colonic delivery. To assess in vivo performance, two ritlecitinib MR formulations were administered to healthy human volunteers, pre- and post-prandially, and a ritlecitinib oral solution was administered as a control. Using a combination of the resulting pharmacokinetic dataset, ritlecitinib physicochemical properties, in vitro release profiles of the administered formulations, and formulation-specific gastrointestinal transit profiles, a PBBM was established to predict the ritlecitinib dose fraction absorbed in each gastrointestinal compartment, pre- and post-prandially. In the fasted state, the ritlecitinib dose fraction absorbed in the colon (Facolon) was enhanced for both the faster-releasing (Facolon: 0.38 ± 0.07) and slower-releasing (Facolon: 0.40 ± 0.08) MR formulations relative to the oral solution (Facolon: 0.01 ± 0.01). In the fed state, Facolon was consistent for the slower-releasing formulation (Facolon: 0.38 ± 0.07), whereas Facolon for the faster-releasing formulation was notably reduced (Facolon: 0.27 ± 0.09), indicating that consistent colonic delivery across prandial states depends on release rate optimization. Clinical Trial Records: ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT06172348; EU CTR number 2023-505603-23-00.

articles.title: 3,4-dehydro-3‑hydroxy-α-lapachone, a novel naphthoquinone, ameliorates hepatic fibrosis by targeting the guanine nucleotide-binding protein G(i) subunit alpha-2/peroxiredoxin 1 signaling axis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatic fibrosis progresses to irreversible cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma without timely clinical intervention. Despite substantial clinical burden, no targeted therapies are currently approved specifically for hepatic fibrosis across the broad spectrum of chronic liver diseases, leaving a critical unmet need. Verbena officinalis L. has long been used in traditional medicine for hepatobiliary disorders, yet its active constituents, molecular targets, and mechanisms of antifibrotic action remain largely uncharacterized. PURPOSE: This study was designed to identify novel anti-hepatic fibrosis components of Verbena officinalis and elucidate their underlying mechanisms of action. METHODS: Therapeutic efficacy was assessed in bile duct ligation and carbon tetrachloride-induced liver fibrosis mouse models. Bioactivity-guided fractionation coupled with high-content screening was applied to isolate active metabolites. Drug affinity responsive target stability identified candidate targets; direct binding was validated via surface plasmon resonance, cellular thermal shift assay, and molecular docking. Mechanisms were confirmed through integrated molecular and functional studies. RESULTS: The ethyl acetate fraction exhibited the most potent anti-hepatic fibrotic activity, from which thirty-four metabolites, including two previously undescribed naphthoquinones (1 and 2) and one new dammarane-type triterpenoid (16), were isolated. Compound 1, identified as 3,4-dehydro-3‑hydroxy-α-lapachone (DH), demonstrated robust anti-fibrotic efficacy. Notably, DH at 10 mg/kg achieved in vivo efficacy comparable to the clinical agent pirfenidone at 200 mg/kg under the tested experimental conditions. Mechanistically, DH directly binds guanine nucleotide-binding protein G(i) subunit alpha-2 (GNAI2) at residues Phe171 and Leu250, suppressing the GNAI2-peroxiredoxin 1 (PRDX1) signaling axis to attenuate fibrogenesis. GNAI2 is consistently associated with fibrotic progression across multiple disease contexts and acts as an important functional mediator of hepatic stellate cell activation and hepatic fibrosis. CONCLUSION: This work establishes DH as an anti-fibrotic agent with a rigorously validated protein target and binding mechanism, addressing a longstanding translational gap in phytochemical research. DH acts primarily through GNAI2-PRDX1 pathway inhibition. We acknowledge that DH possesses well-described redox-active properties and may therefore engage additional intracellular targets; accordingly, the GNAI2-PRDX1 axis represents the primary validated mediator rather than the exclusive mechanism of action. These findings establish GNAI2 as a novel therapeutic target and identify DH as a promising lead compound for the development of novel anti-fibrotic agents.

articles.title: Controlling the uncontrollable? navigating naturalistic and controlled dosing in cannabis research.
articles.abstract: Cannabis research is advancing rapidly, yet fundamental questions persist regarding the optimal design of human studies to empirically assess the potential harms and benefits of cannabis. There exist central methodological differences between studies that rely on controlled dose paradigms, ensuring internal validity, and those that utilize naturalistic, self-administration approaches which better reflect real-world use. Controlled paradigms offer precision and regulatory alignment but fail to capture the complexity of real-world cannabis consumption. Naturalistic designs enhance ecological validity but introduce variability and pose challenges for dosing, safety, and replicability. This perspective article presents two methods: one emphasizing the scientific rigor and utility of controlled dose paradigms for regulatory outcomes (e.g., FDA), and the other advocating for naturalistic models that prioritize real-world relevance of legal market cannabis consumption which can inform policy decisions (e.g., guidelines around high THC concentrate). However, rather than representing competing alternatives, controlled laboratory and naturalistic paradigms occupy distinct positions within the evidentiary framework of cannabinoid research, each addressing scientific questions that the other cannot. An integrated methods section proposes ways to incorporate the best features of both approaches to advance cannabinoid science study design.

articles.title: The cGAS-STING pathway in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: mechanistic insights and therapeutic opportunities.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a highly prevalent chronic metabolic liver disease worldwide, encompassing a spectrum that includes simple steatosis, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), liver fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), with immune-metabolic-inflammatory dysregulation at its core pathogenesis. The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway serves as the central axis of cytosolic DNA sensing and innate immune activation. Endogenous stimuli, including mitochondrial DNA leakage, DNA damage, and gut microbial DNA translocation, can persistently activate this pathway, which in turn regulates lipid metabolism imbalance, hepatic inflammation amplification, hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation, and malignant transformation through downstream signaling axes, driving the full spectrum of MASLD pathology. Molecules associated with the cGAS-STING pathway may serve as non-invasive diagnostic biomarkers for MASLD, and natural compounds, traditional Chinese medicine, and nanosystems targeting this pathway have demonstrated promising therapeutic effects. This review systematically summarizes the molecular mechanisms of the cGAS-STING pathway, its regulatory roles in MASLD, and advances in targeted therapy, providing a theoretical foundation for disease mechanism elucidation and the development of diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Insights from multi-omics on GLP-1 receptor agonists in type 2 diabetes and obesity.
articles.abstract: Glucagon like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have revolutionized the management of T2D and obesity. T2D clustering highlights distinct phenotypes that differ in GLP-1RA benefit. While they have markedly improved quality of life for many individuals, converging evidence indicates that genetic variation, metabolomic remodeling, and gut microbiota composition contribute to substantial inter-individual variability in GLP-1RA efficacy and tolerability. GLP-1RAs, in return, can variably affect the metabolome and microbiome composition in treated individuals. This review focuses on human multi-omics GLP-1RA intervention studies, complemented by relevant mechanistic preclinical evidence. Genetic variation in GLP1R, TCF7L2, and other loci has been associated with differences in glycaemic and weight outcomes, although most findings remain preliminary, inconsistent across populations, or not yet replicated. Pharmacometabolomic studies show recurrent of lipid-related pathways including, glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids, ceramides, amino acids, and bile acids, with drug-specific signatures. GLP-1RAs are also associated with changes in gut microbial composition, including taxa such as Akkermansia and Bacteroides, although the direction and clinical significance of these changes vary across studies due to methodological and population heterogeneity. Multi-omics and AI-based models show promise for predicting treatment response by integrating genetic, metabolic, microbial, and clinical data to supporting more effective and individualized therapy and advancing precision medicine.

articles.title: From pathophysiology to therapy: dual and triple agonists as a new frontier in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as the most prevalent chronic liver condition worldwide, reflecting the growing global burden of obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D). The complex pathophysiology of MASLD, characterized by insulin resistance (IR), lipotoxicity, and chronic low-grade inflammation, necessitates therapeutic strategies that address systemic metabolic dysfunction rather than isolated hepatic markers. Current evidence highlights the synergistic potential of targeting multiple incretin and metabolic pathways. Dual agonists, most notably Tirzepatide (a GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist), have demonstrated profound efficacy in clinical trials (SURPASS and SURMOUNT programs), achieving significant reductions in hemoglobin A1c, body weight, and liver fat content. Furthermore, dual GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonists like Survodutide and Cotadutide offer complementary benefits by enhancing energy expenditure and modulating hepatic lipid metabolism. The development of triple agonists, such as Retatrutide (targeting GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptors), represents a further escalation in potency, showing unprecedented results in liver fat reduction and weight loss. The integration of these multi-target agents, together with emerging pathways involving amylin analogues and pan-PPAR agonists like Chiglitazar, marks a paradigm shift toward holistic cardiometabolic management. These therapies not only target the resolution of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis and fibrosis but also address the interconnected risks of cardiovascular and renal complications. This review aims to explore the evolving landscape of pharmacological interventions, focusing on the emergence of dual and triple receptor agonists as a transformative frontier in metabolic dysfunction and MASLD therapy.

articles.title: SphK1/S1P signaling network: From molecular mechanism to therapeutic targeting.
articles.abstract: Sphingosine kinase 1 (SphK1) is a key rate-limiting enzyme in the sphingolipid metabolic network. It generates sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) by catalyzing the phosphorylation of Sphingosine (Sph). It plays a key regulatory role in various physiological and pathological processes such as cell proliferation, survival, migration, inflammatory response and immune regulation. SphK1 closely connects intracellular lipid metabolism with extracellular GPCR signaling network, forming a complex "inside-out" signal transduction system. In this review, we focus on the current understanding of SphK1, including its structure characteristics, activation mechanism and signal transduction pathway. We also review the roles of SphK1 pathway in tumor, inflammation and immunity, cardiovascular, nervous system, digestive system, respiratory system and metabolic disease. Establishing a correlation between SphK1 or the SphK1/S1P signal axis and targeted drugs such as inhibitors, agonists, even some natural Chinese medicines, provides important theoretical support for understanding the potential of SphK1 as a therapeutic target. Finally, we propose future research directions based on current advances and shortcomings.

articles.title: Mechanisms of cetuximab resistance in head and neck squamous cell Carcinoma: Focus on the EGFR-ERK pathway.
articles.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is the sixth most common cancer worldwide. Major risk factors include tobacco use, excessive alcohol consumption, and infection with oncogenic human papillomaviruses (HPV). Despite advances in treatment, HNSCC remains associated with poor outcomes, particularly in patients with advanced or recurrent/metastatic disease. The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) has been recognized as a key oncogenic driver in HNSCC, as it is frequently overexpressed and promotes activation of multiple pro-tumorigenic signaling pathways, including ERK and PI3K/Akt. Cetuximab remains the only approved molecularly targeted agent directed against a tumor-associated receptor in HNSCC. However, its clinical benefit is limited by low response rates and the frequent development of resistance even in initially responsive tumors. Understanding the molecular basis of resistance to EGFR-targeted therapy is therefore critical for developing more effective pharmacological strategies and improving the clinical utility of cetuximab. In this review, we summarize EGFR alterations, activation of parallel compensatory pathways, and the reactivation of downstream signaling cascades, including PI3K/Akt and Ras/ERK, as major mechanisms underlying resistance to EGFR-targeted therapy in HNSCC. We focus particularly on the ERK signaling pathway as a central integrator of genetic, epigenetic, and adaptive resistance mechanisms. Sustained ERK activity restores downstream EGFR outputs, promotes feedback ligand production, drives epithelial-mesenchymal transition and cellular plasticity, and engages parallel oncogenic pathways, thereby enabling tumor cells to evade cetuximab-mediated EGFR blockade. Combined targeting of ERK and EGFR may therefore represent a promising strategy for overcoming cetuximab resistance in selected molecular contexts.

articles.title: Machine learning-empowered nanomaterial design and application for tear fluid-based point-of-care tests: from material discovery to clinical decision-making.
articles.abstract: Tear fluid harbors a rich array of cellular and molecular biomarkers that mirror both ocular and systemic health, positioning it as an ideal medium for non-invasive point-of-care testing (POCT). Yet its analytical utility is constrained by sub-microliter sample volumes, dynamic compositional fluctuations, and trace-level biomarker concentrations. Nanomaterials, with their surface-to-volume ratio, programmable surface chemistry, and tunable optical and catalytic properties, have been engineered into miniaturized platforms to enable target enrichment, multiplexed recognition, and signal amplification within microliter samples. Building on this material foundation, machine learning (ML) is now reshaping the entire analytical workflow. Data-driven algorithms accelerate the in-silico discovery and rational optimization of functional nanomaterials. Deep learning models further decouple matrix interference to enable ultra-sensitive, multiplexed readouts, while downstream algorithms translate multi-biomarker profiles into actionable clinical decisions. This review summarizes design strategies for ML-empowered, tear fluid-based POCT and examines how nanomaterials address the inherent constraints of tear analysis. However, clinical translation remains limited by non-standardized tear collection and data acquisition, insufficient large-scale clinical validation, and concerns regarding algorithm robustness and interpretability. The review further outlines translational applications spanning disease diagnosis, patient stratification, therapeutic monitoring, and decentralized longitudinal surveillance to support biomarker-driven precision medicine.

articles.title: Paediatric Fentanyl Population Pharmacokinetics: A Scoping Review of Published Models.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE AND PURPOSE: Fentanyl is a highly lipophilic opioid widely used within paediatric peri-operative and intensive-care settings, yet dosing is commonly titrated empirically because of substantial pharmacokinetic variability across developmental stages and clinical contexts. Population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) models provide a quantitative framework to characterise variability, but these have not been systematically synthesised. This scoping review aimed to identify and summarise published paediatric PopPK models of fentanyl, to compare model structures and covariate effects. METHODS: We searched Embase and MEDLINE databases from database inception to 17 February 2026 for paediatric PopPK models of fentanyl. Two reviewers independently screened papers and extracted data in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. RESULTS: Fourteen paediatric PopPK models of fentanyl were identified. Infants (64%, 9/14) and patient populations spanning multiple age groups (e.g., inclusion of infants and children) (64%, 9/14) were most frequently studied. Intravenous fentanyl was modelled in all studies. Two-compartment structures predominated (79%, 11/14). Body weight was the most consistently retained covariate (79%, 11/14), while maturation functions based on postnatal or postmenstrual age were frequently required in neonatal and infant cohorts (50%, 5/10). Other covariates (e.g., obesity, concomitant CYP3A modulators, and genetic factors) were variably explored and inconsistently retained. CONCLUSION: Within the existing fentanyl literature, important evidence gaps remain, particularly beyond intravenous administration. Existing models highlight body weight and developmental maturation as principal determinants of clearance and distribution. Evidence remains limited to intravenous administration, with no model data of non-intravenous routes and under-representation of dynamic covariates and external validation. Addressing these gaps will support robust model-informed precision dosing of fentanyl in children.

articles.title: Trimetazidine in Heart Failure: From Metabolic Modulation to Clinical Outcomes-A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Heart Failure (HF) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide despite major advances in guideline-directed medical therapy. Metabolic remodeling with impaired myocardial energy utilization has emerged as an important therapeutic target in HF. Trimetazidine, a metabolic modulator that partially inhibits fatty acid beta-oxidation and favours glucose oxidation, enhances myocardial energy efficiency without changing systemic hemodynamics. This narrative review summarizes the molecular mechanisms underlying the cardioprotective effects of trimetazidine and critically evaluates the available clinical evidence supporting its use in HF. Experimental studies have shown that trimetazidine increases ATP production, maintains mitochondrial function, decreases oxidative stress, inhibits apoptosis of cardiomyocytes, regulates autophagy, and reduces myocardial inflammation and fibrosis. Clinical studies and meta-analyses have shown that adjunctive therapy with trimetazidine has been associated with improved left ventricular ejection fraction, ventricular remodeling, exercise capacity, New York Heart Association functional class, biomarkers of myocardial injury, and quality of life in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. The available evidence also indicates reductions in cardiovascular hospitalization and possibly all-cause mortality, but these findings are based primarily on relatively small randomized trials and pooled analyses, and need confirmation in adequately powered multicenter studies. The potential role of trimetazidine alongside contemporary therapies, including sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors and other guideline-directed treatments, is also discussed. Overall, trimetazidine appears to be a promising adjunctive metabolic therapy that may complement existing pharmacological strategies in selected patients with heart failure (Central Illustration). Further large-scale clinical trials are needed to better define its place in contemporary HF management.

articles.title: The Forgotten First Contact: The Oral Cavity as a Site of Local Biotransformation Shaping the Chemical Form of Polyphenolic Drugs and Dietary Compounds.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Polyphenols are dietary constituents and active substances in dosage forms applied locally in the mouth, yet their bioavailability is interpreted almost exclusively in terms of intestinal absorption and colonic microbial metabolism. This review examines the oral cavity as a site of local biotransformation, a compartment that can chemically modify polyphenols before absorption, and asks whether this conversion could be measured as a phenotype. Methods: Narrative synthesis is reported according to SANRA. Four databases were searched from inception to 31 August 2026. Results: Flavonoid glucosides are hydrolysed to aglycones within minutes of contact with saliva; anthocyanins are deglycosylated to cyanidin and converted to protocatechuic acid; epigallocatechin gallate is de-esterified. Local concentrations reach 2-145 μM, two orders of magnitude above plasma. Conversion capacity varied more than twenty-fold among 17 subjects in the only quantitative study. Conclusions: The oral cavity can alter the chemical form of the polyphenols presented to absorption. The orally transformed fraction of an ingested dose is small; a first-pass effect is not demonstrated, and the established consequences are local and qualitative. Oral metabotypes have not been demonstrated; the concept and its operational classification are proposed as hypotheses to be tested in adequately sized cohorts.

articles.title: Nephron-Sparing Strategies for Tumor-Bearing Horseshoe Kidney: From Surgeries to Pharmaceuticals.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Horseshoe kidney (HSK) is a type of congenital renal fusion anomaly with extreme anatomic complexity. The malrotation of kidneys and ureters and malformation and altered isthmus and vascular supply may boost several renal and extrarenal complications. Organ preservation of tumor-bearing HSK is rather difficult and only available in a small minority of patients. Methods/Results: This review introduces new advances for nephron-sparing surgical strategies for tumor-bearing HSK, such as super-selective artery clamping, ultrasound-guided renal artery balloon catheter occluded hybrid partial nephrectomy, and focal therapies. It also puts forward novel pharmaceuticals for kidney function preservation to alleviate ischemia-reperfusion injury and medications for neoadjuvant therapies. Conclusions: HSK possesses unique etiology, complex anatomic characteristics, and hidden complications. Renal function preservation is extremely important for tumor-bearing HSK. For long-term high-quality lifespan, precise preoperative planning, surgeon's versatility with multiple surgical techniques, and novel pharmaceuticals to avoid IRI are promising strategies for nephron-sparing surgery.

articles.title: Targeting Neuroinflammation After Traumatic Brain Injury: Addressing Sex Differences to Improve Clinical Translation.
articles.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of death and disability worldwide. Following the initial mechanical insult, a complex secondary injury cascade is triggered, resulting in neuroinflammation that can exacerbate neuronal damage and contribute to long-term neurological and psychiatric complications. Despite the development of numerous promising therapies targeting neuroinflammation after TBI, none have successfully translated from preclinical research into clinical practice. This persistent translational gap reflects limitations in preclinical and clinical study design, including inadequate representation of the biological heterogeneity of clinical TBI populations. This review critically evaluates the current landscape of therapies modulating neuroinflammatory pathways following TBI, with particular focus on how biological sex can influence therapeutic efficacy. Across multiple preclinical studies, sex-dependent differences were identified in molecular, histological, and functional responses to therapies targeting central regulators of neuroinflammation, indicating that biological sex can influence therapeutic efficacy across multiple inflammatory pathways. The influence of biological sex may also extend beyond preclinical development into clinical trials, where the underrepresentation of females and the failure to incorporate preclinical evidence of sex-dependent pharmacokinetics and therapeutic responses may represent potential contributors to variable or unsuccessful outcomes. Collectively, the evidence reviewed here suggests that biological sex may represent an important, yet underappreciated, contributor to the challenges of therapeutic translation and may obscure clinically meaningful treatment effects in defined patient subgroups. The findings presented throughout this review therefore suggest that biological sex should be considered a core component of therapeutic development, rather than solely as a secondary exploratory variable, to better characterise sex-dependent treatment responses and aid the clinical translation of therapies targeting neuroinflammation after TBI.

articles.title: ENaC and Tight Junction Proteins: Coordinated Regulation of Alveolar Fluid Homeostasis in ALI/ARDS.
articles.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) and its more severe form, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), remain critical clinical challenges characterized by acute diffuse lung inflammation, alveolar-capillary barrier disruption, and refractory pulmonary edema, leading to high morbidity and mortality. The alveolar epithelium, a key structural and functional unit of the lung, plays a pivotal role in maintaining alveolar fluid homeostasis, which depends on coordinated transcellular ion transport and paracellular barrier integrity mediated primarily by the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) and tight junction proteins. As a central regulator of alveolar fluid clearance, ENaC mediates sodium ion reabsorption across the alveolar epithelium, whereas tight junction proteins, including zonula occludens-1, occludin, and claudins, restrict paracellular leakage and maintain epithelial barrier integrity. In the pathological setting of ALI/ARDS, both ENaC and tight junction proteins undergo significant dysregulation, with reduced ENaC function leading to impaired alveolar fluid clearance and exacerbated edema, while alterations in the expression, distribution, and function of tight junction proteins further compromise barrier integrity. Despite their individual roles being increasingly recognized, the complex interplay between ENaC and tight junctions in the alveolar fluid homeostasis of ALI/ARDS, as well as the underlying regulatory mechanisms, remain incompletely understood. This review therefore focuses on the mechanistic and functional crosstalk between ENaC and tight junction proteins, integrating their coordinated roles in alveolar fluid transport, barrier dysfunction, and pulmonary edema, and discussing potential therapeutic strategies with this coupled regulatory system in ALI/ARDS.

articles.title: Dosimetry Data Infrastructure for Individualized Radiopharmaceutical Therapy: International Experience and a Proposed Framework for China.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: There is increasing interest in moving selected radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) applications toward treatment informed by patient-specific quantitative data. Patient-specific dosimetry supports this transition, but routine implementation remains limited by methodological heterogeneity and incomplete linkage of absorbed dose with response, toxicity, and subsequent treatment decisions. This review examines evidence relevant to longitudinal dosimetry infrastructure and proposes a framework for China. Methods: This narrative review mapped evidence from established therapies, including 177Lu-DOTATATE, 177Lu-PSMA-617, 131I-NaI, and 131I-meta-iodobenzylguanidine (131I-MIBG), with 90Y microsphere selective internal radiation therapy used as a methodologically distinct comparator. International registries, quantitative imaging standards, and dosimetry resources were reviewed in parallel. Results: Available studies show substantial interpatient variation in absorbed dose and growing evidence of dose-response relationships. However, prescription, dosimetry methods, outcome definitions, and follow-up remain heterogeneous. Existing platforms address separate components of RPT care, but few link administration, pretherapy imaging, post-therapy quantitative imaging, dosimetry, clinical outcomes, toxicity, and later decisions across a complete treatment course. We propose seven core data domains and a three-tier architecture comprising hospital-based treatment decision platforms, regional dosimetry centers, and a national data center. Conclusions: A standardized longitudinal dosimetry infrastructure could improve multicenter comparability and provide a testable data foundation for individualized treatment, radiopharmaceutical development, and real-world evaluation. The proposed architecture is conceptual and requires staged consensus, pilot implementation, and prospective validation.

articles.title: Beehive-Derived Products for Wound Management with a Focus on Diabetic Wounds: Mechanistic Insights, Advanced Delivery Strategies, and Translational Evidence.
articles.abstract: Wound healing is a complex biological process that can be severely impaired by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, microbial infection, impaired angiogenesis, and defective extracellular matrix remodelling. These abnormalities are particularly prominent in diabetic wounds but also contribute to delayed healing in burn, venous, pressure, traumatic, and post-surgical wounds. Beehive-derived products, including honey, propolis, royal jelly, beeswax, and bee venom, have attracted considerable interest as multifunctional natural therapeutics because of their diverse antimicrobial, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, and regenerative activities. Honey supports wound repair through its acidic pH, high osmolarity, hydrogen peroxide generation, and bioactive phytochemicals, whereas propolis provides flavonoids and phenolic compounds that contribute to antimicrobial, antioxidant, and tissue-regenerative effects. Royal jelly promotes cellular proliferation, angiogenesis, and tissue repair, while beeswax primarily provides moisture retention, barrier protection, and structural properties in wound dressings. Bee venom and its major component, melittin, exhibit antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and regenerative effects, although dose-dependent toxicity and hypersensitivity remain important concerns. Recent advances in hydrogels, polymeric films, electrospun nanofibres, nanoparticles, and composite scaffolds have improved the stability, local retention, controlled release, and therapeutic performance of these products. Preclinical studies demonstrate enhanced antimicrobial activity, fibroblast migration, collagen deposition, angiogenesis, and wound closure, while emerging clinical evidence supports their potential across several wound types. However, variability in composition, standardisation, safety, formulation stability, and limited large-scale clinical evidence remain major challenges.

articles.title: The MASLD-Heart Axis: Biological Mechanisms, Cardiac Remodeling, and Clinical Implications.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), the hepatic manifestation of cardiometabolic dysfunction, is closely linked to atherosclerosis, heart failure, and adverse cardiovascular outcomes. This review summarizes current evidence on the biological basis of the MASLD-heart axis, with particular emphasis on vascular injury and adverse cardiac remodeling. Methods: A narrative review of contemporary literature was conducted, including experimental studies, observational cohorts, meta-analyses, randomized clinical trials, and current guideline recommendations addressing the cardiohepatic axis. Results: The interaction between the liver and the heart involves interconnected mechanisms, including insulin resistance, lipotoxicity, oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and neurohormonal activation. Experimental and translational evidence supports biologically plausible links between MASLD-related metabolic and inflammatory pathways and vascular or myocardial injury, while clinical studies consistently associate MASLD with arterial stiffness, microvascular dysfunction, atherosclerotic disease, adverse cardiac remodeling, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and cardiovascular events. Several of these associations persist after adjustment for conventional cardiometabolic risk factors, although residual confounding and shared risk determinants limit causal inference. Non-invasive tools, including the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) score and transient elastography, may help identify patients at higher risk of advanced fibrosis and cardiometabolic complications. Lifestyle interventions remain the cornerstone of management, while glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, and fibroblast growth factor-21 analogs may provide combined hepatic and cardiovascular benefits. Conclusions: The cardiohepatic axis is an important component of cardiometabolic disease, linking hepatic dysfunction with vascular and myocardial injury through shared biological pathways. Incorporating hepatic assessment into cardiovascular risk evaluation may support earlier identification of high-risk patients.

articles.title: Targeting PAK1 Within Group I PAKs: Current Challenges and Pharmacological Perspectives.
articles.abstract: The p21-activated kinase 1 (PAK1) has been investigated as a therapeutic target for more than two decades, particularly in cancer, where it contributes to cytoskeletal regulation, proliferation, survival, migration and therapy resistance. Despite the development of numerous potent inhibitors, selective pharmacological modulation of PAK1 remains difficult because of the high similarity of the group I PAK catalytic domains, especially PAK1 and PAK2, together with differences in conformational state, cellular localization and kinase-independent functions. This review examines PAK1 within the broader PAK kinase family and critically evaluates the principal pharmacological strategies developed to modulate its activity, including ATP-competitive and allosteric inhibition, targeted degradation, polypharmacology, combination therapies and indirect approaches. Recent structural studies indicate that local conformational differences between PAK1 and PAK2 can be exploited for improved isoform discrimination, while PAK1-selective degraders provide an alternative means of affecting both catalytic and non-catalytic functions. A snapshot analysis of current ChEMBL bioactivity data further shows that, although numerous compounds display high reported potency against PAK1, matched quantitative information for PAK2 and PAK3 is available for only a limited subset, leaving isoform selectivity unresolved for most compounds. Recent findings also position PAK1 within adaptive and treatment-resistance signaling rather than as a universal oncogenic dependency. Future progress will therefore depend not only on improving compound potency, but on integrating isoform profiling, cellular target engagement, structural information and disease-specific biomarkers to identify the settings in which PAK1 modulation can provide a meaningful therapeutic advantage.

articles.title: Neurotensin-Based Radioligands for NTS1R-Targeted Cancer Theranostics: Background, Current Status and Future Trends.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The neurotensin subtype-1 receptor (NTS1R) is overexpressed in a number of human tumors, representing a valid biomolecular target for neurotensin-based radionuclide carriers. The latter are designed to deposit diagnostic-therapeutic radionuclides specifically on cancer lesions. This review summarizes research efforts toward the development, preclinical evaluation and first clinical outcomes of neurotensin-based radioligands in the diagnosis and therapy-radiotheranostics-of NTS1R-positive cancer. Methods: The preclinical and few clinical studies related to NTS1R-targeted radiotheranostics are discussed. The crucial issue of in vivo metabolic stability is highlighted. Results: Much effort has been dedicated to the development of effective NTS1R-directed radioligands for cancer theranostics, most of which are peptide-based. However, clinical success has been sub-optimal thus far, partly as a result of their fast degradation in the biological milieu. Conclusions: The administration of key protease inhibitor regimens, the introduction of branched or otherwise stabilized analogs and the advent of non-peptidic NTS1R-antagonists are some of the new promising approaches towards achieving clinical breakthroughs in the battle against NTS1R-expressing cancer.

articles.title: Delivering Phytochemicals to the Implantation Window: The Dual Constraint of Achieving Endometrial Exposure Without Compromising the Embryo.
articles.abstract: Whether a phytochemical promotes or suppresses endometrial receptivity is context-dependent, and the dose axis of that context cannot be placed on a concentration scale without knowing how much compound reaches the endometrium-a measurement this review's documented search did not retrieve for the human endometrium. This review asks why oral administration does not produce interpretable endometrial exposure, which routes can, and what safety constraint follows from targeting an endometrium that contains an embryo. Poor oral bioavailability is not a single obstacle: absorption failure, loss of the parent compound, intestinal conjugation, systemic metabolism and host-dependent speciation overlap, and what differs by class is which step dominates. Endometrial targeting is not unprecedented-vaginal progesterone attains endometrial concentrations disproportionate to serum through the first uterine pass, quantified in human tissue-but that precedent is specific to a small lipophilic steroid and to the released drug rather than the carrier. Uniquely, this target is dual-constrained: a carrier must reach the tissue without exposing an embryo that lipid nanoparticles reach by crossing the zona pellucida. Peri-implantation delivery therefore requires context-dependent design choices: release aligned to a defined window, bounded exposure, and separate verification of carrier distribution, released-drug exposure, endometrial effect and developmental outcome.

articles.title: Capivasertib Combination Therapy in Advanced Breast Cancer and Other Solid Tumors: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Efficacy, Safety, and Biomarker-Defined Outcomes.
articles.abstract: Background: Capivasertib is an oral pan-AKT inhibitor evaluated in combination with multiple systemic therapies across solid tumors, but its efficacy and safety vary by disease setting, biomarker status, and treatment backbone. We aimed to systematically evaluate the efficacy, safety, and early-phase clinical activity of capivasertib-containing combination regimens in advanced breast cancer and other solid tumors. Methods: MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, trial registries, and major oncology conference sources were searched from inception to 31 May 2026. Randomized comparative studies, single-arm phase II studies, and phase I/Ib combination cohorts were included. Random-effects meta-analyses used restricted maximum likelihood estimation, with randomized and noncomparative evidence synthesized separately. Results: Twenty-seven reports representing 23 independent cohorts were included. In hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, capivasertib plus fulvestrant improved progression-free survival in the overall population (HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.51-0.69) and in PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered disease (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.38-0.62), and increased objective response (RR 2.23, 95% CI 1.31-3.80). In triple-negative breast cancer, progression-free survival improved (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.62-0.84), whereas overall survival remained inconclusive (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.55-1.17). In PTEN-deficient metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, radiographic progression-free survival improved (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.66-0.98). Capivasertib increased grade ≥ 3 adverse events (RR 1.66, 95% CI 1.06-2.60) and treatment discontinuation (RR 2.97, 95% CI 1.27-6.96). Conclusions: Capivasertib demonstrated disease-, biomarker-, and treatment backbone-specific activity, with the most consistent comparative benefit observed in hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer. Increased toxicity should be considered when selecting patients and treatment combinations.

articles.title: Impact of Aggregation on the Immunogenicity of Therapeutic Recombinant Biological Products.
articles.abstract: Background: Therapeutic recombinant biological products are essential in modern medicine, but their immunogenicity remains a major concern for both clinical safety and therapeutic efficacy. Protein aggregation may occur during manufacturing, storage, transportation, and administration, potentially increasing immune recognition. Here, we have reviewed the mechanisms underlying aggregation-associated immunogenicity and summarized strategies for mitigating the associated risks. Methods: We integrated published evidence on therapeutic recombinant proteins, monoclonal antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, peptide and glycoprotein hormones, and recombinant blood products. We focused on aggregation-induced structural changes, immune activation pathways, differences among product types and aggregation states, and approaches for controlling aggregation and mitigating immunogenicity. Results: Protein aggregation creates or reveals neoepitopes by disrupting the native conformational state, exposing previously buried hydrophobic regions, and generating nonnative interfaces. Aggregates may further promote innate and adaptive immune responses through repetitive epitope presentation, pattern-recognition receptor signaling, complement activation, cytokine release, dendritic-cell maturation, enhanced antigen presentation, and B-cell receptor cross-linking, ultimately increasing the likelihood of anti-drug antibody formation. Aggregate size and morphology, protein characteristics, formulation, storage conditions, administration route, and other biological factors influence the immunogenic potential of aggregates. Thus, effective risk reduction requires integrated control strategies, including molecular and structural optimization, formulation design, manufacturing-process control, appropriate storage and transportation, and sensitive analytical monitoring. Emerging artificial-intelligence approaches may further facilitate the prediction and design of low-immunogenicity biologics. Conclusions: Protein aggregation is a multifactorial determinant of immunogenicity. Controlling aggregation throughout the product lifecycle is essential to reduce immune-mediated risks and maintain safety, stability, and efficacy of therapeutic recombinant biological products.

articles.title: Microglial Therapeutic Potential in Alzheimer's Disease: From Phenotypic Diversity to Targeted Interventions.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by β-amyloid (Aβ) deposition, tau pathology and cognitive decline. Increasing evidence from genetic, transcriptomic, experimental and clinical studies has identified microglia as key regulators of AD pathogenesis. Under physiological conditions, microglia maintain central nervous system homeostasis through immune surveillance, phagocytosis and neurotrophic support. However, persistent exposure to pathological stimuli promotes a shift toward dysfunctional inflammatory states that contribute to neuroinflammation, synaptic impairment, tau propagation and neurodegeneration. Recent advances have revealed substantial microglial heterogeneity, highlighting the existence of dynamic and disease stage-dependent activation states rather than fixed phenotypes. In early disease stages, microglia can promote Aβ clearance and tissue repair, whereas chronic activation may exacerbate pathological processes. These findings have driven the development of microglia-targeted therapeutic strategies aimed at enhancing protective functions while limiting maladaptive inflammatory responses. This review summarizes current knowledge regarding microglial involvement in AD and discusses emerging therapeutic approaches, ranging from immunomodulation and metabolic reprogramming to gene-based and nanotechnology-driven interventions, with a focus on their translational potential.

articles.title: Selenium Nanoparticles Functionalized with Tumor-Targeting Peptides for Lung Cancer Therapy: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract: Lung cancer is among the most fatal malignancies worldwide, with approximately 85% of diagnosed cases being non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Despite the considerable progress in surgical, chemotherapeutic, radiotherapeutic, and immunological treatments, the prognosis of NSCLC remains poor due to late-stage diagnosis, molecular heterogeneity, treatment resistance, recurrence, and systemic toxicity. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop more effective and less toxic therapies, and cancer nanotechnology has emerged as a promising approach. Selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) are a viable option for lung cancer treatment because of their unique physicochemical and biochemical properties. They can be used for targeted drug delivery into cancer cells, as selenium possesses inherent anti-cancer properties, such as the induction of reactive oxygen species (ROS), mitochondrial disruption, DNA damage, cell-cycle arrest, and modulation of several signaling pathways, including PI3K/Akt, MAPK, NF-κβ, STAT3, and p53, leading to cancer cell death and repression of tumor progression. Green synthesis of SeNPs using plant-derived phytochemicals is a sustainable strategy as it allows for simultaneous reduction and stabilization of nanoparticles, with an additional therapeutic phytochemical effect against cancer. Various phytochemicals, such as flavonoids, polyphenols, terpenoids, and alkaloids, have the ability to chelate metal ions and act as reducing agents and stabilizers in the synthesis of SeNPs. The antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, anti-proliferative, and anti-metastatic activities of phytochemicals, along with their ability to inhibit the overexpressed enzymes, e.g., matrix metalloproteinases, in cancer cells, could provide an additional therapeutic benefit. However, the application of SeNPs in practice is limited by their low targeting ability, which results in poor bioavailability due to fast clearance from the bloodstream, reduced tumor accumulation, and poor cellular uptake. Conjugation of SeNPs with tumor-targeting peptides could enhance their delivery into the cancer cells. There is a variety of cell surface receptors that are overexpressed in lung cancer cells and can be used for targeted drug delivery. The most common receptors are EGFR, integrins, gastrin-releasing peptide receptor, neuropilin-1, and transferrin receptor. The ligands for these receptors, including the GE11 peptide for EGFR (epidermal growth factor receptor), RGD for integrins, bombesin for GRPR, and iRGD for neuropilin-1, could be used for targeting, as well as cell-penetrating peptides, such as TAT. This review discusses the current knowledge on the application of functionalized SeNPs for lung cancer treatment, specifically synthetic methods, physicochemical properties, mechanisms of action, and targeting strategies. Particular attention is paid to the combination of the anti-cancer effects of selenium and phytochemicals and their synergistic impact on tumor cell death. In addition, the challenges of the application of SeNPs for lung cancer treatment and possible future developments for functionalized SeNPs as novel therapeutic nanocarriers are discussed.

articles.title: New and Emerging Drug Therapy in Primary Open-Angle and Normal-Tension Glaucoma: Pharmacology, Neuroprotection and the Endpoint Problem.
articles.abstract: Glaucoma is a group of progressive optic neuropathies characterized by retinal ganglion cell (RGC) loss, optic nerve head damage and corresponding visual-field loss. Intraocular pressure (IOP) is the principal modifiable risk factor, and lowering IOP remains the only treatment approach that has been shown in randomized clinical trials to slow glaucomatous progression, including in normal-tension glaucoma (NTG). However, IOP reduction does not eliminate progression in all patients, indicating that susceptibility to pressure-related damage is heterogeneous and that additional biological mechanisms are relevant. This review examines current and emerging pharmacological strategies for IOP lowering, approaches intended to protect RGCs independently of IOP, and the methodological problem of demonstrating neuroprotection in clinical trials.

articles.title: Polysaccharide Reengineering: Strategic Modifications and Biofunctional Outcomes of Natural Polysaccharides.
articles.abstract: Natural polysaccharides have attracted considerable interest in pharmaceutical and biomedical applications. However, native polysaccharides often possess limitations, like poor solubility, inadequate mechanical strength, limited stability, and insufficient control over their functional and biological properties. Consequently, structural modification and function-driven reengineering of natural polysaccharides have emerged as important strategies for tailoring the physicochemical and biological characteristics to meet the requirements of advanced pharmaceutical and biomedical systems. Beyond individual modification strategies, polysaccharide reengineering provides a design-oriented framework in which structural features are deliberately tuned to establish relationships between molecular or network architecture, physicochemical properties, biointerfacial interactions, and biological function. This review examines polysaccharide reengineering as a function-driven approach to tailoring the structure and performance of natural polysaccharides. Rather than simply cataloguing modification methods, the review critically connects principal reengineering strategies, including carboxymethylation, sulfation, phosphorylation, grafting, and interpenetrating polymer network (IPN) formation, with their effects on structural characteristics, physicochemical properties, biointerfacial interactions, biological functions, and pharmaceutical performance. Particular emphasis is placed on identifying structure-property-biofunction relationships and on extracting design principles that can guide the selection and combination of reengineering strategies for specific applications. Reengineering of natural polysaccharides provides a versatile strategy to overcome the inherent limitations of native materials and to develop polysaccharide-based platforms with tailored physicochemical and biological properties. Different modification approaches offer distinct functional advantages: carboxymethylation can improve hydrophilicity and pH-responsive swelling, whereas sulfation and phosphorylation introduce anionic functionalities that modulate charge-dependent interactions and biological responses. Similarly, grafting and interpenetrating polymer network (IPN) formation provide greater control over mechanical strength, swelling, stability, drug-loading capacity, and controlled-release behavior. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the performance of reengineered polysaccharides is determined not by the modification strategy alone, but by the combined effects of the resulting molecular structure, physicochemical characteristics, and interactions with biological environments. Despite these advances, the development of predictable structure-function relationships remains challenging because of variations in polysaccharide source, molecular weight, degree and distribution of modification, and characterization methodologies. Therefore, future research should shift from empirical modification toward rational, function-driven polysaccharide reengineering, in which structural parameters are deliberately controlled to achieve predefined material and biological outcomes.

articles.title: A Narrative Review of Cutaneous Wound-Healing Botanicals in South Africa: Integrating Ethnomedicinal Use, Pharmacological Evidence, and Conservation Prioritization.
articles.abstract: African Traditional Medicine (ATM) remains an important component of primary healthcare in South Africa; however, evidence for plants used in cutaneous wound care is dispersed across ethnobotanical, pharmacological, toxicological, and conservation literature. This narrative review integrates these evidence streams and proposes a conservation- and safety-aware translational prioritization framework for wound-healing botanicals used in South African ethnomedical practice. A structured search of PubMed, ScienceDirect, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and SciFinder identified eligible peer-reviewed ethnobotanical and preclinical studies published between January 1999 and June 2026. After taxonomic harmonization, 173 accepted taxa were documented from South African ethnobotanical reports as being traditionally used for wound care. Only seven taxa had direct wound closure evidence in relevant in vitro or in vivo models, while twenty-eight taxa had wound-relevant anti-inflammatory evidence. Reported mechanisms included keratinocyte and fibroblast migration, collagen-associated responses, angiogenesis, wound contraction, and inflammatory modulation. The evidence base remains uneven: many taxa are supported primarily by traditional use, while dose, formulation, treatment frequency, duration of use, dermal safety, and sustainable sourcing are poorly reported. Safety concerns were identified for selected toxic or irritant taxa, and destructive harvesting of roots, bulbs, corms, rhizomes, and bark may increase conservation risk. Overall, the review highlights a substantial gap between ethnomedical documentation and pharmacological validation, and it provides a prioritization strategy to guide future phytochemical, mechanistic, formulation, dermal-safety, and preclinical wound-healing research in South Africa.

articles.title: Microneedle-Delivered Plant-Derived Exosome-like Nanovesicles for Dermatological Diseases: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract: Plant-derived extracellular vesicle-like nanovesicles (PELNs) are being investigated as plant-derived preparations with intrinsic bioactivity and potential utility as nanocarriers. Microneedles (MNs) can create transient skin microchannels and may support localized intradermal delivery of vesicle-containing formulations. The intersection of these approaches is promising, but the available evidence remains heterogeneous and includes direct PELN-MN studies, PELN studies without MNs, and related mammalian extracellular vesicle platforms. Here we provide a comprehensive review of PELN identity, isolation, characterization, cargo, and proposed dermatological activities, followed by an assessment of MN designs relevant to vesicle delivery. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase, screened records in duplicate, and classified each included study by the directness of evidence into studies providing direct PELN-MN skin evidence, PELN evidence without MNs, mammalian extracellular vesicle MN analogue evidence, and non-dermatological or conceptual evidence. Current limitations include uncertain vesicle identity, co-isolated plant constituents, variable preparation and dosing methods, limited controls for the mechanical effects of microneedling, and incomplete clinical follow-up. Progress toward translation will require source-specific quality attributes, orthogonal potency assays, transparent comparators, and adequately controlled clinical studies.

articles.title: Drugging the Undruggable in Oncology: Structural Computation, Machine Learning, and Generative AI for Historically Intractable Targets.
articles.abstract: For four decades the central oncogenic drivers of human cancer the RAS GTPases, the transcription-factor MYC, mutant p53, and the protein-tyrosine phosphatases, fusion oncoproteins and intrinsically disordered regulators that surround them were regarded as undruggable: lacking deep, well-defined small-molecule binding pockets, governed by femtomolar substrate affinities, or driven through flat protein-protein interfaces that classical medicinal chemistry could not engage. The last decade has overturned that verdict. This narrative review argues that the convergence of three advances has made the undruggable proteome systematically approachable: the discovery of cryptic, allosteric and induced pockets through molecular dynamics and deep learning; the maturation of physics-based and machine-learned models that can read out binding from structure; and the rise in generative artificial intelligence that can design novel molecules conditioned directly on a three-dimensional target. We develop the argument in full formal detail. We set out the mathematics of modern molecular machine learning E(3)/SE(3)-equivariant graph neural networks, denoising diffusion and score-based generative models, and generative flow networks alongside the statistical mechanics of binding free energy (free-energy perturbation, thermodynamic integration, MM-PBSA), the kinetics of covalent inhibition, the equilibrium theory of ternary complexes and cooperativity that governs molecular glues and degraders, and the pharmacology that determines whether a designed molecule reaches and acts on a tumour. We then examine, target by target, the biology that made each oncoprotein intractable and the campaigns structural, chemical and increasingly computational that have begun to defeat it, distinguishing throughout what classical structural and computational work achieved, what machine learning demonstrably contributed, and what generative design has so far only promised: the switch-II pocket and the covalent KRAS-G12C and non-covalent KRAS-G12D and pan-RAS(ON) inhibitors; the mutation-created cavity of p53-Y220C and its first reactivators; the disordered MYC-MAX interface and the miniprotein Omomyc; and the allosteric tunnel of SHP2. These four are selected for mechanistic non-redundancy, on grounds we state explicitly, and the structured search framework and eligibility criteria underlying the review are documented. We foreground the newest evidence AlphaFold3, RoseTTAFold All-Atom, deep cryptic-pocket predictors, and the first generative-to-clinic existence proofs while maintaining candour about the field's hard limits: the physical-validity and generalisation gaps of deep docking, the bounded accuracy and cost of free-energy methods, the synthesizability gap, dual-use risk, and a clinical attrition that artificial intelligence has not yet reduced. The synthesis we offer is not that the problem is solved but that it has changed in kind: from a search for the rare tractable target to the deliberate, computable engineering of molecules against targets once thought beyond reach.

articles.title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Ciprofol Versus Propofol in Adults Undergoing Fiberoptic Bronchoscopy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: Background: Ciprofol, a novel intravenous sedative, has recently gained increasing clinical attention for procedural anesthesia. Emerging evidence suggests it may possess potential safety advantages over propofol. This study aimed to systematically compare the efficacy and safety of ciprofol and propofol for sedation in patients undergoing fiberoptic bronchoscopy. Methods: A comprehensive literature search was conducted in eight electronic databases. Statistical analyses were performed using the R software (version 4.5.2). The risk ratio (RR) with 95% confidence interval (CI) was used for dichotomous outcomes, and the mean difference (MD) with 95% CI was used for continuous outcomes. Results: This meta-analysis included 22 RCTs with 2452 participants. Compared with propofol, ciprofol significantly reduced the incidence of hypotension (RR, 0.39; 95% CI, 0.28-0.55), injection pain (RR, 0.14; 95% CI, 0.10-0.19), hypoxemia (RR, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.35-0.90), and respiratory depression (RR, 0.23; 95% CI, 0.12-0.43). No significant differences were found in cough (RR, 1.01; 95% CI, 0.89-1.14), bradycardia (RR, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.42-1.14), nausea and vomiting (RR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.56-1.27), induction time (MD, 0.03; 95% CI, -10.57-10.62), operation time (MD, -0.3060; 95% CI, -0.6127-0.0008), recovery time (MD, 0.10; 95% CI, -0.59-0.79), or procedural success rate (RR, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.99-1.01). Conclusions: Ciprofol provides comparable sedative efficacy to propofol for fiberoptic bronchoscopy, while reducing the incidence of adverse events, suggesting it may be a favorable alternative.

articles.title: Combination Therapy Potential of HTD1801 (Berberine Ursodeoxycholate) in MASLD/MASH and Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Disease: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) continuum is characterized by the close interrelatedness of metabolic, hepatic, cardiovascular, and renal disease, making multidomain therapies particularly relevant to MASLD/MASH. HTD1801, an investigational ionic therapeutic, combines berberine's metabolic effects with the hepatoprotective effects of ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA), making it a potential multidomain therapy within this setting. This review had two related goals: first, to synthesize the mechanistic and clinical evidence for HTD1801 itself; and second, to evaluate the rationale and available evidence for extending this complementary-action approach through combination with other therapies relevant to MASLD/MASH and CKM disease. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, ClinicalTrials.gov, conference abstracts, and selected regulatory or sponsor sources were reviewed through 9 August 2026. Six CKM-relevant therapeutic classes were selected for their human evidence of multidomain benefit: metformin, GLP-1 receptor agonists, statins, SGLT2 inhibitors, PPAR agonists, and resmetirom. Studies of both HTD1801 and its individual components, berberine and UDCA, were included. A systematic review or meta-analysis was not feasible due to the limited and heterogeneous evidence base, instead necessitatinganarrative review. Results: Across seven completed HTD1801 clinical studies with publicly reported results, treatment showed multidomain metabolic and hepatic benefits across the CKM spectrum, including improvements in HbA1c, LDL-C, MRI-PDFF hepatic fat, ALT, AST, and GGT. Direct human evidence: HTD1801 + metformin, supported by a Phase 3 randomized add-on trial. Indirect human evidence: HTD1801 + SGLT2 inhibitors. Preclinical evidence: HTD1801 + GLP-1 receptor agonists; berberine + statins. Theoretical mechanistic rationale only: HTD1801 + PPAR agonists; HTD1801 + resmetirom. Overall, mechanistic and preclinical rationale has advanced further than direct human validation, and evidence remains centered largely on surrogate rather than definitive clinical outcomes. Conclusions: HTD1801 has demonstrated multidomain metabolic and hepatic activity, but direct human evidence supporting its use with other CKM therapies remains limited and is currently established only for metformin. The principal next step is to test HTD1801 in dedicated combination RCTs for clinically meaningful benefit. Further studies should characterize combination-specific safety and tolerability and compare HTD1801 with separate berberine and UDCA administration.

articles.title: Beyond Genotype: Integrating Phenoconversion into Pharmacogenetic Decision-Making in Psychiatry.
articles.abstract: Interindividual variability in psychotropic drug response contributes to treatment failure, adverse drug reactions, and repeated medication adjustments. Pharmacogenetics supports precision prescribing by identifying genetic variants associated with drug metabolism, efficacy, and tolerability, and evidence-based recommendations are available for several psychotropic medications. However, genotype predicts metabolic capacity rather than the enzyme activity actually expressed in vivo or the systemic drug exposure achieved at a given time. This narrative review examines phenoconversion, the mismatch between genotype-predicted and observed metabolic phenotype, and its implications for psychiatric pharmacotherapy. Drug-drug interactions, smoking, inflammation, physiological changes, and disease-related factors can modify drug-metabolizing enzyme activity or otherwise alter systemic drug exposure despite an unchanged genotype. We discuss how these influences can limit the applicability of genotype-based dosing recommendations and propose a dynamic framework integrating pharmacogenetic results with concomitant medications, clinical conditions, lifestyle factors, therapeutic drug monitoring, and longitudinal changes in patient status. This framework may also refine the assessment of treatment adequacy, because prescribed dose, duration, and adherence do not necessarily ensure adequate drug exposure. Future clinical decision-support systems should combine pharmacogenetic and longitudinal clinical data to enable more individualized and dynamically informed psychopharmacological treatment.

articles.title: Machine Learning for Screening Bioactive Compounds in Traditional Chinese Medicine: Computational Prediction, Multi-Omics Integration, and Clinical Translation Potential.
articles.abstract: Identifying bioactive compounds in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) requires computational prioritization to be connected with chemical and pharmacological evidence. This structured narrative and critical review examines machine learning applications in compound prediction, formula-compatibility analysis, multi-omics integration, and drug development and repurposing. Molecular fingerprints, graph and sequence representations, knowledge graphs, and generative models are discussed in relation to their intended endpoints and validation conditions. Studies are classified along two independent dimensions: application scope, distinguishing direct TCM applications from natural-product studies and general drug-discovery methods, and validation level, ranging from computational prediction to chemical, experimental, and clinical evidence. Three case analyses illustrate a TCM-specific graph-learning platform with chemical confirmation, a downstream animal and metabolomics study without machine learning screening, and a proposed causal framework assembled from separate studies. Across these applications, machine learning supports candidate ranking and hypothesis generation, but predicted targets, attention weights, and multi-omics associations do not independently establish target engagement, formula synergy, or therapeutic efficacy. Major limitations include chemical-domain shift, inconsistent database provenance, data leakage, sparse negative results, and incomplete experimental follow-up. Reliable advancement requires scaffold-aware or external evaluation, explicit applicability domains and uncertainty, traceable data processing, and constituent-resolved intervention studies. A minimum reporting checklist consolidates these requirements, while route-specific assessment distinguishes synthetic accessibility from biosynthetic feasibility. Together, these considerations provide a basis for evaluating screening claims and designing reproducible workflows toward experimentally supported TCM compound discovery.

articles.title: Adjunctive Corticosteroids in Pediatric Meningitis: Current Evidence, Clinical Controversies, and Future Directions.
articles.abstract: Background: Pediatric bacterial meningitis remains an important cause of death and long-term neurological disability despite advances in vaccination, antimicrobial therapy, and supportive care. Because host inflammation contributes substantially to secondary neuronal injury, adjunctive corticosteroids have been investigated as a strategy to reduce inflammation-mediated complications. This narrative review aims to critically evaluate the current evidence on corticosteroid therapy in pediatric meningitis, with particular emphasis on acute bacterial meningitis, major clinical and neurological outcomes, treatment timing, pathogen-specific effects, and the impact of changing post-vaccination epidemiology. Methods: A structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted for relevant publications available up to June 2026. Randomized controlled trials, observational studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and international guidelines involving patients aged 0-18 years were considered. Evidence was synthesized narratively, focusing on mortality, hearing loss, neurological sequelae, long-term outcomes, safety, causative pathogen, and timing of corticosteroid administration. Results: Adjunctive dexamethasone has not demonstrated a consistent mortality benefit, while evidence concerning hospital stay, intensive care utilization, and healthcare costs remains limited. Its most reproducible benefit is a reduction in sensorineural hearing loss, particularly in Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) meningitis. Benefits in pneumococcal meningitis are less consistent, and evidence supporting routine use in meningococcal disease remains limited. Efficacy appears greatest when dexamethasone is administered before or with the first antibiotic dose and may be less pronounced in the post-vaccination era. In tuberculous meningitis, corticosteroids improve survival, whereas routine use is not supported in uncomplicated viral meningitis or cryptococcal meningitis. Conclusions: Adjunctive dexamethasone should be used selectively in pediatric meningitis, with its clearest benefit being hearing preservation in early-treated Hib meningitis. Treatment decisions should account for pathogen, timing, and epidemiological context.

articles.title: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Advances of Natural Products Regulating Non-Coding RNAs in Cancer.
articles.abstract: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs, long non-coding RNAs, circular RNAs, tRNA-derived fragments, PIWI-interacting RNAs, and small nucleolar RNAs, have been identified as crucial regulators of gene expression and key drivers of cancer progression. Natural products, owing to their structural diversity and multi-targeting capacity, represent a promising reservoir for anticancer drug discovery through the modulation of these ncRNA networks. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the regulatory roles of natural products on ncRNAs in cancer. Compared with previous reviews that focus on individual ncRNA classes or single natural product categories, this review provides an integrated framework linking ncRNA biology, natural product pharmacology, and therapeutic delivery in cancer. First, the biogenesis, classification, and molecular functions of major ncRNA classes are systematically described, and the dysregulation of each ncRNA class across various cancer types and their contributions to tumor pathogenesis are then discussed. Subsequently, the modulation of these ncRNA networks by representative natural products, including polyphenols, flavonoids, terpenoids, and alkaloids, to influence multiple hallmarks of tumor progression, encompassing cell proliferation, programmed cell death, metastatic dissemination, tumor microenvironment remodeling, and therapeutic resistance, is reviewed. The potential of ncRNAs as diagnostic, prognostic, and pharmacodynamic biomarkers in the context of natural product-based therapy is discussed, together with emerging nanoparticle-based delivery strategies for co-delivering natural products and ncRNA therapeutics; however, most of the evidence summarized here remains preclinical, and clinical translation will require rigorous pharmacological and clinical validation. Finally, we address current challenges and future perspectives for the clinical translation of natural product-ncRNA-based anticancer strategies.

articles.title: Lysine Acetylation as a Regulatory Mechanism in Cardiometabolic Disease: A Focus on Sirtuins.
articles.abstract: Protein lysine acetylation is a widespread post-translational modification that regulates metabolic enzyme activity and cellular function. Sirtuins (SIRTs) are a family of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+)-dependent deacetylases that act as key metabolic sensors coupling cellular energy status to the regulation of protein acetylation.
