articles.title: Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis Interactions with CNS Drugs: A Critical Mechanistic Review of Biopharmaceutical, Pharmacokinetic, and Pharmacodynamic Evidence.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA) modifies central nervous system (CNS) pharmacotherapy by influencing the biopharmaceutics, pharmacokinetics (PK), and pharmacodynamics (PD) of drugs, while CNS drugs reciprocally reshape the MGBA. This review examines these interactions and their clinical relevance, explicitly grading the strength of the evidence. Methods: This narrative, mechanistically oriented review focuses on four oral drugs representing distinct mechanistic archetypes: levodopa/carbidopa (biopharmaceutical-dominant), olanzapine (PK-dominant), sertraline (PD-dominant), and amitriptyline (mixed). PubMed/MEDLINE, Google Scholar, and Google were searched up to 1 September 2026; of approximately 260 records screened, 64 were cited. No PRISMA reporting or dual screening was performed. Findings were assigned to five evidence tiers (L1-L5) and classified as associative or causal. Results: For levodopa/carbidopa, fecal tyrosine decarboxylase (tdc) gene abundance correlates with daily dose requirement (human observational), and Helicobacter pylori eradication or treatment of small intestinal bacterial overgrowth improves levodopa exposure or motor outcomes (human interventional). For olanzapine, microbiota depletion increased bioavailability ~1.8-fold in rats (single study), and microbiome-dependent weight gain is causal in rodents, whereas human data are phenomenological only. For sertraline, antimicrobial activity and fecal depletion are demonstrated in vitro; the pharmacodynamic blockade derives from fluoxetine models. For amitriptyline, antimicrobial and anticholinergic effects are preclinical, and the ATLANTIS trial demonstrates efficacy in irritable bowel syndrome without measuring the microbiome. Conclusions: The microbiome is a measurable modifier of CNS drug fate, but few interactions are clinically actionable. Progress requires prospective trials with standardized MGBA biomarkers, microbiome-informed PK/PD models, and independent replication.

articles.title: Beyond the Needle: Transforming Traditional Healthcare with Microneedle Drug Delivery Systems.
articles.abstract: In the present era, modern drug delivery systems play a fundamental role in ensuring the systematic delivery of the drug into the body, reaching the desired targets. Across recent decades, the drug delivery system has evolved from simple oral and injectable formulations to interpolating with various developed techniques to fabricate innovative treatment approaches for safer, effective, and better patient compliance. Progressive techniques like nanoparticles, microparticles, liposomes, polymer-based systems, 3D printing, and biological carriers have been extensively combined with specifically targeted drug-delivery techniques across infectious, oncological, pulmonary, and neurological conditions. Microneedle transdermal patches have advanced in tandem. They have gained attention for their advancement to surpass the stratum corneum, minimal invasiveness, independent delivery, and patient compliance. This review provides a translational perspective by integrating MN materials and device engineering with drug-delivery performance, patient usability, clinical evidence, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory considerations to examine the progression of MN technologies from laboratory development toward real-world healthcare implementation. Microneedles are fabricated in different types, such as solid, coated, hollow, dissolving, and hydrogel-based, to enhance precision in dosing, better permeability, and suitability across diverse populations, and complex molecules are designed, such as proteins, peptides, hormones, vaccines, and cosmetic agents. Moreover, studies suggest MN are widely accepted by geriatric and pediatric groups, reduce anxiety, and significantly benefit individuals with trypanophobia, swallowing difficulties in the case of oral doses, and compromised venous action, in addition to breaking social inequity. MN-induced microchannels can transiently increase skin permeability and may facilitate sustained or controlled drug delivery depending on MN geometry, formulation, application conditions, skin site, and individual skin characteristics. The persistence of these microchannels and their safety profile are dependent on both device and formulation characteristics. MN is a pivotal part of the novel drug delivery system, addresses the complications arising due to conventional drug delivery, and proves to focus on the improvement of pharmacokinetic parameters, patient-centric therapy, target delivery, and real-world accessibility. Further transformation in the enhancement of MN technology can lead to clinically promising drug delivery systems for the management of long-term treatment and boost next-generation therapies.

articles.title: Nanoparticle-Based Drug Delivery Systems for Anticancer Therapy: Microenvironment-Driven Strategies, Advances, and Challenges.
articles.abstract: Cancer remains a major global health challenge, and nanoparticle-based drug delivery systems have emerged as a promising strategy for targeted cancer therapy. However, clinical translation is still limited by an incomplete understanding of how nanoparticles navigate the tumor microenvironment (TME) throughout the delivery process. This review presents an integrated, stage-by-stage framework for nanoparticle design that addresses the TME barriers encountered during systemic circulation, tumor-targeted enrichment, and drug release. During systemic circulation, PEGylation, hydrophilic polymer modification, cell membrane- or exosome-based biomimetic technologies, and biomolecular corona formation are employed to prolong circulation half-life. In the tumor-targeting stage, charge-reversal surfaces, ligand conjugation, ligand shielding, and tuning of physical properties enhance tumor accumulation and cellular internalization. For drug release, molecular and structural design enables intracellular responsive release, stepwise extracellular-to-intracellular release, and sequential release to distinct target cells. Beyond summarizing these strategies, we highlight the newly proposed active transport and retention (ATR) principle as a unifying mechanistic framework that explains how nanoparticles achieve tumor accumulation through active endothelial transport and retention via tumor component interactions. We further discuss translational barriers including complex fabrication, scalability hurdles, and biocompatibility constraints, and outline emerging solutions such as novel nanoparticle fabrication methods (microfluidics, turbulent jet, and microfluidic mixing), engineered biomimetic exosomes, organ-on-a-chip evaluation platforms, and AI-driven design screening. By connecting stage-specific design strategies to the ATR framework, this review offers a mechanistic foundation for the rational design of next-generation nanomedicines.

articles.title: A Systematic Review of Complement-Targeting Therapies for Geographic Atrophy: Insights into Advanced Drug Delivery Systems and Gene-Based Approaches.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Geographic atrophy (GA), an advanced form of dry age-related macular degeneration (AMD), causes irreversible central vision loss and has limited treatment options. Complement dysregulation plays a pivotal role in GA pathogenesis. This systematic review synthesizes the efficacy, safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of approved and investigational complement-targeting therapies, alongside emerging drug delivery systems and gene-based approaches. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane were searched and studies screened against predefined eligibility criteria. Risk of bias and pharmacokinetic quality were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and ClinPK Statement checklist, respectively. Results: Thirty-one studies evaluating C3, C5, factor D, and factor B inhibitors; recombinant factor H; soluble CD59 gene therapy; and an indirect anti-amyloid-β strategy were analyzed. Only two agents are FDA-approved: pegcetacoplan (C3 inhibitor) and avacincaptad pegol (C5 inhibitor). They both significantly, albeit modestly, slowed GA lesion growth. However, both increased the risk of exudative AMD conversion and required frequent intravitreal injections. Other complement targets showed limited efficacy or failed to meet clinical endpoints. Pharmacokinetic data, largely derived from serum measurements and model-based predictions, suggest that intravitreal half-life and injection volume dose limitations may complicate the translational development of complement inhibitors. Conclusions: Current evidence indicates a modest, agent-, dose-, and regimen-dependent slowing of GA anatomical progression. Clinically meaningful visual function benefit has not been firmly established, although post hoc analyses suggest possible benefits for photoreceptor structure and vision-related risk. Gene therapy and advanced intraocular delivery systems have emerged as potential strategies, but further research must determine whether they can provide sustained, multitarget, patient-centered treatment with acceptable ocular and systemic safety.

articles.title: Synergistic induction of apoptosis in human prostate cancer PC3 cells by silver-coated cerium oxide nanoparticles: unveiling the role of ROS-mediated p53-associated apoptotic signaling and antioxidant system depletion.
articles.abstract: Castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) represents a formidable clinical challenge due to intrinsic defects in apoptotic execution, elevated baseline antioxidant capacity, and rapid resistance to standard chemotherapy. Herein, we report the rational design, template-directed synthesis, and antineoplastic evaluation of silver-coated cerium oxide core-shell nanoparticles (Ag@CeO2 NPs) derived from a cerium-based metal-organic framework (Ce-UiO-66) for targeted intervention in androgen-independent prostate carcinoma. Uniform Ce-UiO-66 MOF nanoparticles were thermally converted via controlled calcination (550 °C, 3 h) into porous cubic fluorite nanoceria (CeO₂) cores, followed by in situ surface nucleation and reduction of a metallic silver (Ag⁰) nanoshell stabilized by polyvinylpyrrolidone. The physicochemical properties were characterized by FTIR, PXRD, FESEM, EDX mapping, DLS, and Zeta potential analysis. In vitro anticancer efficacy was evaluated in human androgen-independent PC-3 prostate cancer cells and normal human fibroblasts (HFF-1). Cellular viability, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, superoxide dismutase (SOD) and catalase (CAT) enzymatic kinetics, apoptosis-related transcriptomics (p53, Bax, Bcl-2 via qRT-PCR), and p53 protein levels (ELISA) were systematically quantified. PXRD and Scherrer analysis confirmed the formation of pure, face-centered cubic fluorite CeO₂ (Cerianite-(Ce), Fm3̄m, *a* = 5.4110 Å) with an average primary crystallite size of 7.27 ± 0.36 nm (7.44 nm for the (111) reflection), alongside characteristic reflections of metallic Ag. FESEM, DLS, and electrophoretic measurements revealed spherical, cauliflower-like hierarchical clusters with a hydrodynamic diameter (Z-average) of 111.68 nm, narrow polydispersity (PDI = 0.2860), and stable negative surface charge (ζ = - 14.96 mV). The Ag@CeO2 NPs displayed pronounced, tumor-selective cytotoxicity, yielding an IC₅₀ of 32.14 µg/mL against PC-3 cells while sparing normal HFF-1 fibroblasts (IC₅₀ = 171.6 µg/mL, > 5.3-fold selectivity window). Mechanistically, the nanocomposite triggered a severe, concentration-dependent intracellular ROS burst (*p* < 0.0001 at 30 µM) accompanied by the functional collapse of the cellular antioxidant barrier through profound suppression of SOD (*p* < 0.01) and CAT (*p* < 0.0001) activities. This unmitigated oxidative crisis was associated with increased TP53 transcript levels and increased p53-associated protein signals as measured by ELISA (*p* < 0.0001), which coincided with upregulated Bax, downregulated Bcl-2, and elevated the Bax/Bcl-2 ratio (*p* < 0.001), consistent with activation of mitochondrial apoptotic signaling. Ag@CeO2 NPs function as a potent, tumor-selective pro-oxidant nanotherapeutic platform capable of overriding endogenous antioxidant defenses, enhancing p53-associated apoptotic signaling and promoting mitochondrial apoptotic responses, suggesting that Ag@CeO2 NPs may serve as a potential candidate for further investigation in prostate cancer nanomedicine.

articles.title: The gut microbiota-IPA axis mediated by catalpol alleviates DSS-induced colitis through AhR activation.
articles.abstract: Current management strategies for colitis predominantly involve broad immunosuppression, underscoring the urgent need for strategies that restore essential homeostatic pathways. Insufficient activation of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) by microbial metabolites compromises its crucial role in maintaining mucosal integrity, a defect commonly observed in colitis. While the natural compound catalpol exhibits preventive potential, its precise function within host-microbiota crosstalk remained undefined. This study aims to investigate the protective effects of catalpol on colitis, focusing on the role of gut microbiota and its metabolite, indole-3-propionic acid (IPA). A mouse model of DSS-induced colitis was utilized. The protective outcomes and mechanisms were assessed through integrated multi-omics analyses, functional validation via microbial manipulation, and molecular studies confirming the activation of the AhR pathway. In this study, catalpol protects against DSS-induced colitis in mice, and this protection is associated with alterations in gut microbiota composition. Integrated multi-omics analysis suggests that catalpol treatment is associated with increased relative abundance of Lachnospiraceae at the family level and with elevated levels of the microbial metabolite indole-3-propionic acid. Functional validation through fecal microbiota transplantation from catalpol-treated mice or direct IPA supplementation partially reproduced several protective effects, suggesting that IPA may be a downstream mediator contributing to the protective effects of catalpol. Molecular analyses indicate that both catalpol and IPA can physically interact with AhR. Importantly, pharmacological suppression of AhR partially reversed the protective effects, suggesting that AhR activation contributes to the protective effects of catalpol. Collectively, these findings suggest that catalpol protects against DSS-induced colitis, and this effect is associated with increased relative abundance of Lachnospiraceae at the family level and elevated IPA levels, potentially contributing to a microbiota-IPA-AhR axis. This work highlights the preventive potential of restoring host-microbiota metabolic crosstalk and provides a rationale for developing microbiota-targeted protective strategies.

articles.title: Contraindication-adjusted prescription omission patterns of RASi, beta-blockers, and MRAs in hospitalized heart failure: associations with 30-day and 1-year mortality.
articles.abstract: Guideline directed therapy is still underused in heart failure and little is known about how missing specific medications near discharge relates to survival. The aim of this study is to examine whether study-defined omission patterns of RASi (ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or ARNIs), beta-blockers, and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) in the final 48 h before discharge were associated with short-term and 1-year mortality among hospitalized adults with heart failure. Adult admissions with a recorded heart failure diagnosis were identified using ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes. The three classes were RASi, beta-blockers, and MRAs (SGLT2 inhibitors were not included). A contraindication-adjusted operational framework was used to identify admissions without selected laboratory or hemodynamic barriers to these therapies and to classify late-hospital prescription omission patterns. Final-48-h orders were a proxy for treatment near discharge, not a reconciled discharge list. This framework did not establish heart failure phenotype-specific guideline eligibility. Associations with mortality within 30 and 365 days after discharge were evaluated using multivariable regression models. The final analytic cohort included 57,098 admissions from 24,922 patients. The reference group with prescriptions for all three study classes was small whereas omission of 2 or 3 therapies was substantially more common across the cohort. Admissions with prescriptions for all three study classes had the lowest 365-day mortality (13.88%). Crude 365-day mortality was higher in all omission groups, reaching 30.84% when RASi and beta-blocker were omitted and 27.50% when all three classes were omitted. In adjusted analyses, omission of all 3 therapies was associated with higher 30-day mortality (OR = 1.67). For 365-day mortality, the strongest adverse association was observed for omission of renin-angiotensin system inhibitor plus beta-blocker (HR = 1.33). Late-hospital omission patterns involving RASi and omission of all three study therapies were associated with higher post-discharge mortality. As heart failure phenotype and left-ventricular ejection fraction were not incorporated into the eligibility definition, these findings should be interpreted as prognostic associations of prescribing patterns rather than causal effects of withholding guideline-indicated HFrEF therapy.

articles.title: Combined melatonin and edaravone therapy attenuates methylmercury-induced amyotrophic lateral sclerosis-like neurodegeneration through GLP-1 modulation and myelin preservation.
articles.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive and fatal neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the selective degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons, resulting in progressive muscle weakness, paralysis, and respiratory failure. Despite the availability of disease-modifying therapies, current treatment options provide only modest clinical benefits, highlighting the need for novel therapeutic strategies targeting multiple pathological mechanisms. Melatonin, a pleiotropic neuroprotective molecule with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic properties, has emerged as a promising candidate; however, its influence on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-associated neuroprotective signaling and related molecular events in ALS remains poorly understood. Therefore, the present study investigated the neuroprotective efficacy of melatonin in a methylmercury (MTMR)-induced rat model of ALS and explored its effects on GLP-1-associated molecular alterations, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, neurotransmitter homeostasis, demyelination, and neuronal injury. Molecular docking analysis was performed to predict the interaction of melatonin with proteins implicated in ALS pathology. Adult Wistar rats were exposed to MTMR (5 mg/kg, p.o.) for 21 days to induce ALS-like neurodegeneration, followed by treatment with melatonin (5 or 10 mg/kg, i.p.), edaravone (3 mg/kg, i.p.), or their combination for an additional 21 days. Neurobehavioral performance, biochemical alterations, hematological parameters, molecular biomarkers, and histopathological changes were subsequently evaluated. MTMR administration produced profound motor deficits accompanied by reduced GLP-1 levels, neurotransmitter imbalance, increased neuroinflammatory and apoptotic markers, elevated neurofilament light chain (NEFL), skeletal muscle injury, methylmercury accumulation, and extensive myelin and neuronal damage. Melatonin treatment significantly attenuated these pathological alterations in a dose-dependent manner by increasing GLP-1 levels, improving antioxidant status, reducing inflammatory and apoptotic responses, restoring neurotransmitter balance, preserving myelin integrity, and improving neuronal morphology across multiple brain regions and the spinal cord. Molecular docking further predicted favorable interactions between melatonin and several proteins associated with ALS pathophysiology, supporting its potential as a multitarget therapeutic agent. In most outcome measures, combined treatment with melatonin and edaravone produced greater neuroprotective effects than either intervention alone. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that melatonin substantially attenuates methylmercury-induced ALS-like neuropathology through coordinated modulation of multiple pathological processes associated with neurodegeneration. Although the precise molecular mechanisms require further experimental validation, the observed restoration of GLP-1 levels together with improvements in oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, apoptosis, neurotransmitter homeostasis, and myelin integrity suggests that melatonin may represent a promising adjunctive therapeutic strategy for ALS.

articles.title: Hesperetin-loaded transethosomes for management of skin cancer: formulation and optimization by Box-Behnken design and in vitro, ex vivo, and dermatokinetic studies.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to develop and optimize hesperetin-loaded transethosomes (HSP-TEs) to ameliorate skin cancer, yet enhancing skin permeability, deposition, and stability. HSP-TEs were prepared using thin-film hydration and optimized through a Box-Behnken design (BBD). The optimized formulation exhibited a vesicle size of 134.27 ± 3.17 nm, polydispersity index of 0.209 ± 0.006, zeta potential of - 27.39 ± 0.53 mV, and entrapment efficiency of 90.33 ± 3.88%, confirming nanoscale stability and uniformity. HSP-TEs were further incorporated into a Carbopol-based HSP-TE loaded gel (HSP-TEG) for topical application. Comparative in vitro release studies revealed sustained release from HSP-TEs (71.77 ± 6.79%), followed by HSP-TEG (60.03 ± 4.13%) at 24 h, whereas significantly lower release was observed from hesperetin suspension (HSP-S, 32.23 ± 5.09%) and hesperetin-suspension gel (HSP-SG, 25.76 ± 3.55%) at 24 h. Ex vivo permeation studies demonstrated superior skin penetration from HSP-TEs (63.70 ± 5.19%) and HSP-TEG (51.03 ± 3.12%) compared to HSP-S (27.23 ± 2.16%) and HSP-SG (23.87 ± 1.09%) at 24 h. Confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) analysis of HSP-TEs revealed greater skin permeability. Dermatokinetic analysis confirmed enhanced epidermal and dermal drug deposition from HSP-TEG. The cytotoxicity studies in A431 epidermoid carcinoma cells demonstrated greater time- and concentration-dependent anticancer effects for HSP-TEs relative to free drug (p < 0.05). The optimized formulation revealed sustained release and improved permeability and stability, suggesting a promising platform for management skin cancer.

articles.title: Potentially harmful excipients in drugs: an analysis of labeling practices and adverse drug reactions.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Excipients play a crucial role in pharmaceutical formulations, however, their safety profile in pediatric populations remains inadequately characterized. METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study was conducted in two phases. Phase one reviewed package inserts of pediatric medications used at seven Fujian hospitals (July 2019-June 2024) to assess excipient labeling. Phase two analyzed associations between potentially harmful excipients (PHEs) exposure and adverse drug reactions using the reporting odds ratio (ROR) method at a single children's hospital. RESULTS: The rates of excipient labeling exhibited significant variation based on hospital type, drug source, and drug category. In total, 41.3% of pediatric cases and 43.2% of prescriptions included at least one PHE. Benzyl alcohol was associated with application site pain (ROR = 393.20, P < 0.05) and erythema (ROR = 85.84, P < 0.05); thimerosal was linked to application site irritation (ROR = 278.35, P < 0.05) and pruritus (ROR = 115.20, P < 0.05); and sodium citrate was associated with bradycardia (ROR = 157.59, P < 0.05). CONCLUSION: The labeling of excipients in pediatric pharmaceutical products is insufficient in the institutions examined, potentially hindering the identification of excipient exposure in clinical practice. The safety signals identified in this study necessitate further systematic investigation and careful consideration within both regulatory and clinical contexts.

articles.title: Scorpion toxin peptide BMK86-P1 achieves mutation-reversible inhibition of KCNA2 at the cost of reduced efficacy in heteromers and murine neurons.
articles.abstract: The discovery of distinctive function-phenotype relationships in monogenetic channelopathies has turned out to be critical for the development of precision medicine approaches. However, the most accurate prediction of clinical phenotypes depends on neuronal function, where existing models lack tools to isolate currents of individual voltage-gated potassium channel subunits and to differentiate variant effects in complex systems. Ideally, one should be able to overexpress subunit variants with an additional mutation that would confer resistance against the tool used to isolate the variant effect. Therefore, we solid-phase synthesized the KV1.2 specific scorpion toxin peptide BMK86-P1 and oxidized it with modest efficacy. In mammalian cells this BMK86-P1 selectively inhibited KV1.2 homomers, but not heteromers with KV1.1. Critically, the KCNA2 p. Val381Tyr mutation, which reverses BMK86-P1's selective inhibition of KV1.2, also altered the activation of KV1.2 homomers to resemble those of KV1.1. In addition, in murine neurons, BMK86-P1 did not alter passive membrane properties, single action potential properties, or action potential firing. Surprisingly, it induced only minimal changes in spontaneous excitatory postsynaptic currents. In summary, this KV1.2 subunit selective toxin peptide primarily affects homomeric channels, while only weakly inhibiting KV1.2/KV1.1 heteromeric channels and consequently preventing any meaningful impact on neuronal function. This highlights the limitations of peptide synthesis together with the need for testing specific compounds on complex systems.

articles.title: A redox-inflammasome threshold model of ovulation: a hypothesis on NLRP3-Mediated regulation.
articles.abstract: Ovulation is a highly coordinated biological process involving endocrine regulation, tissue remodeling, immune activation, metabolic adaptation, and redox signaling. Although inflammatory responses are recognized as essential components of follicular rupture, the mechanisms integrating oxidative stress, metabolic alterations, and inflammasome activation during ovulatory progression remain incompletely understood. Here, we propose a hypothesis-driven redox-inflammasome threshold model of ovulatory regulation, in which NLRP3 inflammasome signaling may serve as an important integrator of redox and metabolic cues that modulate inflammatory remodeling during the periovulatory period. This model suggests that successful ovulation requires a precisely balanced inflammatory threshold, whereas insufficient or excessive inflammasome activation may disrupt follicular homeostasis and contribute to ovarian dysfunction. Importantly, NLRP3 is proposed not as an indispensable determinant of follicular rupture, but as one regulatory component within a complex network involving cytokines, prostaglandins, matrix metalloproteinases, immune cells, and hormonal signals. By integrating current evidence linking mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, metabolic stress, and inflammation, this hypothesis provides a conceptual framework for understanding ovulation as a redox-sensitive immune-metabolic process. Future studies using cell type-specific NLRP3 manipulation, quantitative redox analysis, and single-cell approaches will be required to determine the physiological contribution of inflammasome signaling to ovulatory regulation.

articles.title: Evaluating student perceptions of image-based audience response questions in medical education.
articles.abstract: Audience response systems have been extensively utilized in medical and pharmacy education to improve learner engagement and knowledge retention. Unlike traditional ARSs that utilize text-based multiple-choice questions Hotspot is an image-based ARS integrated into PointSolutions that allows students to answer questions by selecting areas of interest on images and figures, rather than choosing from multiple-choice options. The purpose of this study was to evaluate student perceptions of integrating Hotspot into pharmacology and biomedical curricula, including perceived engagement, learning reinforcement, usability and preferences relative to traditional MCQs. Faculty at California Northstate University incorporated Hotspot questions into the lectures of first- and second-year courses across three matriculating classes. Following these sessions, students completed an anonymous survey. Survey items assessed student perceptions of engagement, perceived learning, and ease of use on a seven-point Likert scale. Learners reported that Hotspot technology made it easier to pay attention during lectures (median Likert score of six out of seven [interquartile range (IQR) 5-7]; n = 99). They felt the questions were a good use of class time (6 out of 7 [interquartile range 6-7]; n = 99) and indicated that the interactive format challenged them and reinforced their understanding better than MCQs (6 out of 7 [IQR 5-7]; n = 99). Overall, learners expressed a preference for Hotspot over traditional MCQs and reported that this approach was more engaging. These findings support the feasibility and learner acceptability of incorporating image-based active learning strategies and provide evidence to support the adoption of innovative instructional approaches in medical and pharmacology education.

articles.title: Irrigation fluid absorption induces metabolic and oxidative stress dysregulation activating NLRP3 and NF-κB pathways to drive hippocampal inflammatory responses.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Irrigation fluid absorption during endoscopic procedures can lead to serious complications, but its effects on hippocampal function remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the impact of irrigation fluid absorption on hippocampal metabolic homeostasis and inflammatory responses. METHODS: Adult female Sprague-Dawley rats received intravenous 0.9% saline (control, 40 mL/kg, or 80 mL/kg) to simulate irrigation fluid absorption. Saline was infused over 30 min, and the animals were euthanized 15 min after cessation of anesthesia, corresponding to 45 min after initiation of the infusion. We assessed emergence time from anesthesia, hippocampal energy metabolism through targeted metabolomics, mitochondrial ultrastructure via transmission electron microscopy (TEM), oxidative stress markers, and NLRP3- and NF-κB-related inflammatory markers. RESULTS: The 80 mL/kg group showed significantly prolonged anesthesia emergence time compared to controls (59.0 ± 13.5 vs. 31.7 ± 4.5 s; p < 0.01). Metabolomics revealed dose-dependent perturbations in the TCA cycle, glycolysis, and oxidative phosphorylation (p < 0.05). TEM analysis demonstrated severe mitochondrial ultrastructural damage in hippocampal neurons, including dose-dependent swelling, internal membrane disruption, and matrix dissolution. Both absorption groups showed altered glutathione redox status, characterized by increased GSSG levels and decreased GSH/GSSG ratios (p < 0.01), whereas SOD, CAT, MDA, NADPH, and GSH exhibited heterogeneous and non-linear changes across doses. At this early endpoint, increased NLRP3, P50/P65, IL-6, IL-18, and IL-33 immunoreactivity, together with decreased IκB immunoreactivity, indicated early changes in NLRP3- and NF-κB-related inflammatory signaling. CONCLUSION: Excessive irrigation fluid absorption induces hippocampal neuroinflammation through metabolic disturbance and redox dysregulation, which activates NLRP3 and NF-κB pathways. These findings suggest potential therapeutic targets for preventing neurological complications during endoscopic procedures.

articles.title: Conditional approval of oncology medicines in Europe (2017-2022): evidence maturity, regulatory outcomes, clinical benefit and downstream access.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Conditional marketing authorisation (CMA) is a European regulatory pathway that enables earlier access to medicines for serious conditions while allowing additional evidence generation after approval. Important questions remain regarding the maturity of supporting evidence, subsequent regulatory outcomes, clinical benefit, and patient access. We characterised the evidentiary basis, regulatory outcomes, clinical benefit, clinical practice guideline incorporation, and downstream access of oncology medicines granted CMA between 2017 and 2022. METHODS: We analysed all antineoplastic medicines granted CMA by the European Commission between 1 January 2017 and 31 December 2022. European Medicines Agency documentation was reviewed to assess regulatory characteristics, post-authorisation obligations, pivotal studies, and outcomes through 31 March 2025. Clinical benefit was evaluated using ESMO-MCBS, while reimbursement was assessed in Spain as an illustrative case of downstream access as of 15 December 2025. Kaplan-Meier analysis estimated time to regulatory resolution and reimbursement. RESULTS: Twenty-six antineoplastic medicines received CMA, representing 55.3% of all CMA approvals. Most pivotal studies were single-arm (92.9%), open-label, and used surrogate primary endpoints, with a median efficacy sample size of 100.5 participants (IQR 78.5-128.0). Thirty-five specific obligations were imposed, with a median time of 3.95 years (IQR 1.73-5.23) from CMA approval to the latest due date. By 31 March 2025, 53.8% remained under CMA, 38.5% converted to standard marketing authorisation, and 7.7% were withdrawn. Median time to regulatory resolution was 4.46 years. Only 16.7% (3/18) demonstrated substantial clinical benefit according to ESMO-MCBS. Most medicines were subsequently incorporated into ESMO or EHA clinical practice guidelines, although only five (19.2%) received an IA recommendation corresponding to their first CMA-approved indication; two additional medicines received IA recommendations in earlier treatment settings. Public reimbursement was granted for 84.6% (22/26), with a median time of 2.38 years. CONCLUSION: Oncology medicines granted CMA were frequently supported by limited and immature evidence, while substantial clinical benefit was uncommon and regulatory resolution often required several years. Future optimisation should combine timely access with timely post-authorisation evidence generation, including comparative clinical and real-world evidence.

articles.title: N-acetylcysteine ameliorates oxidative stress-induced decline in sex hormone-binding globulin in HepG2 cells and polycystic ovary syndrome rats.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Low sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) levels are a significant indicator of hyperandrogenism severity in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and are associated with an increased risk of reproductive and metabolic diseases. Oxidative stress suppresses the production and secretion of SHBG. However, the effect of the antioxidant N-acetylcysteine (NAC) on hepatic SHBG expression remains unknown. This study investigated the effects of NAC on SHBG expression and the underlying mechanism in HepG2 cells and a rat model of PCOS. METHODS: HepG2 cells were treated with testosterone propionate (TP), oxidized high-density lipoprotein (ox-HDL), oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL), and NAC. Female Sprague-Dawley rats aged 28 days were randomly allocated to eight groups: control, PCOS, and control and PCOS groups treated with NAC at 100, 200, or 400 mg/kg body weight. The PCOS rat model, induced by TP and a high-fat, high-sugar diet, was treated with different doses of NAC for 8 weeks. The expression of SHBG, hepatocyte nuclear factor 4α (HNF4α), chicken ovalbumin upstream promoter-transcription factor 1 (COUP-TF1), and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ (PPAR-γ) was assessed in HepG2 cells and rat liver tissue. Metabolic, hormonal, and oxidative stress indices were analyzed in the rat model. RESULTS: In HepG2 cells, TP and oxidized lipoprotein treatments significantly suppressed SHBG and HNF4α expression, while NAC treatment reversed the inhibitory effects induced by ox-HDL and ox-LDL (P < 0.05). In PCOS rats, NAC intervention increased the mRNA and protein levels of SHBG by upregulating HNF4α and downregulating COUP-TF1 and PPAR-γ expression in the liver; increased serum SHBG; reduced hepatocytic reactive oxygen species levels (P < 0.05); and ameliorated obesity, estrous cycle abnormalities, hepatic steatosis, circulating sex hormone levels, and the lipid profile, with 200 mg/kg NAC showing the most favorable overall pattern among the three doses tested. CONCLUSION: NAC treatment ameliorates oxidative stress-induced decreases in SHBG and HNF4α expression in HepG2 cells and may restore hepatocytic SHBG production by upregulating HNF4α and downregulating COUP-TF1/PPAR-γ expression in rats with PCOS.

articles.title: Economic evaluation of six immune checkpoint inhibitor-based first-line therapies for advanced squamous non-small-cell lung cancer: a cost-effectiveness analysis based on network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Advanced squamous non-small-cell lung cancer (sq-NSCLC) imposes a substantial clinical and economic burden. Immune checkpoint inhibitors (sugemalimab, tislelizumab, penpulimab, serplulimab, camrelizumab, and pembrolizumab) combined with chemotherapy improve survival, but their comparative cost-effectiveness remains uncertain. METHODS: A three-state partitioned survival model with 3-week cycles and a lifetime horizon was developed from the Chinese healthcare-system perspective. Clinical efficacy was derived from six phase 3 trials and synthesized using network meta-analysis. Costs, life-years (LYs), quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), and incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) for each ICI-based regimen versus chemotherapy were estimated. The willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold was set at $27,906/QALY. Deterministic, probabilistic, scenario, and full incremental analyses were performed. RESULTS: In the base-case analysis, chemotherapy alone yielded 0.71 QALYs at $12,227.47. All ICI-based regimens increased QALYs to between 1.24 and 2.07. Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy provided the greatest health benefit, yielding 2.07 QALYs, but had an ICER of $70,913.04 per QALY versus chemotherapy alone. Penpulimab plus chemotherapy had the lowest ICER versus chemotherapy alone ($13,064.23 per QALY), followed by camrelizumab ($13,361.50/QALY), and tislelizumab plus chemotherapy ($14,022.95/QALY), all below the WTP threshold. Sugemalimab plus chemotherapy and serplulimab plus chemotherapy exceeded the threshold. Probabilistic sensitivity analysis indicated that camrelizumab plus chemotherapy had the highest probability of being cost-effective (95%) at $27,906/QALY. In the full incremental analysis, the efficiency frontier comprised chemotherapy alone, penpulimab plus chemotherapy, camrelizumab plus chemotherapy, and pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy; camrelizumab plus chemotherapy was the preferred strategy after dominated options were excluded. CONCLUSION: At the selected WTP threshold, camrelizumab plus chemotherapy may be the preferred first-line strategy after strictly and extendedly dominated alternatives were excluded. This finding depends on the indirect comparisons, chemotherapy baseline, drug prices, survival extrapolation, and post-progression assumptions.

articles.title: Repurposing farnesyltransferase inhibitors tipifarnib and lonafarnib as antibacterial agents: proteomic and functional analyses.
articles.abstract: Farnesyltransferase inhibitors (FTIs) like tipifarnib and lonafarnib, originally developed as anticancer agents, show antibacterial activity against Gram-positive pathogens through an unknown mechanism of action. Here, we investigated the proteomic response of Bacillus subtilis 168 (Gram-positive) and an efflux-deficient Escherichia coli ΔtolC mutant (Gram-negative) to sublethal concentrations of FTIs. Concentrations resulting in approximately 50% growth inhibition were applied, followed by two complementary proteomic approaches: gel-free quantitative LC-HDMSE (both organisms) and 2D-PAGE with [35S]-methionine pulse labelling of newly synthesized proteins (B. subtilis). Marker proteins from the B. subtilis 2D-PAGE approach were used for comparative proteomic response profiling against a reference library of 96 antibacterial agents. Bacillus subtilis was more susceptible to both FTIs than E. coli ΔtolC, with tipifarnib being more potent. LC-HDMSE analysis revealed a pronounced cell envelope stress signature in B. subtilis, including regulation of YocH, YabE, and YjhA, along with several σB, σW, and σM-regulated stress proteins. In the 2D-PAGE analysis, reflecting acute cellular responses by monitoring newly synthesized proteins, both FTIs induced proteins such as ClpC, PspA, and LiaH. Comparative proteomic response analysis in B. subtilis showed that both FTIs cluster with membrane-active antibiotics, including xanthoangelol, MP196, gramicidin S, MP66, and nisin, which binds the cell wall precursor lipid II and forms pores in the bacterial membrane. Similarities were also observed with pseudopterosin G and pseudopteroxazole, which target the bacterial cell envelope by integration into the membrane and interfering with membrane-bound steps of cell wall biosynthesis. Yet, the similarity of the proteomic profiles does not indicate a perfect match or an identical molecular mode of action within the reference library. In E. coli ΔtolC, the proteomic response was less pronounced, but for treatment with tipifarnib, regulated proteins of the category "membrane-bounded periplasmic space" were enriched. Proteomic profiling, combined with functional validation via membrane integrity and membrane potential assays, indicates that FTIs compromise the bacterial membrane and activate stress and repair pathways. The FTIs may also indirectly affect cell wall biosynthesis. The lack of a perfect match with any of the 96 compounds in the proteomic reference library highlights FTIs as promising lead structures for the development of novel antibiotics.

articles.title: OGT-mediated O-GlcNAcylation stabilizes EGR1 to drive vascular leakage in acute respiratory distress syndrome.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Increased vascular permeability is a hallmark of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), yet the molecular mechanisms underlying this process remain poorly understood. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An ARDS mouse model was established by intratracheal instillation of LPS. Proteomic analysis was performed to identify differentially expressed proteins. Protein and gene expression were assessed by western blotting and RT-qPCR. Immunoprecipitation, mass spectrometry, mutagenesis, ubiquitination, and O-GlcNAcylation assays were employed to investigate the underlying molecular mechanisms. KEY FINDINGS: We identified O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) as a critical regulator of endothelial barrier dysfunction in ARDS. Proteomic profiling of alveolar endothelial cells isolated from LPS-induced ARDS mice revealed marked upregulation of OGT and the transcription factor early growth response 1 (EGR1). Mechanistically, OGT directly O-GlcNAcylates EGR1 at threonine 329, preventing RNF5 (Ring Finger Protein 5)-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation and thereby stabilizing EGR1 under inflammatory conditions. Stabilized EGR1 subsequently associates with the transcriptional coactivators CBP (CREB-binding protein) and PCAF (p300/CBP-associated factor) to form a functional complex that binds the promoters of vascular permeability-related genes, including VEGFA (vascular endothelial growth factor A), ANGPT2 (angiopoietin 2), ICAM1 (intercellular adhesion molecule 1), and MMP9 (matrix metallopeptidase 9), thereby promoting their transcription. Pharmacological inhibition of OGT markedly reduced EGR1 stabilization, suppressed permeability-associated gene expression, and significantly attenuated vascular leakage in ARDS mice. SIGNIFICANCE: These findings reveal a previously unrecognized OGT-EGR1-CBP/PCAF signaling axis that drives endothelial barrier dysfunction in ARDS and highlight potential therapeutic targets for this life-threatening disease.

articles.title: Natural ent-kaurene diterpenoid eriocalyxin B suppresses triple negative breast cancer metastasis via modulation of Smad4 SUMOylation and TGF-β signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: SUMOylation plays a pivotal role in cancer progression by regulating protein stability and signaling pathways. The natural ent-kaurene diterpenoid Eriocalyxin B (Eri B) has been shown to effectively suppress breast cancer metastasis in our previous cell-based and mouse studies. The present study aimed to investigate the potential mechanism of action of Eri B on the interplay between SUMOylation and the TGF-β/Smad pathway in triple negative breast cancer. In vitro and in vivo experiments (including proteomic profiling, western blotting, immunofluorescence assays, breast xenograft-bearing mouse model) have been conducted to evaluate the effects of Eri B on SUMOylation, TGF-β signaling, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and metastasis. Our results showed that Eri B significantly suppressed the expression of SUMO1, SUMO2/3 in breast cancer MDA-MB-231 and BT-20 cells. Proteomic profiling of SUMOylated proteins in MDA-MB-231 xenograft tumors revealed that Eri B specifically attenuated SUMOylation events mediated by E3 ligases, particularly targeting PIAS family members (PIAS1/3/4) with clinical relevance. Furthermore, immunofluorescence analysis in breast cancer cells indicated that Eri B reduced the SUMO1 modification signal associated with Smad4. As SUMOylation of Smad4 is required for its nuclear translocation and transcriptional activity, the inhibition of TGF-β/Smad pathway induced by Eri B might partly mediate through disruption of PIAS1-dependent Smad4 SUMOylation. This mechanism ultimately suppressed TGF-β-induced epithelial-mesenchymal transition and metastasis-related protein expressions. In conclusion, this is the first report to propose Eri B as a modulator of the PIAS1-mediated SUMOylation with downstream effects on TGF-β/Smad signaling, providing a mechanistic basis for its anti-metastatic efficacy in breast cancer.

articles.title: Surface functionalized layer by layer assembled hyaluronic acid/Chitosan emulsomes for localized targeted transdermal breast cancer therapy in a 7,12-Dimethylbenz[a]anthracene-induced rat model.
Liquid crystalline nanoparticle-mediated co-delivery of gentamicin and rhDNase against mature Escherichia coli ATCC 25922 biofilms.
articles.abstract: Biofilm-associated infections remain a major clinical challenge due to restricted antibiotic penetration, matrix-mediated antimicrobial tolerance, and rapid degradation of biofilm-disruptive therapeutics in protease-rich environments. Here, liquid crystalline nanoparticles (LCNPs) were developed as a nanostructured co-delivery platform for gentamicin (GEN) and recombinant human DNase I (rhDNase), integrating antibiotic delivery with enzymatic disruption of the biofilm extracellular matrix. LCNPs exhibited favourable physicochemical properties, including nanoscale particle size, low polydispersity, and preservation of cubosome-like internal morphology following enzyme incorporation. High encapsulation efficiencies were achieved for GEN (∼95%) and rhDNase (∼94%). Compared with conventional liposomes, LCNPs demonstrated sustained GEN release, prolonged rhDNase retention, and improved protection of rhDNase against proteolytic degradation, highlighting the role of the liquid crystalline matrix in therapeutic retention and enzyme stability. Antibiofilm studies against mature Escherichia coli biofilms showed concentration-dependent potentiation of GEN activity by rhDNase, with further enhancement through LCNP-mediated co-delivery. While unformulated GEN produced modest biofilm reduction (∼20-30%), optimised GEN + rhDNase-LCNPs reduced residual biofilm biomass to ∼25-30% of untreated controls and produced ∼5-6 log reductions in recoverable biofilm-associated bacteria in MBEC assays. Confocal imaging showed a broader distribution of membrane-compromised bacteria across the imaged biofilm field following LCNP-mediated co-delivery, without directly resolving penetration depth. LCNP formulations also maintained favourable cytocompatibility at therapeutically relevant concentrations. Overall, these findings provide proof-of-concept that LCNP-mediated co-delivery can improve GEN activity against mature E. coli ATCC 25922 biofilms while protecting rhDNase; validation across additional strains, clinical isolates, and bacterial species is required before broader antibiofilm generalisation.

articles.title: MMP-responsive multiwalled carbon nanotubes enable tumor-selective drug delivery with altered intracellular trafficking and reduced off-target toxicity.
articles.abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) is a widely used chemotherapeutic agent, but its clinical efficacy is limited by multidrug resistance (MDR), poor tumor penetration, and off-target toxicity. To address these challenges, we developed matrix metalloproteinase (MMP)-responsive multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) for tumor-targeted DOX delivery. The MWCNT formulation exhibited MMP-responsive cellular uptake, cell permeability, tissue penetration, and enhanced cytotoxicity of loaded DOX in cancer cells, a transwell model, and tumor spheroids. Mechanistic studies revealed that these CNTs entered cells primarily via clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Acidic endosomal conditions promoted lipid redistribution and membrane destabilization of endolysosomes, facilitating efficient endosomal escape and strong colocalization with the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). This intracellular trafficking pathway bypassed drug efflux mechanisms and prolonged intracellular drug retention in MDR cancer cells. In a mouse breast tumor model, MMP-responsive MWCNTs resulted in approximately 5-fold higher blood DOX levels and 2-fold greater tumor DOX accumulation than free DOX at the end of the treatment regimen. Improved pharmacokinetics and tumor specificity enhanced DOX's tumor inhibitory effects and increased tumor cell apoptosis. Importantly, the MMP-responsive MWCNTs significantly reduced DOX's off-target toxicity, as evidenced by approximately 2-fold lower cardiac DOX accumulation, reduced cardiomyocyte apoptosis, and preservation of white blood cell counts. Overall, this MMP-responsive CNT-based nanoplatform offers a promising strategy to enhance tumor targeting and retention, overcome MDR, and improve the therapeutic index of DOX.

articles.title: A structure-based virtual screening-driven discovery pharmaceutics platform for cancer therapeutics development: FDA 505(b)(2) repurposing of netupitant as a BMX-targeted nanomedicine using quality-by-design lipid nanoparticles and model-informed PBPK translation.
articles.abstract: Bone marrow tyrosine kinase on chromosome X (BMX) is an emerging therapeutic target implicated in prostate cancer progression, metastatic disease, and resistance to current therapies; however, no selective BMX-targeted therapy has advanced to clinical development. Building upon our previously established AI-driven BMX discovery platform, this study presents an integrated Discovery Pharmaceutics strategy combining artificial intelligence-assisted drug repurposing, Quality-by-Design (QbD)-guided lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulation, experimental validation, and physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling to accelerate clinical translation through the FDA 505(b)(2) regulatory pathway. An structure-based virtual screening workflow comprising 2,115 FDA-approved small molecules identified netupitant as one of the highest-ranked candidates against the BMX catalytic domain, exhibiting a predicted binding affinity of -10.9 kcal/mol together with favorable selectivity over closely related Tec-family kinases. Netupitant demonstrated concentration-dependent inhibition of prostate cancer cell growth with IC50 values of 15.97 μM in DU145 cells and 7.1 μM in PC3 cells. A Box-Behnken Design optimized Netupitant-loaded lipid nanoparticles (Netupitant-LNPs) with a particle size of 133.9 ± 3.2 nm, polydispersity index of 0.213 ± 0.005, zeta potential of + 30 ± 1.3 mV, and encapsulation efficiency of 97.3 ± 0.7%. Cryogenic transmission electron microscopy confirmed uniformly dispersed spherical nanoparticles with an average diameter of 130 ± 6 nm, consistent with dynamic light scattering measurements. The nanoformulation substantially enhanced therapeutic efficacy, reducing IC50 values to 1.1 μM in DU145 cells and 0.5 μM in PC3 cells, representing approximately 15-fold and 14-fold improvements, respectively, over free netupitant. To facilitate clinical translation, experimentally determined formulation characteristics were incorporated into a mechanistic Simcyp® Version 25.2 middle-out physiologically based pharmacokinetic model. The exploratory PBPK model compared alternative intravenous dosing scenarios and identified 100 mg once weekly as a candidate regimen for further evaluation; these simulations do not establish a clinical dosing recommendation. Collectively, this work demonstrates that integrating AI-enabled drug repurposing, Discovery Pharmaceutics, nanomedicine engineering, and model-informed drug development provides an effective strategy for accelerating oncology drug development. Netupitant-LNPs emerge as a repurposed nanomedicine candidate with predicted BMX binding while establishing a broadly applicable translational framework for FDA-approved drug repurposing through the 505(b)(2) pathway.

articles.title: Inhibition of ketoprofen photodecomposition mediated by methyl radicals: ion-pair formation with dibucaine and selection of radical-free patch base materials.
articles.abstract: Ketoprofen (KP), the most photosensitive non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug, causes photocontact dermatitis attributed to free radicals generated under irradiation. We examined which radical species KP intercepts and how to limit exposure to them. Of three species generated independently (•OH, O2•⁻ and •CH3), only •CH3 showed a dependence on KP concentration, in both a 2,2'-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (ABTS) competition assay and electron spin resonance (ESR) spin trapping with 5,5-dimethyl-1-pyrroline N-oxide (DMPO). Dibucaine (DBC) suppressed KP photodegradation, reducing the rate constant from 5.88 to 3.20 × 10-2 min-1, and was more effective than Trolox® (6-hydroxy-2,5,7,8-tetramethylchroman-2-carboxylic acid). Differential scanning calorimetry and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy located the interaction at KP's carboxyl group, the site where photodegradation is initiated, with 1:1 stoichiometry, consistent with an ion pair involving hydrophobic hydration. Unlike an antioxidant or a UV absorber, DBC was not consumed under UV irradiation, and unlike an inclusion complex, it engages a single functional group. DBC also reduced the patch release rate constant, so that photostabilization must be balanced against altered release. Styrene-isoprene-styrene copolymer patch bases generated radicals under UV irradiation only in grades containing dibutylhydroxytoluene. Both approaches can therefore limit KP photodegradation.

articles.title: Domain-validated residual XGBoost surrogates for model-informed biopharmaceutics and population pharmacokinetic inference.
articles.abstract: Mechanistic population pharmacokinetic (popPK) models support model-informed biopharmaceutics, but repeated exact simulations can make nonlinear mixed-effects inference computationally expensive. We developed a domain-validated residual XGBoost surrogate embedded in stochastic approximation expectation-maximisation (SAEM) for a two-compartment popPK model implemented in PhysPK®. The emulator learned local residual deviations from a mechanistic baseline and was activated only after held-out validation against exact simulations. Fixed-effect updates were constrained within a log-parameter trust region, with exact fallback outside the validated dosing and parameter domain and exact-model recomputation of final diagnostics. Evaluation used a published six-animal preclinical monoclonal-antibody dataset, internal cohorts, 200 balanced noisy parametric bootstrap replicates of 30 virtual animals each, and sparse-sampling variants. In the external proof-of-concept cohort, surrogate-assisted SAEM reproduced the exact reference solution with profile-level mean relative error of 0.0041 and fixed effects within 3.1%. All 200 bootstrap runs completed and met the prespecified fixed-effect stability criterion by iteration 49. Bootstrap emulator error remained low (mean MRE 0.0027; maximum 0.0028), whereas θ3 (Q) showed the greatest uncertainty. Exact local and Morris sensitivity analyses supported weak practical identifiability rather than surrogate bias as the source of this instability. Single-profile evaluation was approximately 49-fold faster, supporting auditable surrogate-assisted inference within the validated applicability domain.

articles.title: Quantitative in vitro PET/MRI and kinetic modelling of imaging agent release from a thermoreversible intranasal sol-gel.
articles.abstract: Intranasal phase-transforming thermoresponsive gels can prolong nasal residence and enable controlled release of diagnostic or therapeutic payloads. However, quantitative real-time release characterisation of multimodal imaging probes remains limited. Here, we developed a poloxamer-based sol-gel and established a hybrid PET/MRI framework to quantify the release of PET tracers and an activatable MnO2 nanoflower into simulated nasal fluid. The formulations transformed from solution-to-gel at ∼ 28-29 °C with a storage modulus of 8.2-9.5  kPa attained at typical nasal cavity temperature (34 °C), while maintaining a nasal-compatible pH. PET imaging with an extended time window demonstrated diffusion-dominated release with clear size dependence: ionic [64Cu]Cu2+ reached 30.0 ± 3.0 % cumulative release at ∼42  h, whereas [64Cu]Cu-Sar-OP showed 15.6 ± 3.1 % cumulative release under the same simulated conditions. PEGylated MnO2 nanoflowers exhibited negligible apparent release in simulated nasal fluid without reductant due to the absence of redox-triggered MnO2 dissolution to soluble Mn2+ and electrolyte-induced nanoparticle aggregation trapping, which restricts diffusion out of the gel; but with GSH-supplementation, quantitative T1/T2 mapping enabled relaxivity-calibrated tracking of apparent Mn-equivalent accumulation, reaching 13.9 ± 0.7 % of the nominal loaded Mn (T1-based) at ∼24  h. The cytocompatibility of MnO2 NFs-PEG was also evaluated in an RPMI 2650 human nasal epithelial cell model following 24-h exposure. Kinetic modelling (Higuchi and Korsmeyer - Peppas) supported diffusion-dominated transfer of the PET tracers, whereas the MnO2 profile reflected coupled redox and transport processes under limited-GSH conditions. Overall, our integrated PET/MRI approach provides a quantitative framework for comparing in vitro depot release kinetics and informing intranasal PET/MRI formulation design; however, the findings should not be interpreted as direct evidence of mucosal retention or in vivo nose-to-brain transport.

articles.title: Inhibition of The Sphingosine-1-Phosphate Receptor 1 (S1PR1) as a Therapeutic Target for Aromatase Inhibitor-Induced Musculoskeletal Symptoms in Mice.
articles.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the leading cause of cancer death among women worldwide with estrogen receptor positive (ER+) BC comprising 70-80% of all cases. Adjuvant therapy with aromatase inhibitors (AIs), such as letrozole (LTZ), is the standard of care in ER+ BC patients to prevent recurrence but many patients cease treatment prematurely due to the development of musculoskeletal side effects (i.e. arthralgia, myalgia, decreased grip strength) referred to as aromatase inhibitor-associated musculoskeletal syndrome (AIMSS). The lack of efficacious treatments available for AIMSS and premature treatment cessation being linked to increased patient mortality highlights the critical importance of identifying new therapeutic targets for its management. Here, we directly link LTZ treatment with increased levels of sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 1 (S1PR1) endogenous ligands in spinal cord tissue of female ovariectomized (OVX) ICR mice. We therefore investigated the impact of reducing S1PR1 activity as a potential therapeutic strategy for alleviating AIMSS-related behaviors. In C57BL/6J OVX female mice, we found that pharmacological inhibition using the selective and competitive S1PR1 antagonist, NIBR-0213, effectively alleviated AIMSS-like behaviors after acute and repeated dosing regimens, with limited therapeutic effectiveness when given prior to LTZ treatment. In a conditioned place preference (CPP) paradigm, LTZ- but not vehicle-treated animals preferred the NIBR-0213 paired chamber, unmasking the presence of a tonic-aversive state driven by LTZ treatment. These findings identify S1PR1 as an important mediator to AIMSS and suggest that S1PR1 antagonists may be most effective as acute interventions to provide relief from the sensory and affective burden of AIMSS.

articles.title: The GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide reduces alcohol consumption and anxiety-like behaviors during withdrawal in Marchigian Sardinian alcohol-preferring rats.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists have emerged as promising pharmacotherapeutics for alcohol use disorder (AUD). Here, we examined the effects of semaglutide, a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist, on alcohol intake and anxiety-related behaviors in Marchigian Sardinian alcohol-preferring rats, a model characterized by excessive alcohol intake and pronounced anxious and depressive-like phenotypes. Male and female rats were treated with semaglutide (0.001, 0.01 and 0.1 mg/kg, s.c.) and vehicle. Voluntary alcohol consumption was assessed using the two-bottle choice paradigm. Locomotion, anxiety, and stress responses were evaluated during withdrawal and in naïve rats, following administration of the highest dose of semaglutide (0.1 mg/kg). Furthermore, the acute effects of semaglutide on GABAergic transmission were assessed in the central nucleus of the amygdala and in the infralimbic (IL) medial pre-frontal cortex (mPFC) of naïve rats. Semaglutide reduced voluntary alcohol consumption in a dose-dependent manner, and it produced anxiolytic-like behaviors during withdrawal in the open field test. In naïve animals, semaglutide reduced locomotor activity, lowered blood glucose levels, and decreased fat mass and GABAergic transmission in the IL mPFC. Our findings support the use of the GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide as a promising pharmacotherapy for the treatment of AUD and its associated psychiatric symptoms.

articles.title: Transcriptomics-informed phenotypic screening of Rhodiola sachalinensis identifies herbacetin as a cardioprotective candidate against adverse cardiac remodeling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Rhodiola sachalinensis Boriss. (Crassulaceae) is a traditional Chinese medicinal plant whose roots and rhizomes are used to invigorate qi and promote blood circulation and have been documented for the management of qi deficiency and blood stasis, chest pain, and angina. Consistent with these traditional uses, modern pharmacological studies have reported antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and cardiovascular protective activities of R. sachalinensis. However, owing to its complex chemical composition, the bioactive constituents contributing to its cardioprotective effects remain poorly defined. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to identify cardioprotective constituents of Rhodiola sachalinensis oral solution (RS) through an integrated transcriptomics-informed phenotypic screening strategy and to elucidate the potential mechanisms underlying their effects on cardiac remodeling. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The protective effects of RS were evaluated in an isoproterenol (ISO)-induced cardiac remodeling model, followed by cardiac transcriptomic profiling. Transcriptomic signatures were then integrated with complementary phenotypic assays of phenylephrine-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and transforming growth factor-β1-induced cardiac fibroblast activation to screen a library of 101 candidate constituents. The prioritized compound was further evaluated in ISO-induced cardiac remodeling and myocardial infarction (MI) models. RESULTS: Transcriptomic profiling of RS-treated hearts identified disease-associated signatures that informed the selection of complementary phenotypic assays for cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and fibroblast activation. Screening of 101 candidate constituents prioritized herbacetin (HBT), a flavonoid showing dual activity in both assays. In vivo, HBT attenuated ISO-induced cardiac dysfunction, cardiomyocyte enlargement, and myocardial fibrosis. These effects were associated with improved mitochondrial ultrastructure, preservation of mitochondrial network integrity, and restoration of ISO-suppressed OPA1 expression. In a complementary MI model, HBT improved cardiac function and reduced adverse remodeling. Mass cytometry (CyTOF) and immunofluorescence analyses further showed that HBT treatment was associated with reduced CCR2-positive inflammatory macrophage features and increased MRC1-positive reparative macrophage features during the early post-MI response. CONCLUSIONS: This study establishes a transcriptomics-informed phenotypic screening strategy for identifying bioactive constituents of RS and identifies HBT as a cardioprotective flavonoid constituent. HBT exhibited protective effects across complementary models of cardiac remodeling, with additional evidence of mitochondrial preservation and altered post-infarction macrophage-associated features in the respective experimental settings. These findings expand the cardiovascular pharmacological understanding of R. sachalinensis and provide a framework for discovering bioactive constituents from complex medicinal plants.

articles.title: Integrated Analysis of the Blood-Absorbed and Gastric Tissue-Distributed Components of Huangqi Fuling Decoction Reveals the Inhibitory Effect on Gastric Cancer Liver Metastasis via the PRMT1/FOXO1 Axis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Huangqi Fuling Decoction (HQFLT) is a classic formula that has shown therapeutic potential against gastric cancer (GC) in clinical practice. However, its components and underlying mechanisms remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the inhibitory effect of HQFLT on liver metastasis of GC and to elucidate its potential pharmacological basis and underlying mechanisms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: UPLC-MS was used to detect the absorbed components in blood and gastric tissues from mice administered intragastrically with HQFLT. WGCNA, LASSO, SVM-RFE, and random forest were applied to screen for HQFLT targets against GC, and the core target was validated in patient tissues. Downstream proteins interacting with the core target were predicted by the STRING database, and the interactions were further analyzed by molecular dynamics simulations. CCK-8, wound healing, Transwell, and rescue assays were performed to evaluate the effects of HQFLT on GC cells. In vivo validation was conducted using a mouse hematogenous colonization model with bioluminescence imaging, H&E, and IHC staining. RESULTS: UPLC-MS identified 128 components in blood and 188 in gastric tissues, with 65 common components of HQFLT detected in both blood and gastric tissues. Machine learning identified protein arginine methyltransferase 1 (PRMT1) as a core target of HQFLT, with elevated expression in GC tissues, and Forkhead box protein O1 (FOXO1) as its downstream target. Inhibition of PRMT1 or FOXO1 suppressed cell migration and invasion, while rescue assays showed that HQFLT exerted its effects partially through regulating the PRMT1/FOXO1 axis. In vivo, HQFLT inhibited liver metastasis of GC, as evidenced by reduced bioluminescence signals, and counteracted the pro-metastatic effect of PRMT1 expression inducer. CONCLUSIONS: This study elucidated the potential pharmacological basis of HQFLT and suggested that its inhibitory effect on liver metastasis of GC was partially mediated through the PRMT1/FOXO1 axis.

articles.title: Baicalin alleviates Renal interstitial fibrosis by targeting SIRT1/HIF-1α Signaling Pathway.
articles.abstract: UNLABELLED: RENAL INTERSTITIAL FIBROSIS IS A DEFINING FEATURE OF PROGRESSIVE CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE: (CKD) with no effective therapeutic drugs in the clinic. Baicalin (BA) is a natural product sourced from Scutellaria baicalensis and has been proven to treat renal fibrosis and multiple kidney diseases. However, the anti-renal fibrosis effects of BA have not been systematically studied, and its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. AIM OF STUDY: This study aims to investigate the role of BA in renal interstitial fibrosis and its potential pharmacological mechanism. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The model of unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) mouse and TGF-β-induced cells were employed to evaluate the anti-fibrotic effect of baicalin in vivo and in vitro, respectively. The molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) were used to verify the relationship of BA and its specific target, Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1). The gene-knockdown cells, RNA-sequence analysis, western blotting assay, and RT-qPCR analysis were performed to clarify the BA-SIRT1 interaction and explore its underlying pharmacological mechanisms. RESULTS: BA significantly ameliorated renal fibrosis and promoted renal function in UUO mice, with suppressing fibroblast activation in cultured cells. The results of molecular docking, SPR, and CETSA suggested that SIRT1 is a specific target of BA. The anti-fibrotic effects of BA were abolished after SIRT1 was knocked down. The following RNA sequencing and western blotting analysis revealed that BA inhibits the TGF-β1-induced HIF-α signaling pathway via targeting SIRT1. CONCLUSIONS: This study indicated that BA is a SIRT1 agonist in suppressing the HIF-1α signaling pathway to quell renal fibroblast activation and improve renal function in renal interstitial fibrosis.

articles.title: Total polyphenols from Hemerocallis citrina Baroni leaves improve sleep quality in mice with perimenopausal insomnia and are associated with altered expression of 5-HT1AR, ADCY5, PKA, and GABRA2.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Hemerocallis citrina Baroni has a long history of dietary and medicinal use in China. Its dried whole herb is documented as an ethnic medicinal material in the 2003 edition of the Guizhou Provincial Quality Standards for Chinese Medicinal and Ethnic Medicinal Materials, while Hemerocallis flowers are traditionally used for "ye shao an mei" (), referring to reduced or disturbed sleep at night. Modern studies have demonstrated sleep-improving effects of the flowers, and previous work showed neuroprotective and antidepressant-like activities of total polyphenols from Hemerocallis citrina Baroni leaves (HLTP). However, the effects of HLTP on perimenopausal insomnia (PMI) remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate the effects of HLTP on sleep disturbances in mice exhibiting perimenopausal and insomnia-like features and investigate associated molecular changes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: HLTP was prepared using a previously reported procedure. Network pharmacology predicted candidate targets and pathways for 32 phenolic constituents identified in an earlier HLTP batch, while molecular docking assessed predicted binding to 10 core targets selected by protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis. A composite mouse model was generated using 4-vinylcyclohexene dioxide (VCD) to induce perimenopausal features, followed by para-chloro-DL-phenylalanine (PCPA) to induce insomnia-like disturbances. Seventy female C57BL/6J mice were randomized into seven groups (n = 10 per group): Control, Con+HLTP, Model, HLTP-L/M/H (10, 20, and 40 mg/kg, respectively), and zopiclone. Treatment began with model induction. Behavioral tests, pentobarbital-induced sleep testing, 24 h electroencephalographic/electromyographic (EEG/EMG) polysomnography, histopathology, biochemical assays, and Western blotting were used to evaluate pharmacological effects and associated molecular changes. 16S rRNA sequencing, serum untargeted metabolomics, and brain transcriptomics were additionally performed to characterize complementary changes in the gut microbiota, systemic metabolism, and central gene expression. RESULTS: Network pharmacology prioritized the serotonergic synapse pathway for further investigation. HLTP improved behavioral and sleep-related abnormalities, with the most consistent effects at the high dose. EEG/EMG polysomnography showed a partial shift in sleep-wake distribution toward the Control pattern. During the inactive phase, high-dose HLTP shortened non-rapid eye movement (NREM) and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep latencies, reduced Wake bout number and NREM-to-Wake transitions, prolonged NREM bout duration, and increased NREM sleep time (P < 0.05). HLTP also attenuated neuronal morphological abnormalities and improved sex hormone, monoamine neurotransmitter, oxidative stress, and inflammatory indicators. Western blotting showed increased expression of the 5-hydroxytryptamine 1A receptor (5-HT1AR) and gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptor α2 subunit (GABRA2), together with decreased expression of adenylyl cyclase 5 (ADCY5) and protein kinase A (PKA) after HLTP treatment. Multi-omics analyses revealed changes in gut microbial composition, serum metabolism, and brain gene expression following HLTP treatment. Pathway enrichment analysis of exploratory candidate metabolites identified FDR-supported enrichment of steroid biosynthesis. Brain transcriptomics identified FDR-supported enrichment of circadian rhythm in the Model vs. Control comparison and neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction in the HLTP-H vs. Model comparison. None of the tested cross-omics correlations remained significant after FDR correction. CONCLUSIONS: HLTP ameliorated sleep disturbances in mice subjected to the VCD+PCPA composite model, accompanied by improvements in neuroendocrine indicators and changes in 5-HT1AR, ADCY5, PKA, and GABRA2 protein expression. The omics findings provided complementary exploratory evidence, although the functional relationships among these changes remain to be established.

articles.title: Preparation and Pharmacodynamic Evaluation of Cang'erzi San In Situ Temperature-Sensitive Gel for the Treatment of Allergic Rhinitis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Cang'erzi San (CEZS), recorded in the Song dynasty medical text Yan Shi Ji Sheng Fang, has been used for centuries to treat allergic rhinitis (AR). However, its clinical application has been limited due to short residence time at the target site, low bioavailability, and high dosage requirements. AIM OF THE STUDY: To establish a preparation process for CEZS-Gel and optimize its parameters; identify key targets and pathways involved in the anti-allergic rhinitis (AR) effects of CEZS-Gel; and elucidate its pharmacological actions and underlying mechanisms in AR rat models. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Preparation parameters such as drug loading, gelation temperature, and ratios of P407, P188, and extract in CEZS-Gel were optimized using single-factor and Box-Behnken designs. The quality of CEZS-Gel was evaluated by assessing gelation time, pH, mucosal adhesion, swelling ratio, water retention capacity, and in vitro release behavior. Network pharmacology (TCMSP, UniProt, TTD, OMIM) was employed to predict active compounds, targets, and signaling pathways. The therapeutic efficacy of the formulation in an ovalbumin (OVA)-induced AR rat model was assessed through behavioral scoring, histopathology, ELISA, and Western blot analyses. RESULTS: Single-factor screening and Box-Behnken optimization yielded an optimal gel containing 17.68% P407, 1.46% P188, and 48.98% extract, with a gelation temperature of 32-35 °C, suitable mucoadhesion, and 24-h sustained release (cumulative release: chlorogenic acid 96.38%, imperatorin 90.72%). Network pharmacology predicted 76 overlapping targets of CEZS and AR, highlighting the TNF, IL-17, and TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathways. These target- and pathway-level predictions were subsequently validated by the in vivo pharmacodynamic evaluation: in OVA-induced AR rats, CEZS-Gel alleviated nasal symptoms, restored mucosal structure, reduced goblet cell hyperplasia, and lowered serum IgE, IL-4, and TNF-α levels and nasal mucosal TLR4/NF-κB expression (P < 0.05), consistent with the network predictions. CONCLUSION: A P407/P188-based thermosensitive in situ gel loaded with Cang'erzi San extract (CEZS-Gel) was successfully developed as a nasal delivery system for the classical formula. It prolonged nasal residence, enabled 24-h sustained release, and relieved ovalbumin-induced allergic rhinitis, with effects associated with inhibition of the TLR4/NF-κB pathway and Th2-type inflammatory mediators. Through prolonged nasal residence and sustained release, CEZS-Gel improved bioavailability relative to oral administration. To our knowledge, this is the first thermosensitive in situ nasal gel developed from CEZS for the treatment of AR, providing an experimental basis for further mechanistic study and the development of topical delivery systems for classical TCM prescriptions.

articles.title: Role and mechanism of action of PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy in nonylphenol-induced podocyte apoptosis and glomerulonephritis.
articles.abstract: Podocyte injury is an early and critical event in the development of glomerulonephritis (GN). Nonylphenol (NP) can accumulate in the kidney and induce nephrotoxicity. However, the mechanism by which NP promotes GN progression by inducing podocyte apoptosis remains unclear. This study aimed to determine whether NP exposure activated PTEN-induced kinase 1/Parkin RBR E3 ubiquitin protein ligase (PINK1/Parkin)-mediated mitophagy, leading to mitochondrial homeostasis imbalance in podocytes and promoting apoptosis, thereby inducing pathological changes associated with GN in mice. Cell experiments were performed in Mouse Podocyte Clone-5 (MPC-5) cells by activating or inhibiting Parkin. In vivo, 72 male wild-type and Parkin-/- C57BL/6 mice were treated with different doses of NP by gavage for 90 days to investigate the role of Parkin in NP-induced renal injury. The results showed that NP exposure activated the PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy pathway in MPC-5 cells and was accompanied by increased apoptosis and inflammatory responses. Parkin inhibition impaired mitophagy and exacerbated NP-induced cellular injury, whereas Parkin activation enhanced mitophagy and attenuated inflammation and apoptosis, indicating a cytoprotective role of Parkin.
