Consistently, NP exposure for 90 days induced renal dysfunction, podocyte injury, mitochondrial ultrastructural damage, inflammation, apoptosis, and activation of the PINK1/Parkin pathway in mice. These alterations were further aggravated in Parkin-/- mice, which exhibited impaired autophagy and more severe mitochondrial and renal injury. Collectively, Parkin-mediated mitophagy plays a key protective role in maintaining podocyte homeostasis and alleviating glomerular structural and functional damage.

articles.title: Modeling Ethnic Differences via Drug-Predicted Clearance from Chemical Structures.
articles.abstract: Ethnic differences in pharmacokinetics can result in clinically relevant differences in drug efficacy and safety, even when identical doses are administered. Although mechanistic approaches such as physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling can be used to evaluate population-specific pharmacokinetics, there remains a need for complementary screening approaches that can assess ethnic difference risk at very early stages of drug discovery with limited experimental information. The aim of this study was to develop a machine-learning-based approach to assess the risk of ethnic differences in oral clearance between Japanese and Western populations by integrating chemical structural features with in silico-predicted pharmacokinetic (PK) parameters. The models incorporating extended-connectivity fingerprints (ECFPs) and 17 DruMAP-derived PK parameters demonstrated improved predictive performance compared with the models using structural information alone, achieving a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve of 0.811 vs, 0.701 for the ECFP-only model. Model interpretation using SHapley Additive exPlanations indicated that biologically plausible factors, including the unbound fraction in the plasma and the predicted contributions of specific cytochrome P450 enzymes, were important contributors to the classification. External validation using an independent set of compounds (n = 21) achieved a recall of 75% for compounds exhibiting ethnic differences, thereby supporting the feasibility of the proposed approach. These results suggest that integrating chemical structural information with DruMAP-derived PK properties enables the early-stage assessment of ethnic differences in risk without relying on clinical pharmacokinetic data. The proposed framework may support rational decision-making for bridging strategies and efficient design of multiregional clinical trials in international drug development.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetic investigation of TRPA1 receptor antagonists: A967079 and HC-030031 in mouse model.
articles.abstract: Our investigation aimed to delineate the pharmacokinetic parameters of the most commonly used TRPA1 receptor antagonists, A967079 and HC-030031, concerning their drug-likeness and penetration into the central nervous system (CNS). Both substances were tested at two different dosages and two different formulations using the intraperitoneal and subcutaneous routes of administration. We determined the drug-like properties of the substances using several different models. Our findings demonstrate that both substances are able to pass the blood-brain barrier and remain in the CNS for a relatively long period when administered via the appropriate mode and formulation. In the case of A967079, effective concentrations can not only be achieved but also maintained for hours in both plasma and brain tissue. In the case of HC-030031, a shorter residence time and less favourable kinetics are observed. During the study, elimination half-lives were determined separately for plasma and brain tissue, and the brain-to-plasma distribution ratio was calculated. In addition to elimination kinetics, the temporal distribution of the compounds in the liver and kidney was also assessed. Overall, these results provide important pharmacokinetic insights that may facilitate further investigation of TRPA1 ion channel inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: Novel Benzimidazol-2-Acetamide Derivatives as Submicromolar Casein Kinase 1δ Inhibitors with Favourable Predicted Drug-like Properties.
articles.abstract: Background/Objective: Casein kinase 1δ (CK1δ) plays a central role in regulating circadian rhythms, DNA repair, apoptosis, and cell proliferation, and its dysregulation is associated with both cancer and neurodegenerative diseases, making CK1δ an attractive therapeutic target. This study aimed to develop novel CK1δ inhibitors with favourable drug-like properties through the synthesis and biological evaluation of benzimidazol-2-acetamide derivatives. Methods: A novel series of benzimidazol-2-acetamide derivatives was synthesized, incorporating different substituents on the benzimidazole core (5-chloro, 5,6-dichloro, 5-nitro, and 5-cyano) and various saturated cyclic amines on the acetamide moiety. Compounds were evaluated for CK1δ inhibitory activity, while molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were performed to investigate their binding mode. In silico ADME predictions assessed pharmacokinetic properties, and cytotoxicity was evaluated in SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells. Results: The 5,6-dichloro derivatives 20 and 24, bearing piperidin-4-ylmethanamine and morpholine moieties, respectively, displayed the highest CK1δ inhibitory activity (IC50 = 0.172 and 0.223 μM). The 5-cyano analogue 22 also exhibited a good potency (IC50 = 0.224 μM). Computational studies confirmed an ATP-competitive binding mode and highlighted the dynamic behaviour of the solvent-exposed substituents within the CK1δ binding site. Predicted pharmacokinetic properties suggested favourable oral absorption and blood-brain barrier penetration. Compounds 20, 22, and 24 showed no cytotoxicity in SH-SY5Y cells at concentrations up to 10 μM. Conclusions: The new benzimidazol-2-acetamide derivatives exhibited good inhibitor activity against CK1δ, favourable predicted ADME properties, and low cellular toxicity. The combined experimental and computational findings provide valuable insights for the further optimization of this scaffold toward the development of therapeutics for CK1δ-related diseases.

articles.title: Nelfinavir Synergizes with Cisplatin and Promotes GSDME-Associated Lytic Cell Death in Platinum-Resistant Ovarian Cancer Cells.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Platinum resistance limits the efficacy of ovarian cancer treatment and arises through multiple mechanisms, including enhanced DNA repair, activation of stress responses, and increased survival signaling. Nelfinavir (NFV), an HIV protease inhibitor with reported anti-tumor activity, is a candidate for drug repurposing, but its interaction with cisplatin (CDDP) in ovarian cancer has not been established. Here, we investigated whether NFV enhances CDDP cytotoxicity in platinum (Pt)-resistant ovarian cancer cells and characterized the associated cell death response. Methods: Drug interaction was assessed using cell vitality and viability assays and Loewe additivity modeling together with Bliss and ZIP analyses. Cell death was characterized by Annexin V/7-AAD staining, mitochondrial membrane potential analysis, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release, immunoblotting, pharmacological caspase inhibition, and bulk mRNA sequencing with differential expression and gene set enrichment analyses. Results: NFV synergistically enhanced CDDP cytotoxicity across three Pt-resistant ovarian cancer cell lines, reducing CDDP IC50 values by 4.2-5.8-fold and producing mean Loewe synergy scores of approximately 25-30. Combination treatment increased LDH release and was accompanied by caspase-8, caspase-3, PARP, and the pore-forming death effector gasdermin E (GSDME) cleavage. Caspase inhibition attenuated viability loss and GSDME processing. Transcriptomic analysis identified enrichment of stress- and death-associated programs, including the unfolded protein response (UPR), apoptosis, reactive oxygen species (ROS)-associated signaling, and TNF/NF-κB signaling. Conclusions: Together, these findings demonstrate a reproducible synergistic interaction between CDDP and NFV in Pt-resistant ovarian cancer cells and characterize an associated lytic cell death phenotype involving apoptotic signaling and accompanied by GSDME processing. These findings support further investigation of NFV as a repurposed combination partner to enhance CDDP cytotoxicity in Pt-resistant ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Computational Assessment of CKP-25 Binding at Receptor-Recognition Interfaces Across Diverse Human Coronaviruses.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The continued emergence of novel coronaviruses motivates the search for small molecules that bind conserved features of the spike receptor-recognition interface across diverse species. CKP-25 was recently reported as a small-molecule inhibitor of the SARS-CoV-2 spike receptor-binding domain. This study aimed to assess computationally whether CKP-25 can maintain stable binding at receptor-recognition interfaces across phylogenetically diverse human coronaviruses. Methods: CKP-25 was docked to the spike receptor-binding regions of Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV), severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 1 (SARS-CoV-1), and human coronaviruses NL63, 229E, and HKU1 (HCoV-NL63, HCoV-229E, and HCoV-HKU1). SARS-CoV-2 (PDB 6M0J), for which CKP-25 has documented antiviral activity, was processed identically and included as an experimentally validated reference system. Each selected complex was subjected to three independent 100 ns all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations initialized with different random velocities. Binding stability was evaluated using protein and ligand root-mean-square deviation (RMSD), residue flexibility, radius of gyration, protein-ligand contact persistence, polar interactions, and Molecular Mechanics-Generalized Born Surface Area (MM-GBSA) calculations. Results: CKP-25 was retained at the targeted receptor-recognition interface in all three replicates for four of the five test targets-MERS-CoV, HCoV-NL63, SARS-CoV-1, and HCoV-HKU1-each of which reproducibly engaged the same aromatic and hydrophobic anchor residues in every independent run. HCoV-229E was the sole exception, the ligand relocating from its docked site in two of three replicates. Ligand RMSD plateaus were generally low, mostly below 2.0 Å. Contact analyses indicated a shared dependence on shape-complementary van der Waals packing involving hydrophobic and aromatic residues, including tyrosine- and tryptophan-rich anchoring environments. MM-GBSA estimates, averaged across replicates, ranged from -24.28 to -34.57 kcal/mol. No test target differed from the SARS-CoV-2 reference (-29.15±3.46 kcal/mol) by more than the replicate-to-replicate spread, with MERS-CoV and HCoV-NL63 giving the most favorable means. Conclusions: CKP-25 remained at the receptor-recognition interface of four of the five human coronaviruses tested, and it did so in all three replicates. In the SARS-CoV-2 control, the same pipeline independently reproduced the experimentally established binding mode, which supports the reliability of these predictions. HCoV-229E was the exception: the ligand left the docked site in two of the three replicates, and no contact was reproducible across all three repetitions. Experimental binding measurements and cell-based entry assays are required to test these predictions.

articles.title: Effect of Probiotics on Stress Scores, Cortisol Levels, and Immune Functions in Moderately Stressed Adolescents and Young Adults: Results of a Feasibility Clinical Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Stress can negatively affect immune system functions by regulating cytokine production. The purpose of this feasibility study was to investigate the effects of a probiotic supplement on stress, cortisol levels, and the immune functions of moderately stressed adolescents and young adults. Methods: A randomized, single-blind clinical trial was conducted at Primary Children's Hospital, Utah. Eighty-seven moderately stressed (Perceived Stress Score, PSS, 14-26) volunteers (12-20 years old) completed the study. Participants took either a probiotic blend containing three Lactobacillaceae strains or placebo capsules for 12 weeks. Participants' PSSs were evaluated following office visits at baseline, and after 8 and 12 weeks of supplementation. Participants' collected salivary samples were analyzed for cortisol, secretory IgA, and a panel of cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α, and IL-10). Results: Both cohorts showed decreases in PSS and increases in morning salivary cortisol levels; the difference between cohorts was not statistically significant. Probiotics slowed the increase in cortisol levels and had a beneficial effect on cytokine production, with a statistically significant reduction in IL-1β levels compared to placebo (p = 0.03-0.004). A statistically significant, weak positive correlation between cortisol levels and IL-1β (r = 0.16, p = 0.015) has been observed. Conclusions: This study's results suggest that probiotic supplementation may influence cortisol dynamics and cytokine responses in moderately stressed adolescents and young adults, with IL-1β showing the most consistent between-cohort difference. These findings support further investigation of probiotic supplementation in more rigorously designed trials that account for the types of stress experienced by participants in early life and during the study.

articles.title: Folic Acid-Functionalized Chitosan-Coated Oleosomes Engineered for Enhanced Anti-Arthritic Delivery of Syzygium cumini Seed Extract.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of folic acid-functionalized chitosan-coated oleosomes (F-CS-OL) loaded with Syzygium cumini (SYG) seed extract against rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in a complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA)-induced arthritis rat model. Methods: Rats received treatments via the oral route for 11 days following arthritis induction. The colloidal formulation exhibited an average particle size of 80.78 ± 1.02 nm, a zeta potential of -15.5 ± 1.12 mV, and an encapsulation efficiency (EE) of 94.98 ± 0.56%, alongside characterization by TEM, FTIR, and DSC. CFA-induced arthritis produced a pronounced inflammatory and angiogenic response, marked by significantly elevated serum levels of TNF-α, IL-6, CRP, VEGF, ICAM-1, MMP-3, and CXCL13 compared with the normal control group. Results: While treatment with free SYG extract resulted in moderate reductions in these biomarkers, the nanoencapsulated extract (SYG-loaded F-CS-OL) produced significantly greater reductions in inflammatory, chemotactic, matrix-remodeling, and angiogenesis-associated biomarkers compared with the untreated CFA-induced arthritis group. Histopathological examination of joint tissues further supported the biochemical findings. Conclusions: Overall, SYG-loaded F-CS-OL exhibited potent anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory activities and significantly reduced biomarkers associated with angiogenic signaling in CFA-induced arthritis in CFA-induced arthritis. These findings suggest that folic acid-functionalized nanocarriers may represent a promising strategy for enhancing the therapeutic potential of SYG; however, further pharmacokinetic and safety studies are warranted to support clinical translation.

articles.title: Comparative Phytochemical and Biological Evaluation of Walnut Septum and Pellicle Extracts in Chemical, Computational, and Cell-Based Models.
articles.abstract: Background: Walnut (Juglans regia L.) processing generates polyphenol-rich by-products, including the septum (WS) and pellicle (WP). This study comparatively characterized the phytochemical composition of WS and WP from Romania and investigated their antioxidant and preliminary immunomodulatory properties using chemical, computational, and cell-based approaches. Methods: Extracts were characterized by targeted LC-QTOF-MS/MS, and antioxidant capacity was evaluated using ABTS, DPPH, and FRAP assays. Major phenolic compounds were docked against Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (KEAP1), followed by 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations. Cytocompatibility was evaluated in Caco-2, Jurkat, and THP-1 cells, and cellular antioxidant activity was assessed in H2O2-stimulated Caco-2 cells using the DCFH-DA assay. Immunomodulatory potential was investigated following lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation of the same cell lines. Results: WSLE contained 25 quantified compounds, with ellagic acid, catechin, procyanidins, and quercitrin among the major quantified constituents, whereas WP contained 13, with higher ellagic acid, gallic acid, and castalagin levels. WPE showed greater cell-free antioxidant capacity, while both extracts attenuated the H2O2-induced increase in intracellular DCF fluorescence in Caco-2 cells. Simulations suggested favorable KEAP1 interactions, with quercitrin and catechin predicted to form the most stable complexes. LPS induced an insufficient cytokine response in Caco-2 and Jurkat cells. In THP-1 cells, IL-8 was the only responsive marker, and both extracts reduced its LPS-induced secretion. Conclusions: The extracts showed distinct polyphenolic profiles and redox-related cellular activity. Their effects on IL-8 secretion in THP-1 cells and predicted KEAP1 binding are preliminary and hypothesis-generating; Nrf2 activation was not measured, and validation in physiologically relevant in vivo and clinical models is required to establish the biological relevance and potential applications of these extracts.

articles.title: From Design to Synergy: Triazine-Triazole Hybrids as Anti-Breast Cancer Leads Targeting Survival and Invasion Pathways for Augmenting Lapatinib Efficacy.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Breast cancer is the most common cancer diagnosed and the leading cause of cancer-related deaths among women, ranking fourth overall in both sexes. Its treatment is difficult due to drug resistance and side effects from conventional therapies. Developing multitargeted agents and combination approaches offer a promising way to overcome these challenges. This study details the design and testing of new triazole-triazine hybrids as potential anti-breast cancer drugs, exploring their use in combination with lapatinib to enhance its efficacy in breast cancer. Methods: Sixteen triazine-triazole hybrid compounds with amide and ureido linkers were synthesized via click and coupling protocols and tested for their cytotoxic effects on MCF-7 cells using an MTT assay. The most effective compound was evaluated for its inhibitory effect against AXL using an ADP-Glo™ kinase assay, then examined in combination with lapatinib on cellular and molecular levels. In vitro experiments included chemoinvasion assays for metastasis, flow-cytometric analysis of apoptosis, and ELISA to evaluate the molecular mechanisms of promising hits. Molecular docking studies were conducted to simulate the potential target-hit interactions and predict the plausible structural determinants of activity, paving the way for further lead optimization. Results: Compound 6e demonstrated the highest activity (IC50 = 24.58 μM) and good selectivity (SI = 7.87). The combination therapy showed a synergistic effect and increased tumor sensitivity to lapatinib. Biological tests indicated inhibition of the AXL enzyme, downregulation of key pathways (AKT, NF-κB, STAT3, ERK), decreased levels of VEGF, MMP9, and cyclin D1, and increased caspase-3 activity, suggesting apoptosis, which was strengthened by the flow-cytometric analysis findings. Docking results supported multitarget interactions. Conclusions: Compound 6e is a promising multitarget anti-breast cancer candidate with synergistic potential in combination with lapatinib, warranting further in vivo studies.

articles.title: Detachable Modular Blood-Brain Barrier-on-a-Chip with a Concentration Gradient Generator for Stepwise Inflammation Modeling and Drug Evaluation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) is compromised in many neurological disorders, yet in vitro models rarely reproduce graded inflammatory stimulation of brain endothelial cells in vivo. This study developed a detachable, modular BBB-on-a-chip for stepwise inflammation modeling with multi-marker readout, and compared the anti-inflammatory efficacy of quercetin (QUER) and kaempferol (KAE). Methods: The chip combines a Christmas-tree concentration gradient generator with a four-channel culture module, fabricated separately and assembled on demand for stepwise seeding, exposure, dosing, and sampling. hCMEC/D3 cells were exposed to a TNF-α gradient (0-30 ng/mL); extracellular ATP, ROS, NO, cytokines, ZO-1, and ICAM-1 were monitored over 48 h. Transcriptomics and network pharmacology were integrated with molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations; QUER and KAE were administered gradient-wise (0-20 μM), with dexamethasone as a control. Results: The TNF-α gradient induced time- and concentration-dependent injury, with ATP and IL-8 responding at 8 h, ROS and NO at 12 h, and IL-1β, IL-6, and tight-junction impairment later, yielding spatiotemporally resolved readouts across four parallel channels. Ten hub inflammatory genes, including ICAM1, were identified, and network pharmacology nominated QUER. QUER was predicted to bind ICAM-1 more strongly than KAE, its structural analog differing by one B-ring hydroxyl group; gradient administration confirmed QUER suppressed ICAM-1 expression and inflammatory mediator release at lower concentrations. Conclusions: The detachable modular design makes multi-step inflammation modeling and gradient-based anti-inflammatory evaluation convenient on a single chip; QUER's consistent advantage over KAE across binding calculations and functional assays supports a structure-activity relationship consistent with ICAM-1 engagement.

articles.title: Niosomal Mexiletine Attenuates Rotenone-Induced Parkinsonism via Modulation of the circDLGAP4/miR-134-5p/p-CREB Axis and Restoration of Mitochondrial-Autophagic Homeostasis.
articles.abstract: Background: Parkinson's disease (PD) is distinguished by progressive dopaminergic degeneration driven by the convergence of oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired autophagy. Mexiletine (Mexil), which has demonstrated antioxidant properties, has not been systematically investigated yet for its potential to mitigate mitochondrial-dysfunction-related neurodegeneration in PD. Using an integrated computational and experimental approach, we characterized, for the first time, the neuroprotective mechanisms of Mexil's action against rotenone (Rot)-induced Parkinsonism and employed niosomes as a nanocarrier platform to enhance mexil delivery and augment its neuroprotective potential in a Parkinson's disease model. Methods: Molecular docking identified candidate molecular targets underlying niosomal Mexil's neuroprotective potential. Sprague-Dawley male rats were assigned to control, Rot, and Rot plus niosomal Mexil (30 and 50 mg/kg) groups. Motor performance was evaluated, while dopaminergic degeneration, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and autophagy were assessed biochemically, histopathologically, and immunohistochemically. Results: Docking revealed promising interactions between Mexil and both phosphorylated cAMP response element-binding protein (p-CREB) and alpha-synuclein, with binding scores of -5.2 and -4.9 kcal/mol, respectively. Niosomal Mexil improved motor function, restored dopamine and tyrosine hydroxylase levels, and curtailed alpha-synuclein accumulation. Most notably, niosomal Mexil engaged a previously unexplored circular RNA DLGAP4/microRNA-134-5p/p-CREB axis, promoted mitochondrial biogenesis via the phosphorylated AMP-activated protein kinase (p-AMPK)/peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha (PGC-1α)/sirtuin-1 (SIRT-1) pathway, and rebalanced mitochondrial dynamics. These changes were accompanied by restored autophagic axis and suppressed oxidative stress and inflammation. Conclusions: Niosomal Mexil confers neuroprotection against Rot-induced Parkinsonism by orchestrating oxidative, mitochondrial, autophagic, and inflammatory pathways, positioning it as a mechanistically novel disease-modifying candidate warranting further preclinical evaluation in PD.

articles.title: Codeine and Testosterone Concentration Patterns During Co-Administration of Codeine and Testosterone Undecanoate in Male Wistar Rats.
articles.abstract: Background: Three widely separated sampling days cannot establish conventional pharmacokinetic parameters. We therefore examined exploratory whole-blood codeine and plasma total-testosterone concentration patterns during co-administration of codeine and testosterone undecanoate in male Wistar rats. Methods: Thirty-two rats were allocated to saline (S), codeine (C), testosterone undecanoate (T), or combined codeine plus testosterone undecanoate (CT) groups (eight animals per group). Codeine (10 mg/kg by oral gavage) was administered once daily from Day 0 through Day 5 (six total doses) and testosterone undecanoate (100 mg/kg intramuscularly) on Day 3. On Day 0, whole blood was collected two hours after codeine administration; therefore, Day 0 was a post-dose sampling point rather than a pre-dose baseline. No codeine was administered on Day 6; the Day 6 sample was collected after completion of the six-dose treatment schedule. Codeine dose volumes were adjusted according to each rat's baseline body weight. Measurements unavailable because of insufficient sample volume were treated as missing without imputation. Codeine was quantified only in C and CT; the corresponding model therefore estimated the association of adding testosterone undecanoate among codeine-treated animals rather than a full factorial drug-drug interaction. Results: All 14 available Day 0 samples had instrument-reported whole-blood codeine concentrations (range, 0.339-4.705 ng/mL), consistent with their post-dose status. The C-versus-CT group-by-day test using all instrument-reported values yielded Wald chi-square = 8.487 (df = 2, p = 0.014). With the verified LOQ of 0.25 ng/mL, only CT7 Day 14 (0.08 ng/mL) was below the LOQ while remaining above the LOD of 0.07 ng/mL; excluding this observation yielded Wald chi-square = 7.856 (df = 2, p = 0.020). Plasma testosterone availability varied by group and day (n = 3-8); the raw-scale group-by-day test was p = 0.0076, whereas the log-scale sensitivity test was p = 0.052. Conclusions: The observed numerical patterns are exploratory. Sparse sampling, one below-LOQ codeine value, an influential CT7 observation, unequal plasma-testosterone availability, and sensitivity to analytical and modeling choices prevent causal, pharmacokinetic, metabolic, endocrine-mechanistic, or clinical conclusions.

articles.title: Design, Synthesis, and Evaluation of Novel Adenine-Based Hydrazones as Potential Anticancer Agents: Cytotoxicity Against A549 and MRC-5 Cell Lines with In Silico Insights.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Lung cancer remains a leading cause of global cancer-related mortality, necessitating the development of new therapeutic candidates. In this study, we aimed to design, synthesize, and biologically evaluate novel adenine-based hydrazone derivatives as potential anticancer candidates. Methods: A series of novel adenine-hydrazones were synthesized via the condensation of 2-(6-amino-9H-purin-9-yl)acetohydrazide with various aldehydes and isatin derivatives. Their antiproliferative activities against human lung adenocarcinoma (A549) and normal lung fibroblast (MRC-5) cell lines were evaluated using the MTT assay. Mechanistic investigations-including cell membrane damage (LDH release), oxidative stress (TOS, iROS), mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP, ΔΨm), cell cycle distribution, and apoptosis (Annexin V/PI)-were conducted for the lead derivatives, complemented by multi-target in silico molecular docking against PLK1, TrxR1, and MDM2. Results: Compounds 3d, 3c, and 4j showed the strongest antiproliferative activity within the synthesized series against A549 cells, with IC50 values of 37.2 ± 1.8 µM, 41.8 ± 1.9 µM, and 42.9 ± 1.7 µM, respectively, together with comparatively more favorable A549/MRC-5 activity profiles than several other derivatives. These compounds induced oxidative stress-associated cellular injury, accompanied by mitochondrial depolarization, G2/M phase accumulation, and Annexin V-confirmed apoptotic cell death. Complementary multi-target in silico molecular docking provided theoretical insights into potential binding interactions with PLK1, TrxR1, and MDM2. Conclusions: Adenine-hydrazone hybrids, particularly 5-halogenated isatin derivatives such as compound 3d, provide preliminary lead scaffolds with moderate in vitro cytotoxicity against lung cancer cells, serving as a platform for future structural optimization to enhance potency and selectivity.

articles.title: A Pathway-Driven Computational Drug Discovery Framework Integrating Machine Learning and Virtual Screening for Identification of Anti-Rheumatoid Arthritis Natural Small Molecules.
articles.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to establish a pathway-driven computational drug discovery framework integrating machine learning, target prioritization, virtual screening, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and in vitro evaluation to identify natural small molecules with potential anti-rheumatoid arthritis (RA) activity. Methods: Sixteen RA-related Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets were included, with 15 cohorts used for model development and one reserved for independent external validation. Pathway features quantified by gene set variation analysis (GSVA) were subjected to cohort-aware feature selection using a leave-one-dataset-out framework across seven machine-learning algorithms. Predictive modeling and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis were subsequently performed, followed by random-effects meta-analysis (REMA) and network analysis for candidate-target prioritization. Natural compounds were screened by molecular docking and further evaluated using ligand efficiency, multiple scoring approaches, explicit-membrane MD simulations, and a TNF-α-induced MH7A inflammatory model. Results: Ten stable RA-associated pathways were identified. The final CAT+ET model achieved ROC-AUCs of 0.783 (95% CI, 0.731-0.836) and 0.610 (95% CI, 0.496-0.720) in the internal and independent external validation sets, respectively, indicating limited cross-cohort generalizability. SHAP and cross-cohort analyses supported Complement and coagulation cascades for downstream investigation, and integrated expression and network evidence prioritized C3AR1 as a candidate target. Virtual screening identified four candidate natural compounds (SM1-SM4). Ligand-size analysis, ligand efficiency, multiple scoring approaches, and explicit-membrane MD simulations provided complementary structural and energetic assessments of these candidates. Among them, SM1 showed comparatively favorable computational characteristics and a relatively consistent reduction in the inflammatory markers IL6 and MMP3 in TNF-α-stimulated MH7A cells, accompanied by changes in C3AR1 expression. These convergent computational and experimental findings supported the prioritization of SM1 for further investigation. Conclusions: This study established a pathway-driven framework linking cross-cohort pathway identification with candidate-target prioritization and natural-product screening in RA. Complement and coagulation cascades and C3AR1 were prioritized for downstream investigation, while integrated computational and experimental evidence identified SM1 as a candidate with promising anti-inflammatory potential. Although direct compound-C3AR1 engagement and its functional involvement require further validation, the present study provides a systematic and extensible strategy for translating robust RA-associated pathway signals into candidate targets and natural compounds, offering a valuable foundation for subsequent natural-product drug discovery in RA.

articles.title: Cryptococcosis After Initiation of Janus Kinase Inhibitors or Biologic DMARDs in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Three Pairwise Active-Comparator Analyses of Propensity Score-Matched TriNetX Cohorts, 2005-2025.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Comparative safety evidence for cryptococcosis during advanced rheumatoid arthritis (RA) therapy is limited. We compared newly recorded cryptococcosis after initiation of Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi), tumor necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitors (TNFi), and non-TNF biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (non-TNF bDMARDs). Methods: Three retrospective active-comparator analyses were conducted in the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network: JAKi versus TNFi, JAKi versus non-TNF bDMARDs, and TNFi versus non-TNF bDMARDs. After 1:1 propensity score matching, outcomes from day 1 to 10 years after initiation, capped at 30 June 2025, were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models. E-values assessed sensitivity to unmeasured confounding. Results: Matched cohorts included 27,833, 32,440, and 37,351 patients per group, respectively; all absolute standardized mean differences were <0.10. Events occurred in 20 JAKi and 12 TNFi initiators (hazard ratio [HR], 2.20; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.06-4.54) and in 22 JAKi and 13 non-TNF bDMARD initiators (HR, 2.15; 95% CI, 1.07-4.31). In the secondary comparison, 17 TNFi and 19 non-TNF bDMARD initiators had events (HR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.43-1.60). Point-estimate E-values for the JAKi comparisons were 3.82 and 3.72; CI-limit E-values were 1.31 and 1.34. Conclusions: JAKi initiation was associated with an approximately twofold higher hazard of newly recorded cryptococcosis than either biologic comparator, while estimated 10-year cumulative event probabilities were below 0.2% in all groups. The separately selected and matched populations do not support an indirect ranking of treatment classes. Low event counts, wide CIs, possible outcome misclassification, fixed exposure classification, and residual confounding preclude causal conclusions. The findings require independent confirmation.

articles.title: Dose-Related Effects of Cannabidiol on Inflammatory and Redox Responses, Bacterial Dissemination, and Multiorgan Injury in CLP-Induced Septic Rats.
articles.abstract: Background: Sepsis couples dysregulated inflammation, oxidative imbalance, microbial dissemination, and multiorgan injury. Cannabidiol (CBD) has anti-inflammatory and redox-modulating properties, but its dose-related effects in polymicrobial sepsis, particularly alongside culture-recoverable bacterial burden, remain incompletely characterized. Methods: Forty-eight male Wistar rats were randomized to Control, Sham, Untreated CLP, or CLP plus CBD at 2.5, 5, or 25 mg/kg (n = 8/group). CBD or vehicle was administered intraperitoneally after cecal ligation and puncture (CLP). Inflammatory, immunometabolic, neurotrophic, oxidative, biochemical, microbiological, and histopathological outcomes were evaluated at 10 h. Results: Untreated CLP increased pro-inflammatory cytokines, asprosin, resistin, oxidative-stress indices, organ-injury biomarkers, and reported culture-recoverable bacterial burdens, while decreasing IL-10, apelin, BDNF, TAS, and immunoreactive SOD, CAT, and GPx concentrations (all omnibus p < 0.001). CBD was associated with progressive improvement across most systemic outcomes, and 25 mg/kg produced the most consistent overall response. Histopathological lesion scores were greatest in Untreated CLP animals and generally lower in CBD-treated groups; however, tissue-level changes were not uniformly dose-ordered across every organ and lesion domain. Conclusions: Within this acute exploratory model, CBD exposure was associated with coordinated improvements across host-response, redox, biochemical, and morphological domains. The microbial summaries suggested lower recoverable burdens, but require animal-level verification of non-detect handling. These findings support pharmacokinetic, safety, mechanistic, survival, and prospectively powered confirmatory studies; they do not establish direct antibacterial activity or a clinically applicable dose.

articles.title: A Practical Roadmap for Implementing the LC-MS-Based Multi-Attribute Method for Analysis of Therapeutic Proteins.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The mass spectrometry-based multi-attribute method (MAM) enables site-specific monitoring of multiple product quality attributes (PQAs) within a single LC-MS peptide mapping assay and is increasingly being adopted in biopharmaceutical development and quality control (QC). However, its analytical and operational complexities necessitate a structured approach to method development, qualification, system readiness, and assay transfer. This study presents a practical roadmap for implementing LC-MS-based MAM, aligned with USP-NF General Chapter ⟨1060⟩. Methods: Sample preparation and LC-MS acquisition parameters were optimized to minimize analytical artifacts and support robust workflow performance. System readiness was established using a publicly available monoclonal antibody reference standard. Adalimumab and etanercept were then used as representative biotherapeutics to evaluate key elements of MAM implementation, including qualification and interlaboratory transfer. Results: The refined workflow provided consistent digestion performance, chromatographic stability, mass accuracy, and reliable data processing across both molecules. Qualification studies demonstrated acceptable specificity, precision, sensitivity, and quantitative performance for targeted PQA monitoring, while new peak detection (NPD) assessments supported the detection of emerging or changing species. Interlaboratory transfer studies demonstrated successful transfer of the standardized workflow across laboratories and LC-MS platforms. Conclusions: These results establish a technical and operational foundation for MAM implementation, including system readiness, qualification, and assay transfer. The proposed implementation framework provides a robust and broadly applicable roadmap for MAM deployment across diverse biopharmaceutical programs while supporting subsequent product-specific refinement and validation for routine QC applications.

articles.title: sDR5-Fc Administered Post-Exposure Alleviates Radiation-Induced Enteric Injury by Inhibiting ROS and NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD-Dependent Pyroptosis and Inflammatory Response.
articles.abstract: Background: The risk of ionizing radiation exposure, including accidents and medical complications, has increased with the rapid development and broad application of nuclear technology. The intestine is highly susceptible to radiation, with radiation-induced intestinal injury characterized by a complex cascade of cellular and molecular reactions. This cascade results in the death of intestinal epithelial cells, which compromises the integrity of the intestinal mucosal barrier and disrupts immune regulation. At present, there are several limitations in the research on the therapy of radiation-induced intestinal injury, including uncertain mechanisms and an absence of optimal pharmaceuticals. This study aims to explore the post-exposure treatment effects of sDR5-Fc (a DR5 antagonist) on radiation-induced intestinal pyroptosis damage. Methods: In this study, C57BL/6 mice, human HIEC-6, and rat IEC-6 intestinal epithelial cells were exposed to a single 15 Gy high-dose γ-irradiation to establish an acute radiation-induced intestinal injury model. All sDR5-Fc treatments were administered after radiation exposure to simulate clinical post-exposure intervention. In vivo histological staining was performed for quantitative evaluation of intestinal damage. In vitro cell viability and LDH release assays were used to evaluate intestinal epithelial injury. Multiple detection methods, including scanning electron microscopy (SEM), flow cytometry, peripheral blood routine analysis, organ index detection, immunohistochemistry, qRT-PCR, and Western blotting, were applied to assess radiation-induced alterations in oxidative stress (ROS, MDA) and pyroptosis-associated inflammasome indicators (NLRP3, caspase-1, GSDMD-N, IL-1β, IL-18). Results: It was observed that treatment with soluble DR5-Fc fusion protein (sDR5-Fc), a DR5 antagonist, markedly reduced these radiation-induced effects. Mice subjected to 15 Gy total abdominal γ-irradiation exhibited similar outcomes after sDR5-Fc administration, including inhibited pyroptosis in intestinal and colonic tissues, enhanced recovery of peripheral blood cells (leukocytes, erythrocytes, and platelets), improved organ indices of the spleen and thymus, and an increased 30-day survival rate. Histological examination and pathological scoring confirmed significant structural damage in the irradiated group, and these pathological alterations were partially reversed following sDR5-Fc administration. Molecular docking and BLI assays suggest a potential in vitro interaction between DR5 and NLRP3, which can be interfered with by sDR5-Fc. Moreover, qRT-PCR and Western blotting assays indicated that sDR5-Fc attenuated pyroptosis by reducing the NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD signaling pathway. Conclusions: These findings suggest that sDR5-Fc, as a DR5 antagonist, is a promising therapeutic candidate for mitigating high-dose radiation-induced intestinal injury; however, further research is warranted.

articles.title: Antimicrobial, Anti-Inflammatory, General Toxicity and Antioxidant Activities of Ultrasound-Assisted Extracts from Prunella vulgaris L.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study compared five ultrasound-assisted extracts of Prunella vulgaris L. prepared with water or aqueous ethanol (30%, 50%, 70%, and 96%) and evaluated their phytochemical composition and preliminary antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, brine-shrimp lethality, and antioxidant properties. Methods: Gallic acid and rosmarinic acid were quantified in all five extracts by a validated HPLC-UV method, with LC-ESI-MS used to support compound identification. Antimicrobial activity was evaluated by broth serial dilution and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) determination. Anti-inflammatory activity was assessed in a carrageenan-induced rat paw edema model. General toxicity screening was performed using the Artemia salina lethality assay. Antioxidant activity was evaluated by a ferricyanide reducing-power assay and the DPPH radical-scavenging assay. Results: Rosmarinic acid was detected in all extracts and was most abundant in PV70 (7.6%). PV70 showed MIC values of 12.5 μg/mL against Staphylococcus aureus and Bacillus subtilis. In the carrageenan model, PV70 produced 76.8% inhibition of paw-weight gain at 25 mg/kg, whereas diclofenac produced 66.6% inhibition at 10 mg/kg; this numerical comparison was descriptive and was not interpreted as evidence of superiority. The tested extracts caused low mortality of Artemia salina under the experimental conditions. Conclusions: The findings identify PV70 as a chemically distinct extract with notable activity in the screening models used. Because the extracts are multicomponent mixtures and mechanistic biomarkers were not measured, the observed biological effects cannot be attributed to rosmarinic acid alone. Further work is required to confirm mechanisms, safety, standardization, and efficacy.

articles.title: Synthesis, Biological Evaluation, and Molecular Dynamics Studies of Novel 1,2,4-Triazole-Functionalized Benzene-Sulfonate Derivatives as Potential Enzyme Inhibitors and Cytotoxicity in HepG2 Cells.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: In this study, novel benzenesulfonate derivatives containing a 1,2,4-triazole ring were synthesized. Methods: Their molecular structures were characterized by IR, 1H NMR, and 13C NMR spectroscopy, together with Q-TOF LC/MS analyses. For compounds 5b and 5d, the available mass spectrometric data were not used for structural confirmation, and their structural assignments were based primarily on the spectroscopic data. The inhibitory effects of the synthesized compounds (3-5) against acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and glutathione S-transferase (GST) enzymes were evaluated. Results: Comparison of the results with the reference inhibitors, donepezil and ethacrynic acid, showed that compound 3e exhibited the highest AChE inhibitory activity among the tested compounds, with an IC50 value of 1.60 ± 0.198 μM. In addition, compound 4a showed remarkable GST inhibitory activity, with an IC50 value of 1.95 ± 0.492 μM, demonstrating greater potency than the reference inhibitor. The cytotoxic effects of the selected compounds were further assessed against the HepG2 cell line after 24 and 48 h of treatment. Overall, the synthesized molecules exhibited potent enzyme inhibitory activities together with promising cytotoxic effects, highlighting their potential as lead candidates for further biological investigations. In silico analyses were performed to elucidate the molecular basis of the experimentally observed acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitory activity of the synthesized derivatives. Molecular docking against human AChE (PDB ID: 4EY7) identified compound 3e as the most favorable binder among the synthesized series, while 3f also exhibited a strong binding profile. Subsequent 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations of the hAChE-3e, hAChE-3f, and hAChE-donepezil complexes demonstrated stable protein conformations and persistent ligand accommodation within the catalytic gorge. MM/GBSA calculations further indicated a more favorable binding-energy profile for 3e than for 3f, whereas donepezil showed the most favorable overall calculated binding energy. Per-residue decomposition highlighted key gorge residues, including Trp86, Trp286, Tyr337, Tyr341, Phe295, and Phe297, as important contributors to ligand stabilization. Conclusions: Collectively, these computational findings provide structural and energetic support for the experimentally observed AChE inhibitory activity of the lead derivatives.

articles.title: Quality of Life in Patients with Treatment-Resistant Depression Treated with Intranasal Esketamine as Add-On Therapy to an SSRI-A Prospective, Comparative Study in Real-World Clinical Practice.
articles.abstract: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) remains one of the most clinically challenging forms of depressive disorders. In many patients, reduction in symptom severity does not translate into full functional recovery; therefore, assessment of treatment effectiveness should also include health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Objective: The aim of the study was to compare changes in HRQoL in patients with TRD receiving a treatment strategy including intranasal esketamine as add-on therapy to ongoing treatment based on selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and in patients treated with SSRI-based therapy without esketamine. Materials and Methods: A prospective, observational, comparative cohort study was conducted in real-world clinical practice. Sixty adult patients were included: 30 received intranasal esketamine as add-on therapy to ongoing SSRI-based treatment and 30 received SSRI-based treatment without esketamine. The study protocol did not impose a separate SSRI dose-optimization algorithm; drug selection and dose modifications remained at the discretion of the treating physician in accordance with routine clinical practice. Quality of life was assessed using the World Health Organization Quality of Life-BREF (WHOQOL-BREF) and the 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36). Depressive symptom severity was assessed using the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) and the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HDRS). Assessments were performed at baseline, weeks 4, 8, and 12, and after 12 months. Results: Both groups showed improvement in quality of life and reduction in depressive symptom severity, with larger absolute changes in the group receiving esketamine. Differences involved WHOQOL-BREF domains and selected standard SF-36 subscales. Conclusions: In this observational cohort, the treatment strategy including intranasal esketamine was associated with greater improvement in several HRQoL measures than SSRI-based treatment without esketamine. Because treatment exposure was not assigned by the investigators and residual confounding cannot be excluded, the findings should not be interpreted as evidence of an isolated causal effect of esketamine.

articles.title: Multi-Omics Analysis Identifies Gut-Associated Metabolic Signatures Associated with Metformin-Mediated Protection Against LPS-Induced Lung Injury.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced lung injury involves pulmonary inflammation, metabolic disturbance, and intestinal dysregulation. This study investigated whether metformin attenuates LPS-induced lung and colonic injury and characterized associated gut microbiota-metabolite changes. Methods: Male C57BL/6J mice were assigned to control (CON), LPS, metformin 200 mg/kg (MET 200 mg/kg), and metformin 400 mg/kg (MET 400 mg/kg) groups. Metformin was administered by gavage for 7 days before intranasal LPS challenge. Lung and colon injury were assessed by histology, immunostaining, ELISA, and RT-qPCR. Untargeted serum metabolomics, colonic-content metabolomics, and colonic-content shotgun metagenomics were performed in the CON, LPS, and MET 400 mg/kg groups. Differential-feature, pathway-enrichment, and exploratory Spearman correlation analyses were conducted. Results: Metformin reduced LPS-induced lung injury, inflammatory cytokine production, F4/80- and MPO-positive immune-cell infiltration, and colonic inflammatory and barrier-related abnormalities. Serum metabolomics identified 468 differential features in LPS versus CON and 286 in MET versus LPS, with 218 overlapping features. Colonic-content metabolomics identified 1000 and 554 differential features, respectively, with 328 overlapping features. Eight metabolites showed metformin-associated directional shifts toward control levels in both serum and colonic contents. Metagenomics showed metformin-associated remodeling of gut microbial composition and predicted gene-content functional potential. Exploratory integrated analyses linked metformin-responsive genera and shared metabolites with pulmonary inflammatory indicators. Conclusions: Metformin was associated with attenuated LPS-induced lung and colonic injury and coordinated gut-associated microbiota-metabolite remodeling. Because the study did not include a metformin-only group or causal perturbation experiments, these findings identify candidate associations rather than demonstrating a causal gut microbiota-metabolite-lung mechanism.

articles.title: Obinutuzumab and Chemotherapy for Front-Line Treatment of Follicular Lymphoma Grade 3B and Composite Follicular Lymphoma: A Study of the Croatian Cooperative Group for Hematologic Diseases (KroHem).
articles.abstract: Background: Data on outcomes of follicular lymphoma grade 3B (FL gr.3B) and composite lymphoma (FL/large B-cell lymphoma (B-LCL)) are scarce and the effect of obinutuzumab is unknown. Patients and methods: We analyzed outcomes of patients with FL gr.3B & FL/B-LCL receiving front-line treatment with obinutuzumab-chemotherapy combinations and compared them to previously published cohorts with FL gr.1-3A and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Results: Twenty-six patients were included; nine had FL gr.3B and 17 had FL/B-LCL. Response rate was 92%, and 60% achieved complete remission. OS and PFS rates at 3 years were 76% and 67%, respectively. Outcomes of patients with FL gr.3B and FL/B-LCL were similar. PFS and OS rates at 3 years were both 100% in patients with FLIPI 0-2 vs. 42% and 61% in those with FLIPI 3-4 (p = 0.005 and p = 0.031). PFS and OS rates at 3 years were both 100% in patients with IPI 0-2 vs. 29% and 55%, respectively, in those with IPI 3-5 (p = 0.004 and p = 0.014). Low-risk patients with FL gr.3B & FL/B-LCL, FL gr.1-3A and DLBCL all had 3-year OS and PFS rates above 80%. High-risk patients with FL gr.3B & FL/B-LCL had outcomes inferior to those with FL gr. 1-3A and similar to those with DLBCL. Conclusions: Our results suggest that front-line therapy with obinutuzumab-chemotherapy combinations has excellent outcomes in patients with low-risk FL gr.3B & FL/B-LCL, that both FLIPI and IPI are of prognostic value and that the clinical course of FL gr.3B & FL/B-LCL is more similar to DLBCL than FL gr.1-3A.

articles.title: MDL-001: An Oral, Direct-Acting Broad-Spectrum Antiviral for Influenza-like Illness (ILI) and Chronic Hepatitis In Vivo.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Endemic viral respiratory illnesses caused by influenza, RSV, and coronaviruses impose a global disease burden of hundreds of millions of infections and hundreds of thousands of deaths annually. Chronic hepatitis B and C infections persist in 254 million and 58 million people worldwide, respectively. No approved therapy addresses these viruses simultaneously. MDL-001 is an oral, direct-acting, broad-spectrum antiviral targeting the Thumb-1 allosteric site of viral polymerases. Methods: Here, we evaluated the antiviral activity of MDL-001 in vitro in influenza A/B, RSV, SARS-CoV-2, endemic human coronaviruses, and hepatitis B/C/D. We next evaluated MDL-001 antiviral activity in vivo in H1N1, SARS-CoV-2, HCV, and HBV. MDL-001's in vivo efficacy was compared head-to-head versus standards of care including oseltamivir, remdesivir, sofosbuvir, and tenofovir alafenamide, or through the literature comparison with nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir. Lastly, we evaluated the pharmacokinetics, metabolism, tolerability, and safety profile of MDL-001. Results: Here, we report that MDL-001 inhibits influenza A/B, RSV, SARS-CoV-2, endemic human coronaviruses, and hepatitis B/C/D viruses with nanomolar EC90 potency in vitro. MDL-001 demonstrated equivalent in vivo efficacy to oseltamivir against mouse-lethal influenza A virus infection, reducing lung viral load by 2.6 log10 and preventing weight loss and mortality. MDL-001 demonstrated equivalent symptom reduction to subcutaneous remdesivir after SARS-CoV-2 infection. MDL-001 reduced SARS-CoV-2 lung viral titers by 2.9 log10, superior to the literature-reported 1.4 log10 and 1.0 log10 reductions for nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir, respectively. MDL-001 reduced HCV viremia by 3.3 log10, equivalent to sofosbuvir. Oral MDL-001 reduced plasma HBV surface antigen by 2.5 log10, superior to tenofovir alafenamide from Day 8 through Day 21. MDL-001 demonstrated an in vitro EC50 of 79.4 nM against infection with RSV strain A2, which is a 416-fold improvement over literature-reported ribavirin. Oral pharmacokinetics studies demonstrate that MDL-001 is rapidly absorbed and partitioned into lung (Kp = 39-52) and liver (Kp = 71-104) tissues. MDL-001 produced no treatment-related tolerability adverse events across 376 animals and showed no hERG, Ames genotoxicity, or micronucleus safety issues. Conclusions: These findings support MDL-001 as a broad-spectrum, direct-acting non-nucleoside antiviral clinical candidate.

articles.title: Onabotulinum Toxin A (BoNTA) in the Treatment of Chronic and High-Frequency Episodic Migraine: A Real-World Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives. Although onabotulinumtoxinA (BoNTA) is an established therapy for chronic migraine (CM), its effectiveness in high-frequency episodic migraine (HFEM) remains uncertain. We conducted an 18-year, single-center, retrospective study of patients treated with BoNTA for CM or HFEM. Methods. We included 136 patients with CM and 71 with HFEM who had previously received multiple oral preventive therapies, who received BoNTA using an injection paradigm based on the PREEMPT protocol. Clinical and laboratory data were collected. Results. Responder rates, defined as a ≥50% reduction in monthly headache days, were 65.4% in CM and 71.8% in HFEM. Both groups showed a significant reduction in the frequency of headache days and headache intensity and improved response to symptomatic treatment. The mean duration of benefit among responders was 3.66 (SD 2.12) months in CM and 3.78 (SD 1.11) months in HFEM. No statistically significant associations were detected between responder status and either the duration of previous preventive treatment or the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio. Responders with CM showed a non-significant tendency to have used a lower number of preventive treatments compared with partial responders plus non-responders. At the end of follow-up, 42.6% of CM and 57.8% of HFEM patients remained on BoNTA. Conclusions. In this retrospective uncontrolled cohort, reductions in headache frequency and other clinical improvements were observed during BoNTA treatment in patients with CM and HFEM. Because this study lacked a control group, these findings cannot establish the efficacy of BoNTA in HFEM and should be interpreted as exploratory.

articles.title: Identification of Novel Potential Tubulin-Targeting Heterocyclic Compounds via Integrated Virtual Screening and In Vitro Studies.
articles.abstract: Background: The development of novel tubulin-targeting agents remains a promising strategy in anticancer drug design. In the present study, novel heterocyclic tubulin-targeting compounds were identified using a complex in silico/in vitro workflow. Methods: An in-house library of approximately 8000 structurally diverse heterocyclic compounds was screened for antiproliferative activity, yielding 260 experimentally validated hits. These compounds were docked against the colchicine, vinca, and taxane binding sites of tubulin. Selected compounds were also tested for their effects on cellular β-tubulin protein levels in Jurkat cells. Results: Docking analysis indicated that 42 compounds matched or exceeded colchicine's binding energy, 3 compounds were comparable to vinblastine, and 18 compounds surpassed paclitaxel, suggesting the colchicine and taxane sites as preferred targets. Five top-scoring compounds (Les-6370, Les-4272, Les-4309, Les-4403, and Les-1419) were further analyzed via molecular dynamics simulations, confirming stable binding-particularly at the colchicine site-and favorable hydrogen-bonding and lipophilic interactions. At 10 µM, Les-1419 and Les-4309 reduced total cellular β-tubulin protein levels in Jurkat cells by 57.73% and 54.31%, respectively, relative to the effect observed for the reference compound Combretastatin A-4. Conclusions: This study resulted in the identification of novel starting scaffolds with favorable tubulin interaction activity and predicted drug-like properties, representing structurally novel parent structures and serving as promising starting points for further structural optimization and analogue development.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of Switching from Prostaglandin Analogs to Omidenepag Isopropyl in Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma and Glaucoma Suspect Patients with Prostaglandin-Associated Periorbitopathy: A Prospective, Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Prostaglandin-associated periorbitopathy (PAP) is a common treatment-related burden of prostaglandin analog (PGA) therapy that may compromise long-term glaucoma management. This study evaluated improvement in PAP and changes in intraocular pressure (IOP) after switching from PGAs to omidenepag isopropyl. Methods: This prospective, multicenter study was conducted in Korea over 24 weeks. Adults diagnosed with PAP who had received PGA eye drops for ≥3 months for primary open-angle glaucoma, normal-tension glaucoma, or glaucoma suspect were switched to omidenepag isopropyl. PAP manifestations were evaluated using investigator assessments, independent assessments, and patient-reported outcome measures. Changes in IOP and safety outcomes were also assessed. Results: A total of 96 patients were included in the final analysis. At Week 24, improvement in deepening of the upper eyelid sulcus was observed in 78.16% of patients. Improvements were also observed in flattening of the lower eyelid bag, upper eyelid ptosis, ciliary hypertrichosis, and periorbital hyperpigmentation. Mean IOP was significantly reduced from baseline (-2.14 mmHg), with 42.71% and 27.08% of patients achieving IOP reductions of ≥15% and ≥20%, respectively. Findings were consistent overall across institutional, independent, and subjective assessments. Most adverse events were mild, and no serious adverse events were reported. Conclusions: PAP manifestations improved following transition from PGA therapy to omidenepag isopropyl, while IOP control and favorable tolerability were maintained in glaucoma or glaucoma suspect patients with PAP. These findings may support the clinical feasibility of switching from PGAs to omidenepag isopropyl in patients with PAP.

articles.title: Phyto-Mediated Synthesized Gold Nanoparticles (AuNPs) from Ozoroa paniculosa Leaf Extracts: Chemical Characterization and Antidiabetic Evaluation.
articles.abstract: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is a serious health concern, as it remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Despite the available antidiabetic drugs used in the management of diabetes, the continuous increase in hyperglycemia has prompted growing interest in developing effective, green alternative therapeutic strategies for diabetes mellitus. Hence, this study aimed to synthesize O. paniculosa extract-passivated AuNPs and evaluate their antidiabetic properties. Methods: The plant material was sequentially extracted with n-hexane, dichloromethane (DCM) and 70% ethanol (70% EtOH), after which the resulting extracts were used to synthesize AuNPs that were characterized through various analytical techniques. The antioxidant activity of AuNPs was screened against DPPH, ABTS, metal iron chelating and reducing power. The enzyme inhibitory activity of AuNPs on α-amylase, as well as the ability of AuNPs to glycate protein, was investigated on a BSA-fructose model over a period of 28 days. Results: The FT-IR, pXRD, HR-TEM, STEM-EDS and UV-Vis spectroscopy analyses confirmed the synthesis of O. paniculosa extract-passivated AuNPs bearing faceted NPs and triangular 2D nanoplates morphologies. Despite the poor scavenging activity of AuNPs on DPPH and ABTS, a significant metal-ion chelating potential with IC50 values ranging from 76.7 ± 0.02 μg/mL to 83.3 ± 0.03 μg/mL and a good reduction potential was observed. Furthermore, an inhibition in concentration-dependent α-amylase activity was observed, with IC50 values ranging from 76.7 ± 0.02 μg/mL to 380 ± 0.12 μg/mL, and the formation of AGEs was suppressed, with an inhibitory effect observed over a period of 28 days. Conclusions: The results obtained suggest that O. paniculosa extract-passivated AuNPs possess some potential antioxidant and antidiabetic properties.

articles.title: The Network Pharmacology of Rosmarinic Acid and Elucidating the Wound Healing Potential of a Rosmarinic Acid-Enriched Trachystemon orientalis Extract.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives:Trachystemon orientalis (L.) D. Don has been reported to be used in folk medicine for the treatment of inflammatory wounds and for its contained rosmarinic acid, a phenolic compound known for its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and wound healing properties. This study aimed to obtain a rosmarinic acid-enriched extract from the aerial parts of T. orientalis and evaluate its in vitro wound healing potential. Methods: Extraction conditions were optimized using fractional factorial design and Box-Behnken optimization. Rosmarinic acid content was quantified by RP-HPLC. A rosmarinic acid-enriched extract was compared with a maceration extract and isolated rosmarinic acid. Elastase, hyaluronidase, and collagenase inhibitory activities were determined. Cytotoxicity was evaluated on L929 fibroblasts using the MTT assay, and non-cytotoxic concentrations were assessed for their effects on in vitro wound healing by scratch assay. In addition, in silico target prediction and network pharmacology analyses were performed using rosmarinic acid. Results: Optimization successfully yielded a rosmarinic acid-enriched extract from T. orientalis. The rosmarinic acid-enriched extract inhibited wound-related enzymes and enhanced wound closure in the scratch assay. Network pharmacology analysis showed putative molecular targets and signaling pathways potentially associated with the wound healing activity of rosmarinic acid, especially those involved in inflammatory responses, extracellular matrix remodeling, and tissue regeneration. Conclusions: The rosmarinic acid-enriched extract exhibited promising in vitro wound healing-related activity through the inhibition of extracellular matrix degrading enzymes and promotion of wound closure. Furthermore, network pharmacology analysis provided preliminary mechanistic insights based on computational predictions.

articles.title: Physicochemical, Predicted ADME, and Structural Positioning of Azelaic Acid Within an Endocrine Oncology Reference Framework.
articles.abstract: Background: Azelaic acid, an established dermatologic dicarboxylic acid, was previously nominated as an unusual anticancer repurposing candidate. However, it remains unclear whether physicochemical properties, predicted ADME, or structural proximity to established endocrine anticancer drugs support this hypothesis. This study positioned azelaic acid relative to a clinically anchored endocrine anticancer reference panel using reference-defined space based on physicochemical and predicted ADME descriptors and two-dimensional structural similarity analyses. Methods: Sixteen clinically used endocrine anticancer drugs defined the reference set, with finasteride and dutasteride included as mechanistic comparators. SwissADME descriptors were screened for redundancy, standardized, and analyzed by principal component analysis and Euclidean nearest neighbor distances. Robustness was assessed by leave-one-reference-out, bootstrap, and WLOGP sensitivity analyses. Structural similarity was evaluated independently using Morgan fingerprints and Tanimoto coefficients. Results: The first two principal components explained 75.31% of reference variance. Flutamide was the nearest Clinical Reference to azelaic acid in physicochemical and predicted ADME space (d = 3.0063), but this distance exceeded the reference q90 threshold (2.6521), classifying azelaic acid as extrapolative. This classification persisted in all 16 leave-one-reference-out analyses and in 73.69% of 992 valid bootstrap replicates. Structurally, the highest reference similarity was observed with toremifene (T = 0.08696), below the minimum internal Clinical Reference nearest-neighbor similarity (0.13761); radius-3 sensitivity analysis preserved this result. Conclusions: Azelaic acid is neither a close structural analog nor a physicochemical and predicted ADME neighbor of established endocrine anticancer drugs. Its network-derived nomination therefore represents a non-canonical repurposing hypothesis requiring further experimental validation.

articles.title: Green Synthesis of Silver Nanoparticles Using Artemisia absinthium and Ziziphus vulgaris Extracts: Comparative Evaluation of Antibacterial, Anti-Inflammatory, Wound-Healing and Anticancer Activities.
articles.abstract: Background: Plant-mediated synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) has emerged as a sustainable alternative to conventional chemical methods, offering environmentally friendly routes for producing nanomaterials with biomedical potential. This study employed aqueous extracts of Artemisia absinthium and Ziziphus vulgaris to synthesize AgNPs and evaluate their antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, anticancer, wound healing activities. Methods: Silver nanoparticles were synthesized by mixing aqueous plant extracts with 1 mM silver nitrate under ambient conditions. The formation of AgNPs was confirmed by UV-Visible spectroscopy, while morphology and structure were characterized using Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. Moreover, the biosynthesized silver nanoparticles were further characterized by dynamic light scattering (DLS) and zeta potential measurements to determine hydrodynamic size and surface charge, and by X-ray diffraction (XRD) to confirm crystalline phase. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) was also performed to assess elemental composition, providing a comprehensive physicochemical profile of the plant-mediated AgNPs. Antibacterial activity was tested against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus using the agar well diffusion, minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimal bactericidal concentration (MBC) methods. Anti-inflammatory activity was evaluated by hypotonicity-induced human red blood cell (HRBC) membrane stabilization assay. Cytotoxic activity was evaluated using the MTT assay against a panel of human cell lines comprising MCF-7 breast cancer cells, A549 lung cancer cells, HepG2 hepatic cancer cells, and WI-38 non-cancerous lung fibroblasts to assess both anticancer potency and selectivity toward normal cells. Scratch wound healing was also evaluated. Results: The biosynthesized AgNPs showed surface plasmon resonance bands at 420-450 nm and mainly spherical particles with sizes of 15-22 nm. FTIR analysis indicated hydroxyl and carbonyl groups involved in nanoparticle reduction and stabilization. DLS and zeta potential analyses revealed monomodal size distributions and strongly negative surface charges (approximately -33 to -34 mV), indicating homogeneous, electrostatically stabilized colloids. XRD patterns confirmed a face-centered cubic metallic silver phase with a dominant (111) orientation, while EDX spectra verified the presence of elemental silver alongside signals from the plant-derived capping layer. The nanoparticles displayed remarkable antibacterial activity against both bacteria, strong inhibition of erythrocyte hemolysis, and dose-dependent cytotoxicity toward MCF-7 cells with IC50 values of 19-21 µg mL-1. MIC values ranged from 15.62 to 125 µg mL-1, with the lowest MIC observed for Ziziphus stem-mediated AgNPs (15.62 µg mL-1). All AgNPs samples exhibited enhanced wound healing, with closure percentages reaching up to 93.4% in Ziziphus leaves compared to WI-38 control (77.6%). Good colloidal stability was maintained for 90 days. Conclusions: These findings show that Artemisia absinthium and Ziziphus vulgaris are effective sources for green synthesis of stable AgNPs with multifunctional in vitro biological activities. This pro-healing effect is consistent with their demonstrated antimicrobial activity, supporting their dual functionality as both antibacterial and wound-healing materials. However, the biological and therapeutic activities require further in vivo confirmation. The results support their biomedical and environmentally sustainable nanotechnology applications.

articles.title: Mechanistic Profiling of Phenethyl Isothiocyanate in CCRF-CEM Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Cells.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Phenethyl isothiocyanate (PEITC), a bioactive compound found in cruciferous vegetables, exhibits potent anti-cancer activity, but its molecular mechanisms in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) remain poorly defined. This study aimed to investigate the anti-leukemic effects of PEITC. Methods: PEITC cytotoxicity was assessed in human cancer cell lines using resazurin reduction assays. Microarray and Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA) were used to investigate altered molecular signaling pathways. Functional assays were performed to assess DNA damage, cell-cycle progression, apoptosis, autophagy, mitochondrial membrane potential, microtubule organization and endothelial tube formation. Western blotting was performed to examine pathway-related proteins, and preliminary in vivo antitumor activity was evaluated using a CCRF-CEM zebrafish xenograft model. Results: PEITC exerted potent cytotoxicity against CCRF-CEM cells (IC50 = 1.76 ± 0.07 µM). Microarray and IPA analyses predicted inhibition of PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling, which was further supported by Western blot analysis. Functional assays demonstrated that PEITC induced DNA damage, cell cycle perturbation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and apoptotic and autophagic responses. PEITC also disrupted microtubule organization in GFP-tagged α-tubulin-expressing U2OS cells. Furthermore, PEITC suppressed endothelial tube formation in EA.hy926 cell lines and exhibited preliminary in vivo antitumor activity in a zebrafish xenograft model (n = 10). Conclusions: These findings provide mechanistic insights into the anti-leukemic activity of PEITC and demonstrate its effects on multiple cellular processes associated with leukemia cell survival and proliferation, supporting further investigation of its therapeutic potential in ALL.

articles.title: Functionalization of Metal-Enriched Pleurotus Biomass with γ-Poly-Glutamic Acid for Cytoprotective and Antimicrobial Wound Care.
articles.abstract: Objectives: Chronic wound dressings require active components that support moisture management, biocompatibility, and local bioburden control. Therefore, in this study, freeze-dried biomass of Pleurotus ostreatus (Po) and Pleurotus djamor (Pdj) was cultivated in vitro under mineral-enriched conditions (calcium, magnesium, zinc) and subsequently modified with poly(γ-glutamic acid) (γ-PGA) to develop a bioactive fungal matrix intended as a functional additive for future wound-care biomaterials. Methods: The elemental content of the biomass was determined using atomic absorption spectroscopy (AAS), and the resulting biomaterial underwent physicochemical analyses-including scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), wettability measurements, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and thermogravimetric analysis (TG)-as well as biological performance assessments using a disk diffusion assay and cytotoxicity analysis. Results: Mineral enrichment enhanced Pleurotus spp. biomass production and metal accumulation, while γ-PGA coating altered surface properties and cytocompatibility. Zinc supplementation significantly promoted biomass formation in both Pleurotus species, while metal accumulation depended on the specific element and fortification regime. γ-PGA modification reduced the accessible BET surface area and formed a denser polymer-associated layer, confirmed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. While the unmodified Po biomass exhibited the strongest in vitro antibacterial activity against S. aureus and P. aeruginosa, it also displayed dose-dependent cytotoxicity toward HaCaT keratinocytes at high concentrations. The addition of γ-PGA moderately reduced the in vitro bacterial inhibition zones but provided a critical cytoprotective effect, mitigating the cytotoxicity of the concentrated fungal extracts and rescuing HaCaT-cell viability to meet ISO 10993-5 safety thresholds. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate that γ-PGA-modified, metal-enriched Pleurotus biomass exhibits a distinct in vitro trade-off between absolute antimicrobial potency and cellular safety, supporting its further investigation as a biocompatible ingredient for multifunctional wound-dressing systems.

articles.title: Adverse Event Reporting Patterns Associated with Concomitant Use of 5-HT3 and NK-1 Receptor Antagonists: A Large-Scale Spontaneous-Reporting Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) is common and compromises quality of life and adherence. 5-HT3 receptor antagonists (RAs) and NK-1 RAs are cornerstones, yet adverse event patterns associated with their concomitant use are not well characterized. Methods: We queried the US Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) from 2004 Q1-2025 Q1 and deduplicated reports per Food and Drug Administration (FDA) guidance. Five algorithms-the Ω shrinkage measure, additive model, multiplicative model, combination risk ratio, and chi-square model-detected disproportionate reporting signals associated with concomitant use. We also performed time-to-onset (TTO) analysis and logistic regression. Results: We identified 965 concurrent use cases with a mean age of 58 years and a mean weight of 70 kg, with 59.7% (n = 575) of these cases being female. These reports included 366 preferred terms (PTs). Forty-nine PTs were significant across all five algorithms, mainly skin and subcutaneous disorders, hypersensitivity reactions, blood pressure abnormalities, hepatic and renal impairment, and nervous system disorders, with additional signals for abnormal antidiuretic hormone secretion, respiratory disorders, and oropharyngeal disorders. TTO showed most adverse drug events (ADEs) occurred within 20 days of therapy initiation. Logistic regression indicated that older age was associated with higher odds of classification as an important medical event (IME). Conclusions: Beyond prescribing information, we detected previously unrecognized adverse event terms that were disproportionately reported with concomitant use and that merit attention in practice.

articles.title: Formulation Development and Characterization of Quercetin Solid Dispersions with Integrated In Vitro Release and In Vivo Pharmacokinetic Assessment.
articles.abstract: Purpose: To address the challenges of low water solubility and poor bioavailability of quercetin (QUE), which limit its clinical application, and to develop an optimized oral solid dispersion formulation to enhance its absorption. Methods: Quercetin solid dispersions (QUE-SD) were prepared using the solvent evaporation method. The study involved screening single-factor and combined carriers, followed by formulation optimization via orthogonal analysis based on solubility and cumulative dissolution rates. The optimized dispersions were characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). Additionally, transmembrane transport was evaluated using Caco-2 and MDCK cell models, and oral bioavailability was assessed through pharmacokinetic studies in rats. Results: The optimal formulation was determined to be a 1:3:1 ratio of Quercetin, Hypromellose E5, and polyvinylpyrrolidone K13-18, with an evaporation temperature of 55 °C and a mixing time of 4 h. In cell transport models, the apparent permeability coefficient of QUE-SD increased by 1.14 (Caco-2) and 1.1 (MDCK) times. Pharmacokinetic data confirmed that the solid dispersion significantly improved both the absorption rate and oral bioavailability of quercetin in rats. Conclusions: The prepared quercetin solid dispersion effectively enhances the water solubility, transmembrane transport, and systemic absorption of quercetin. These findings provide a viable strategy and theoretical basis for developing high-bioavailability oral formulations of quercetin.

articles.title: Comparative Effects of IL-17 and IL-23 Inhibitors on Lipid Profiles and Lipid-Derived Atherogenic Indices in Patients with Psoriasis.
articles.abstract: Background: Psoriasis is associated with increased cardiovascular risk and altered lipid metabolism. The comparative effects of IL-17 and IL-23 inhibitors on lipid-derived atherogenic indices remain unclear.
