Results: We found that SGI-1027 encapsulation improves key NP properties in a SGI-1027-dose-dependent fashion: NP yield, drug encapsulation efficiency, morphology, and morphometrics; on the other hand, the ζ-potential and polydispersity were not affected. A molecular interaction between BSA and SGI-1027 was found at 1057-906 cm-1 using FT-IR. Raman spectroscopy revealed a fingerprint of SGI-1027 encapsulated into BSA at 728-650 cm-1, corresponding to the 2,4-diamino-6-methylpyrimidine of SGI-1027. NPs were internalized by mouse peritoneal macrophages, where accumulation at the cell membrane border, cytoplasm, and nuclear membrane was observed only when loaded with SGI-1027. Internalization coincided with an anti-inflammatory response. Conclusions: We found a synergistic effect between glucose and N2 (solvent drag) on protein self-assembly nanostructuration; this methodology offers an alternative to glutaraldehyde and heat crosslinking to encapsulate hydrophobic or thermolabile drugs.

articles.title: Study on Construction of and Pharmacodynamics of Baicalin-Minoxidil Co-Loaded Nanogel.
articles.abstract: Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) is a chronic and highly prevalent hair loss disorder for which current topical therapies are limited by undesirable side effects, dose-dependent efficacy, and poor skin penetration. Objective: Here, we developed a baicalin-minoxidil co-loaded nanogel (Bai-Min-NGs) to synergistically enhance transdermal drug delivery and promote hair regeneration. Methods: The optimized nanogel exhibited favorable colloidal attributes, featuring a nanoscale hydrodynamic diameter of 156 ± 3.62 nm, narrow size distribution (polydispersity index of 0.144 ± 0.011), surface zeta potential of -26.1 ± 0.37 mV, high encapsulation efficiencies (95.86 ± 1.34% for baicalin and 82.16 ± 2.50% for minoxidil), and satisfactory drug loading capacities (1.92 ± 0.08% and 1.64 ± 0.06%, respectively). Results: Enhanced cellular internalization through endocytosis further promoted the proliferation and migration of human dermal papilla cells, demonstrating a synergistic biological effect beyond either drug alone. In an androgenetic alopecia mouse model, topical Bai-Min-NGs significantly accelerated hair regrowth, as evidenced by increased hair length, hair weight, hair follicle density, and dermal thickness. Notably, the nanogel achieved superior therapeutic efficacy while maintaining excellent local and systemic biosafety. Mechanistically, Bai-Min-NGs activated the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway by upregulating Wnt7b and Wnt10b expression, suppressing TGF-β1, and increasing the protein expression of GSK3β, phosphorylated GSK3β, β-catenin, and VEGF, thereby promoting hair follicle regeneration and angiogenesis. Conclusions: Collectively, Bai-Min-NGs provide a promising topical co-delivery nanoplatform integrating superior cutaneous retention with endogenous pathway activation for hair regeneration therapy.

articles.title: Dual Solid-State PBPK Modelling to Assess the Bio(in)equivalence of Tacrolimus Amorphous Formulations with Storage-Induced Crystallisation: A Potential Application of Virtual Bioequivalence.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Amorphous drug products are susceptible to crystallisation during manufacture or storage, which may alter dissolution and pharmacokinetics (PK). Tacrolimus, a low-solubility, high-permeability drug, relies on amorphous formulations to achieve adequate absorption, making crystallisation a key quality risk. Physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models with simultaneous tracking of amorphous and crystalline fractions as different solid states within the gut enable a mechanistic assessment of how crystallinity may influence PK and bioequivalence (BE) outcomes. Methods: A PBPK model incorporating mechanistic dissolution was developed to evaluate the impact of tacrolimus solid-state composition on BE. Model performance was verified against clinical PK data for formulations spanning a range of crystallinity levels. Virtual BE (VBE) assessments were conducted using two-way and fully replicated four-period crossover designs. Within-subject variability (WSV) was introduced mechanistically through physiological parameters. Results: The PBPK model adequately reproduced the crystallinity-dependent PK of tacrolimus observed in clinical studies. VBE simulations captured the reported trend of crystallinity-driven bioinequivalence, with increasing crystallinity primarily influencing Cmax and having a limited effect on AUC0-24h, suggesting a predominant impact on absorption rate. Model-based extrapolation beyond the clinically evaluated range indicated that crystallinity levels of 5-15% may be associated with a higher likelihood of meeting BE criteria under a fully replicated four-period crossover design. Conclusions: Mechanistic PBPK modelling enabled extrapolation beyond clinically tested crystallinity levels by linking solid-state behaviour to in vivo performance. This approach can complement experimental evidence and support BE assessment and risk evaluation during formulation development, clinical evaluation, and post-approval change management.

articles.title: Population Pharmacokinetics of Amikacin and Monte Carlo Simulation Study in Critically Ill Septic Patients Undergoing Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy with CytoSorb® or oXiris®.
articles.abstract: Background: Adsorptive devices, including CytoSorb® and oXiris®, are increasingly added to continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) in septic patients, but their effect on amikacin clearance and exposure is unknown. We characterized amikacin pharmacokinetics (PK) during adsorptive CRRT and derived dosing implications. Methods: A population PK model was developed in 24 critically ill septic patients (using NONMEM ver. 7.5.0), separating intrinsic clearance (CL_int) from filter-specific extracorporeal clearance (CL_CRRT). Sparse pre-filter sampling was handled using informative priors for distribution parameters. Robustness was assessed by sampling-importance-resampling (SIR) and prediction-corrected visual predictive checks (pcVPC). Monte Carlo simulations (9000 subjects) evaluated probability of target attainment (PTA; Cmax/MIC ≥ 8, AUC24/MIC ≥ 75) and cumulative fraction of response (CFR) against four Gram-negative pathogens across three regimens (500 mg q8h, 500 mg q24h, 1500 mg q24h), two filters, and three connection times. Results: While connected, the CytoSorb® and oXiris® CRRT configurations increased amikacin clearance by 61% and 93%, respectively, accounting for 38-48% of total clearance (CL_TOT). Because these devices were only applied for 10-14 h per 24 h interval in simulated scenarios, there were only minor differences in target attainment. Hence, dosing regimen, not device type or connection timing, dominated. Only amikacin at 1500 mg once daily achieved CFR ≥ 90%, and only for susceptible Enterobacterales. Conclusions: Adsorptive CRRT configurations substantially increase extracorporeal amikacin clearance. These exploratory findings support high-dose, once-daily, concentration-guided amikacin dosing during adsorptive CRRT, although this dose may be insufficient against pathogens with elevated MICs.

articles.title: Development and Physicochemical Characterization of Trans-Resveratrol Liposomes: Influence of Phospholipid Composition and Ultrasound-Assisted Processing.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Trans-resveratrol is a bioactive polyphenol with limited pharmaceutical applicability due to poor aqueous solubility, chemical instability, and low bioavailability. This study aimed to develop trans-resveratrol-containing liposomal formulations and evaluate the influence of phospholipid composition and ultrasound-assisted processing (UAP) using a conventional ultrasonic bath on their physicochemical properties and storage behavior. Methods: Liposomes were prepared by the ethanol injection method using Lipoid® S75, Lipoid® P45, soybean lecithin, egg yolk lecithin, and selected binary phospholipid mixtures. Trans-resveratrol identity was verified by LC-MS. Particle size, polydispersity index (PDI), and zeta potential were determined before and after UAP, and physical stability was assessed after 30 days of refrigerated, light-protected storage. Results: Phospholipid composition markedly influenced liposome physicochemical characteristics. Lipoid® P45-based formulations exhibited favorable initial particle size, PDI, and zeta potential profiles. UAP generally reduced particle size and improved particle size distribution immediately after preparation, although the magnitude of the effect depended on formulation composition. During refrigerated storage, short-term physical storage behavior was strongly formulation-dependent. Selected trans-resveratrol-containing formulations, particularly Lr12, Lr13, and Lr15, exhibited marked particle growth and increased polydispersity, whereas Lr20-Lr22 exhibited the most favorable particle size and PDI profiles after 30 days. Conclusions: Phospholipid composition was a critical determinant of trans-resveratrol liposome performance. Conventional ultrasonic-bath processing provided a simple and accessible means of improving initial liposomal characteristics, but did not universally ensure short-term physical stability during 30 days of refrigerated storage. Selected binary phospholipid formulations, particularly Lr20-Lr22, showed favorable physicochemical profiles and may represent promising candidates for further formulation development.

articles.title: Response Surface Methodology-Guided Development of Hot-Melt-Extruded Cannabidiol Solid Self-Emulsifying Drug Delivery Systems for Enhanced Drug Release and Stability.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cannabidiol (CBD) is a non-psychoactive phytocannabinoid, with numerous therapeutic applications. It can be used to treat pain, inflammation, anxiety, and schizophrenia and it is also used to treat severe forms of infant epilepsy. CBD is a highly lipophilic compound with low oral bioavailability due to poor aqueous solubility and extensive first-pass metabolism. Self-emulsifying drug delivery systems (SEDDSs) offer a promising approach to enhancing the solubility and stability of lipophilic compounds like CBD. This study aimed to design and optimize CBD-loaded solid SEDDSs (S-SEDDSs) using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to identify the optimal formulation parameters for improved drug release and stability. Methods: Excipients were selected through qualitative screening studies, considering their functional properties in SEDDS development. A Central Composite Design (CCD) was employed for response surface optimization to evaluate the effect of independent variables on formulation performance, including oil concentration and the surfactant-co-surfactant ratio. Formulations were processed using hot-melt extrusion (HME). The lead formulation was tested for drug content, in vitro drug release and stability studies. Results: The solid SEDDS formulation showed a drug content of 98.15 ± 1.94% and achieved 76.6 ± 0.6% drug release within three hours during in vitro dissolution testing, compared to 28 ± 0.9% for pure CBD. During stability testing, the lead formulation showed minimal change at both 25 °C and 40 °C. Conclusions: Overall, the study demonstrated that RSM-guided formulation development combined with HME processing can produce CBD S-SEDDSs and improve in vitro drug release compared to pure CBD.

articles.title: Acorn Shell Extract-Functionalized Cotton Biomaterials: A Sustainable Platform with Biological Activities and Controlled Release for Skin Microbiota Dysregulation Conditions.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Skin dysbiosis is associated with several dermatological disorders and is often accompanied by oxidative stress and inflammation. Bioactive textiles offer a promising strategy for localized skin health management; however, many currently available materials rely on synthetic or metal-based agents. This study aimed to develop sustainable cotton-based bioactive textiles functionalized with acorn shell (AS) extract, an agri-food by-product rich in phenolic compounds, and evaluate their biological performance potential for skin-contact applications in the management of skin dysbiosis conditions. Methods: Cotton fabrics were pre-treated with chitosan, a commercial cationic agent, or potassium alum and functionalized with AS extract using exhaustion or padding techniques. The resulting materials were assessed for antimicrobial activity against skin-associated bacteria, antioxidant capacity, anti-inflammatory activity in LPS-stimulated macrophages, cytocompatibility with keratinocytes and macrophages, and phenolic compound release under skin-mimicking conditions. Results: AS-functionalized cotton exhibited strong antimicrobial activity, particularly against Gram-positive bacteria, together with significant antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects. All functionalized textiles maintained keratinocyte viability above established cytocompatibility thresholds, supporting their suitability for direct skin contact. Exhaustion-treated samples showed higher phenolic incorporation and release, resulting in enhanced biological performance, whereas padding-treated fabrics exhibited lower phenolic loading, more sustained release profiles, and comparatively reduced bioactivity. Conclusions: AS extract can be successfully incorporated into cotton textiles using industrially relevant finishing methods, generating multifunctional materials with antimicrobial, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory properties while maintaining cytocompatibility. These findings support the potential of AS-functionalized cotton as a sustainable, plant-based skin-contact textile platform for localized management of skin-dysbiosis-associated conditions, with great relevance for dermatological and healthcare applications.

articles.title: In Silico Investigation of Electrically Guided Drug Transport Toward Morphology-Specific Brain Tumor Treatment.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Iontophoresis employs an applied electric field to induce electromigration, enabling the active and directional transport of drug molecules. This study presents the first computational investigation of iontophoretic drug delivery targeting human brain tumors. The objective was to evaluate the feasibility of this approach and to determine how electrode configurations influence drug transport across different tumor morphologies. Methods: A realistic finite element head model was constructed from T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging data. Two representative glioblastoma morphologies were considered: a spherical tumor in the left hemisphere and a butterfly-shaped tumor extending across the corpus callosum. Six electrode configurations spanning three categories (scalp electrodes, combined catheter and scalp electrodes, and catheter electrodes) were systematically evaluated. The electric field distribution was computed by solving the quasi-static Laplace equation, and the spatiotemporal distribution of gadobutrol was obtained using the Nernst-Planck equation. Drug delivery performance was quantified in terms of tumor coverage and targeting efficiency. Results: Under the simulated conditions, iontophoresis markedly enhanced drug delivery compared with passive diffusion, increasing tumor volume coverage from 13% to 84% in the spherical tumor model. Scalp electrode configurations resulted in the lowest tumor coverage in both tumor models. The combined catheter-scalp configuration generated radial drug transport from the catheter and achieved the highest coverage in the spherical tumor. In the butterfly-shaped tumor model, a three-catheter configuration enabled bilateral delivery along the tumor axis, achieving a tumor coverage of 49% and a targeting efficiency of 82%. The maximum electric field magnitude across all configurations was 49.26 V/m, remaining below reported axonal activation thresholds for deep brain stimulation. Conclusions: These findings support the feasibility of iontophoretic drug delivery to human brain tumors and demonstrate that the effective electrode configuration depends on tumor morphology. This study provides a computational foundation for morphology-specific planning of iontophoretic drug delivery to brain tumors.

articles.title: Exploring the Bioactive Properties of Thymus kotschyanus var. kotschyanus and Endemic Thymus brachychilus: From Plant Extracts to Alginate Film Formulations for Wound Infection Management.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Antibiotic resistance poses significant challenges to the treatment of infectious diseases. Wounds occur as a result of damage to the skin caused by various factors and may become life-threatening with the development of infection. Plants can exhibit considerable microbiological activity due to their rich phytochemical composition. Thymus kotschyanus var. kotschyanus and the endemic species Thymus brachychilus collected from Adıyaman Province, Türkiye, have been widely used by local communities for their therapeutic properties and other purposes. Methods: In this study, ethanol extracts of these plants were prepared and evaluated for their antimicrobial activity against nine Gram-negative bacteria, seven Gram-positive bacteria, one mycobacterial strain, and four yeast strains using agar well diffusion and microdilution methods. Their antibiofilm activity was assessed using a microplate-based assay, anti-quorum sensing activity was evaluated using Chromobacterium violaceum strains, anti-infective activity was investigated using the Caenorhabditis elegans model, and cytotoxicity was evaluated using the MTT assay. The phytochemical composition of the extracts was determined by HPLC-DAD. Alginate film formulations containing the extracts were prepared using the solvent-casting method and characterized by FTIR spectroscopy and light microscopy. Their antimicrobial and antibiofilm activities were subsequently evaluated. Results: Both extracts exhibited antimicrobial, antibiofilm, anti-quorum sensing, and anti-infective activities, while no cytotoxic effects were observed. Rosmarinic acid was identified as the major compound in both extracts. The extract-loaded alginate films exhibited antimicrobial and antibiofilm activities and showed no cytotoxic effects. Conclusions: These findings suggest that alginate film formulations may be a promising approach for the topical application of T. kotschyanus var. kotschyanus and T. brachychilus extracts. In particular, the alginate films containing both plant extracts may have potential as wound dressing materials for preventing wound infections or supporting the treatment of infected wounds.

articles.title: Optimized Flomoxef Dosing Strategy for Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamase-Producing Bacteria, Based on Pooled Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background: Flomoxef exhibits antibacterial activity against extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing bacteria and is a potential alternative to carbapenems. However, its pharmacokinetic (PK) characteristics remain unclear, and the appropriate minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) breakpoint for flomoxef remains controversial. This study aimed to develop a flomoxef PK model using pooled meta-analysis and to evaluate various dosing regimens for ESBL-producing bacterial infections. Methods: Flomoxef concentration data were systematically collected from PubMed and J-STAGE. PK modeling of flomoxef was performed using the collected serum concentration data with NONMEM 7.5. Patient characteristics were examined as covariates for clearance and volume of distribution. For stochastic PK/pharmacodynamic (PD) simulation, the probability of attaining the PK/PD target {70% free time above the MIC [fT > MIC]} was calculated. The target MIC was determined by systematically reviewing flomoxef susceptibility data for ESBL-producing bacteria across different regions. Results: The population PK analysis included 39 adult patients [mean age, 58.2 years; mean body weight, 52.7 kg; and mean creatinine clearance (CLcr), 44.1 mL/min]. In the PK model, CLcr was incorporated as a covariate of flomoxef clearance. A visual predictive check and goodness-of-fit plots demonstrated relatively good stability and predictive performance of the final model. For the PD evaluation, the target MIC was set at 4 µg/mL based on the systematically collected susceptibility data for ESBL-producing bacteria. PK/PD breakpoints for dosing regimens of 1 g twice daily (2 g/day) in typical patients with CLcr = 10 mL/min, 1 g three times daily (3 g/day) in patients with CLcr = 30 mL/min, and 1 g four times daily (4 g/day) with 3 h-infusion in patients with CLcr = 60 and 90 mL/min achieved the target MIC. Conclusions: Based on the stochastic PK/PD simulation results, prolonged-infusion regimens may more effectively cover isolates with a target MIC of 4 µg/mL than short-duration infusion regimens in typical patients with normal renal function (CLcr = 60 or 90 mL/min). However, clinical studies in various scenarios including severe infections are needed to identify the relationship between PK/PD results and clinical efficacy since our findings are based solely on simulation.

articles.title: Acute Immunocompatibility Profiling of Linear Poly(FTC) for Long-Acting Emtricitabine Delivery.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Long-acting therapeutics are being investigated for their potential to enhance medication adherence and improve overall treatment outcomes. Due to the prolonged residence time at the administration site, such as subcutaneous insertion, long-acting preparations may modulate the responses of local immune cells linked to material characteristics. Long-acting Polymer of Prodrug (POP) of Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitor (NRTI) Emtricitabine (FTC) has been developed for subcutaneous administration. Methods: The present study focused on the acute immunocompatibility of an FTC-based POP and its interactions with various cells and components of the immune system following acute exposure using DMSO-dispersed polymer linear poly(FTC). A tiered assessment was carried out, including assessment of pyrogens (MAT), cytotoxicity (MTT/LDH), Leukocyte proliferation (MTT), complement proteins (iC3b, Factor H, sC5b-9, Bb and C4d EIAs) and cytokine secretion in whole blood (Luminex panel). Results: Linear poly(FTC) had no detectable pyrogenic activity, no overt cytotoxicity within the THP-1 cell line, no consistent leukocyte proliferative activation and no broad whole-blood cytokine induction. Complement analysis, however, indicated a concentration-associated higher iC3b signal by linear poly(FTC) and a higher Bb signal by linear poly(FTC) at 80 µg/mL when compared to vehicle (0.4% DMSO). Conclusions: Further investigations are warranted to assess the long-term implications of these implants, given their extended residence times. Therefore, the adaptation of existing safety assessments should be prioritized to facilitate the safe translation of these POPs into clinical studies.

articles.title: Biochemical and Functional Characterization of LIZ, a Marine-Derived Serine Protease That Degrades Cross-Linked Fibrin and Attenuates Experimental Thrombosis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Direct fibrin-degrading proteases may provide a mechanistically distinct approach to clot proteolysis, but their development requires definition of catalytic behavior, fibrin selectivity, molecular identity, and safety. We characterized an activity-containing preparation from the marine polychaete Lepidasthenia izukai, designated LIZ. Methods: LIZ was obtained by ammonium sulfate fractionation and sequential chromatography. N-terminal sequencing, inhibitor profiling, chromogenic-substrate screening and S-2288 kinetics, fibrinogenolysis, direct fibrin-degradation assays, a κ-carrageenan rat-tail thrombosis model, and cell viability were evaluated. Results: The final preparation showed a predominant band at approximately 28 kDa. N-terminal sequencing yielded IMGGSEAS, providing sequence-level characterization without definitive molecular identification. PMSF abolished activity and DFP reduced it to 9.8%, supporting a serine-protease biochemical profile. For S-2288, Km was 0.029 ± 0.003 mM and apparent kcat/Km was 39.7 ± 4.3 mM-1 s-1. LIZ degraded fibrinogen Aα within 30 s and Bβ and γ within 20 min, decreased pre-formed fibrin-polymer turbidity, and degraded FXIIIa-cross-linked fibrin. In the pretreatment model, thrombotic tail length was 0.7 ± 1.0% with LIZ, 86.1 ± 3.2% with κ-carrageenan alone, and 0.5 ± 0.6% with uPA (n = 3/group). Conclusions: LIZ shows direct activity against structurally stabilized fibrin and proof-of-concept antithrombotic activity. However, the data do not establish definitive molecular identity, therapeutic thrombolysis, fibrin selectivity, relative potency, or a therapeutic safety window. Further molecular, pharmacological, and safety studies are required.

articles.title: Preparation of Excipient-Free Molnupiravir Microparticles for Pulmonary Drug Delivery and Process Evaluation via Machine Learning.
articles.abstract: Background/Objective: Molnupiravir (EIDD-2801) was originally designed to treat influenza A virus and showed broad-spectrum antiviral activity, including against influenza virus, Ebola virus, coronavirus and other viruses. Methods: In this study, molnupiravir microparticles were firstly prepared by spray freeze-drying (SFD) and jet milling (JM) methods. Meanwhile, machine learning methodology was applied to evaluate the influence of process parameters such as feeding rate, concentration, and nebulization pressure on powder properties. Results: According to SEM images, the microparticles prepared by SFD presented a porous and near-spherical structure. Moreover, the fine particle fraction (FPF) and mass median aerodynamic diameter (MMAD) of the optimal inhalable powder reached up to 70.19 ± 2.06% and 2.80 ± 0.16 μm, proving the excellent aerodynamic performance. Conclusions: The molnupiravir micropowder showed preliminary short-term storage behavior after storage for 28 days at 25 °C and 60% RH.

articles.title: Pyrvinium Attenuates Amiodarone-Induced Pulmonary Fibrosis in Male Rats: Association with Modulation of Wnt/β-Catenin Related Proteins.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Amiodarone (AmoD) is an effective antiarrhythmic drug whose use is limited by life-threatening pulmonary fibrosis. Although Wnt/β-catenin signaling contributes to several lung diseases, its involvement in AmoD-induced pulmonary fibrosis remains unknown. This study investigated whether Wnt/β-catenin signaling is altered during AmoD-induced pulmonary fibrosis and whether its pharmacological modulation with pyrvinium (Pyrv) attenuates this toxicity. Methods: Rats were allocated into four groups and treated for five weeks as follows: normal control, AmoD (30 mg/kg/day), Pyrv (60 µg/kg/day), and AmoD + Pyrv. Pulmonary injury and fibrosis were evaluated using histopathological examination, Masson's trichrome staining, immunohistochemical assessment of collagen I, α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), and transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1), and measurement of inflammatory cytokines, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and interleukin-6 (IL-6), and Th1/Th2-related cytokines. Wnt/β-catenin-associated proteins, including Wnt3a, active β-catenin, and glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK-3β), were evaluated by Western blotting. Results: AmoD induced marked pulmonary architectural disruption, inflammatory cell infiltration, increased lung weight/body weight ratio, collagen deposition, and increased expression of TGF-β1, α-SMA, and collagen I, as well as increased levels of TNF-α, IL-6, and disruption of Th1/Th2 immune balance. At the molecular level, AmoD increased Wnt3a, active β-catenin, and the p-GSK-3β/total GSK-3β ratio. Co-administration of Pyrv significantly attenuated the histopathological, inflammatory, immune, and fibrotic alterations and reduced the AmoD-associated changes in Wnt/β-catenin-related proteins. Conclusions: The findings indicate that AmoD-induced pulmonary injury and fibrosis are associated with modulation of Wnt/β-catenin related proteins and that Pyrv treatment attenuates these pathological changes. Targeting this pathway could be a promising protective strategy to prevent fibrogenesis during AmoD treatment.

articles.title: A Mesalazine-Aloperine Co-Amorphous System for Simultaneous Dissolution Enhancement, Permeability Improvement, and Synergistic Anti-Ulcerative Colitis Activity: A Combined Pharmaceutics and Network Pharmacology Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Mesalazine (MSZ), the first-line therapy for ulcerative colitis (UC), is a BCS Class IV drug limited by poor aqueous solubility and low intestinal permeability, which together restrict colonic drug delivery and therapeutic efficacy. This study aimed to develop a co-amorphous (CAM) system of MSZ and aloperine (ALO) to enhance MSZ dissolution and permeation while achieving anti-UC synergy. Methods: The MSZ-ALO CAM system was prepared via solvent evaporation and characterized by PXRD, DSC, FTIR, and 1H NMR. Equilibrium solubility, intrinsic dissolution rate (IDR), and in vitro permeability were assessed under biorelevant pH conditions. Physical stability was evaluated under long-term and accelerated conditions. Network pharmacology predicted potential therapeutic targets and synergistic mechanisms. Results: Solid-state characterization confirmed a homogeneous single-phase CAM system stabilized mainly by a carboxylate-ammonium ionic bond and hydrogen bonding. At pH 4.5, where MSZ solubility was lowest, equilibrium solubility and IDR increased up to 71.9-fold and 35.8-fold, respectively. In vitro permeability at pH 6.5 increased 2-fold. The system remained physically stable for eight months under dry conditions and withstood accelerated stresses without recrystallization. Network pharmacology identified 51 shared targets among MSZ, ALO, and UC, enriched in MAPK, HIF-1, and AMPK pathways; core hubs included HSP90AA1, SRC, CASP3, GSK3B, and ALB. Conclusions: This study presented the first MSZ-ALO CAM system that simultaneously addresses the dual solubility and permeability barriers of MSZ and provided a multi-target pharmacological basis for synergistic UC therapy, offering a promising pharmaceutical strategy for colon-targeted delivery.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Quality Control of Pharmaceutical Tablets: A Visual Dataset and Benchmark for Automated Defect Detection.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Automated visual inspection of pharmaceutical tablets is increasingly important for detecting manufacturing defects and maintaining consistent product quality. Progress in artificial intelligence-based defect classification is, however, constrained by the scarcity of publicly accessible image datasets covering defective tablets under diverse visual conditions. This study introduces the PharmaVision (PV) dataset, a public visual dataset and benchmark for classifying normal and defective compressed tablets. Methods: The PV dataset contains 640 smartphone-acquired images spanning varied tablet products, backgrounds, and lighting, with fixed tablet-level splits (190/190 training, 30/30 validation, and 100/100 test images for the normal and defective classes, respectively). Twelve representative architectures spanning classical convolutional networks, mobile networks, and vision transformers were benchmarked under an identical protocol using accuracy, precision, recall, and harmonic mean of precision and recall (F1-score), with 95% confidence intervals and paired statistical tests. Cross-dataset generalization was assessed on the independent pillQC dataset without fine-tuning, and efficiency was profiled using parameters, Giga floating-point operations (GFLOPs), latency, and throughput. Results: EfficientNetV2-S achieved the highest F1-score on the PV test set (88.56%), although paired statistical tests did not distinguish it from Xception (87.08%) or Swin-B (85.71%). On pillQC, GoogLeNet and EfficientNetV2-S showed the strongest cross-dataset performance, whereas both vision transformers declined relative to their in-domain results. AlexNet gave the highest theoretical throughput (602.41 frames per second (FPS), median latency 1.66 ms), whereas ShuffleNetV2 and MobileNetV3-small offered the smallest parameter counts. Conclusions: In-domain accuracy, cross-dataset robustness, and measured latency diverged, with no single architecture best on all three axes. The PV dataset, code, and evaluation protocol are publicly available on GitHub to support reproducible AI-based tablet quality control.

articles.title: Preparation and Investigation of Solvatomorphs of Anti-Tumor Candidate RA-XII.
articles.abstract: RA-XII, a unique natural cyclopeptide, is a potential anti-colorectal cancer candidate by mainly inhibiting protective autophagy, SREBP-1-dependent lipid biogenesis and suppressing activation of the Akt-mTOR pathway in HCT-116 cells. However, there have been no investigations into its solid forms, and its poor solubility restricts its application in the development of clinical anticancer agents. Background/Objectives: To investigate and develop advantageous medicinal solid forms of RA-XII and further improve its solubility characteristics. Methods: Various recrystallization methods were used to screen crystal forms of RA-XII, and single crystals (Forms I, II and V) were obtained by the vapor diffusion method. The forms were characterized by powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), spectroscopy (FTIR, Raman), thermal analyses (DSC, TGA) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Structural parameters were determined by single crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD). The solubility and intrinsic dissolution rate were determined in a pH 7.4 pharmaceutical buffer solution with water. Hirshfeld surface analyses, molecular electrostatic potential surface (MEPs) analyses and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were employed to reveal differences in hydrogen bond interactions of the crystal structure. Results: Five solvatomorphs and an amorphous form of RA-XII were successfully obtained. Then, three single crystals of Forms I, II and V were obtained, and their conformations were investigated. Hirshfeld surface analyses and crystal structures revealed significant differences in hydrogen bonding interactions and molecular packing. Moreover, MEPs analyses and MD suggested the formation mechanisms of RA-XII solvatomorphs, in which the hydrogen bonding strengths increase between RA-XII and solvent molecules. Conclusions: Form I is physically more stable and exhibits great solubility in water. Form I possesses significant medicinal advantages. These findings provide valuable insights into understanding the solvatomorph mechanisms and the quality control of RA-XII.

articles.title: Brazilian Red Propolis Extract-Loaded Colloidal Systems Derived from Microemulsion Compositions: Physicochemical, Antioxidant, and Antileishmanial Properties.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Brazilian red propolis is a rich source of isoflavonoids with promising antioxidant and antileishmanial activities. However, its poor aqueous solubility and chemical instability limit its pharmaceutical application. This study aimed to develop microemulsion-based systems containing high concentrations of Brazilian red propolis extract (RPE) and evaluate their physicochemical properties, phytochemical composition, antioxidant capacity, and antileishmanial activity. Methods: Pseudoternary phase diagrams were constructed by water titration to select suitable microemulsion compositions. RPE was subsequently incorporated into the selected compositions to obtain RPE-loaded colloidal systems. The three selected RPE-free microemulsions and their corresponding RPE-loaded systems were characterized by pH, electrical conductivity, dynamic light scattering, rheological measurements, and polarized light microscopy (PLM). The RPE-loaded systems were further evaluated for phenolic marker content, antioxidant activity, and in vitro activity against Leishmania infantum. Results: Three RPE-loaded colloidal systems (F2-RPE12, F3-RPE30, and F4-RPE50) were developed. F2-RPE12 exhibited characteristics consistent with an oil-in-water microemulsion. Conductivity and PLM indicated physicochemical changes after RPE incorporation in F3-RPE30 and F4-RPE50, with localized birefringent features at higher RPE concentrations. Among the RPE-loaded systems, F4-RPE50 showed the highest phenolic and flavonoid contents and antioxidant activity. The RPE-loaded systems exhibited lower IC50 values than RPE alone, with IC50 values of 3.14, 2.28, and 0.56 µg·mL-1 for F2-RPE12, F3-RPE30, and F4-RPE50, respectively, compared with 5.90 µg·mL-1 for RPE. Conclusions: Overall, F4-RPE50 showed the most favorable phytochemical and biological performance, and the physicochemical and optical changes observed in the RPE-loaded systems open new avenues for investigating the relationship between structural organization and formulation performance.

articles.title: An Engineered Floating Nanoparticulate System to Modulate Biopharmaceutical Performance and Therapeutic Efficacy of Tapentadol in Chronic Neuropathic Pain Management.
articles.abstract: Background: Tapentadol is an effective centrally acting analgesic for treating neuropathic pain. However, its short half-life, high first-pass metabolism, and requirement for frequent dosing limit its therapeutic effect and patient compliance. The purpose of the present innovation was to develop cost-effective tapentadol-loaded floating nanoparticles (TFNs) for sustained oral delivery. Methods: TFNs were prepared using the double emulsion solvent evaporation method. The effects of various formulation and process parameters, including polymer ratio, drug concentration, surfactant concentration and type, sonication time, and external phase volume were systematically studied. Analytical physicochemical characterization, morphology, buoyancy and drug release behavior were carried out. In vivo performance was evaluated by performing pharmacokinetic, tissue distribution, and pharmacodynamics studies in a chronic constriction injury model. Results: The optimized formulation exhibited spherical shape with nano-size (320.66 ± 17.50 nm), and good entrapment efficiency (82.85 ± 6.57%). Analytical characterization confirmed successful drug encapsulation and compatibility with formulation components. The engineered floating nanoparticulate architecture allowed both long gastric drug retention and a controlled drug release, governed by an anomalous diffusion-controlled mechanism. Pharmacokinetic evaluation revealed 3.36-fold higher relative oral bioavailability from TFNs. In addition, 1.49-fold higher drug availability in brain with TFNs was observed. Pharmacodynamic studies demonstrated a marked reduction in neuropathic pain responses, confirming the superior and prolonged analgesic effect of TFNs. Conclusions: The findings establish the developed TFNs as a promising controlled-release system for effective and sustained management of neuropathic pain. Even so, further studies focusing on large-scale production, long-term safety, and clinical evaluation are necessary before the formulation can be advanced for clinical application.

articles.title: Myricetin Modulates Quorum Sensing-Associated Phenotypes, Virulence, and Biofilm Formation in Pathogenic Bacteria: In Vitro and In Silico Studies.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The rapid emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) among pathogenic bacteria has necessitated the development of alternative therapeutic strategies that target bacterial virulence rather than cell viability. Methods: In this study, the flavonoid myricetin was systematically evaluated for its antibacterial, QS-associated phenotypic and biofilm formation-inhibitory activities against clinically relevant bacterial pathogens. Results: Myricetin exhibited moderate antibacterial activity and significantly reduced several QS-associated phenotypes. Violacein and prodigiosin production were reduced by 74.59% and 64.32%, respectively, consistent with QS-modulatory activity under the tested conditions. Furthermore, myricetin markedly attenuated key virulence factors in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, including pyocyanin (70.44%), pyoverdine (75.84%), and rhamnolipids (48.69%). In addition, concentration-dependent reductions in biofilm formation and extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) production was observed across all tested strains. Molecular docking predicted favourable interactions of myricetin with key QS regulatory proteins, particularly CviR and LasR, which was supported by molecular dynamics simulations. Notably, the LasR-myricetin complex showed greater computational stability among the evaluated complexes, supporting its potential role as a key interaction site. Conclusions: This study provides an integrated experimental and computational evaluation of myricetin-mediated modulation of QS-associated phenotypes across multiple bacterial systems, demonstrating reductions in virulence-factor production and biofilm formation under the tested conditions. Collectively, these findings position myricetin as a promising anti-virulence candidate, although further studies are required to validate its clinical applicability.

articles.title: Mannose-Functionalized Polymeric Micelles Target CD206-Expressing Macrophages Within Human Tuberculosis Granulomas and Improve Isoniazid Delivery.
articles.abstract: Background: Latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) remains a global health challenge, in part due to the ability of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) to persist within granulomatous lesions where drug exposure may be limited. Because granulomas are heterogeneous structures composed of different macrophage populations, targeting disease-relevant intracellular niches may improve antimicrobial treatment. Here, we developed mannose-functionalized polymeric micelles loaded with isoniazid (INH) to target mannose receptor (CD206)-expressing macrophages within a human tuberculosis granuloma model. Methods: Mannose-functionalized Soluplus® micelles loaded with INH (ManPM-INH) and non-functionalized micelles (PM-INH) were characterized for particle size, polydispersity, and colloidal stability. Antimycobacterial activity against MtbH37Rv was evaluated by CFU assays. A human peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) three-dimensional in vitro granuloma model was used to assess micelle accumulation and antimycobacterial activity. Cellular uptake was evaluated in M0, M1, and M2 macrophages using rhodamine-labeled micelles. CD206-associated and clathrin-mediated uptake were investigated using D-mannose and chlorpromazine, respectively. Results: ManPM-INH exhibited suitable physicochemical properties and maintained colloidal stability after mannose functionalization. In the granuloma model, ManPM showed significantly greater intracellular accumulation than PM. M2-like macrophages predominated within granulomas, and ManPM displayed preferential uptake by M2 macrophages. Furthermore, D-mannose competitively reduced ManPM uptake in macrophages with significantly greater inhibition in M2 cells. Chlorpromazine reduced ManPM internalization, supporting involvement of a clathrin-dependent pathway. ManPM-INH achieved the greatest reduction in intracellular MtbH37Rv burden compared with INH and PM-INH, particularly at low drug concentrations. Conclusions: Mannose-functionalized micelles enhance intracellular INH delivery by targeting CD206-expressing macrophages within tuberculosis granuloma, supporting macrophage-targeted nanotherapeutic strategies against persistent intracellular Mtb.

articles.title: 3D-Printed Gastroretentive Floating Modified-Release Device for Dual Cardiovascular Drug Delivery: Isosorbide Dinitrate and Hydralazine.
articles.abstract: Background: Isosorbide dinitrate (ISDN) and hydralazine hydrochloride (HDZ) are dual cardiovascular drugs used to treat heart failure. However, the drugs have limitations such as short plasma half-life, low bioavailability, and potential for tolerance of the nitrate component. To address the need for prolonged drug release, a floating dual-compartment drug delivery system was developed to provide controlled drug release under simulated gastric dissolution conditions. Objectives: This study aimed to develop floating dual-compartment devices (FDCDs) to contain ISDN and HDZ gel and modify drug release under simulated gastric conditions. Methods: The FDCD was designed in a cylindrical shape consisting of an air chamber on the upper part for floating ability, and two compartments for loaded drug gel and controlling the drug release rate. Fused deposition modeling (FDM) was selected to fabricate FDCDs using polylactic acid (PLA) filament. The ISDN formulation varied the ratio of polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) to achieve drug release for 12 h. The HDZ formulation was optimized by varying the ratio of PVP and hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) to extend drug release at 24 h. Results: The shape dimension and weight variation in the FDCDs showed low standard deviation (SD). FDCDs exhibited immediate floating, resisted overturning, and demonstrated in vitro floating ability for more than 24 h. The formulation ISDN3 at a PVP: drug: water ratio of 5:2:3 exhibited complete release at 12 h, while the formulation of HDZ1 at an HPMC: PVP: drug: water ratio of 0.3:2.5:2:5.2 showed complete release within 24 h. The ISDN3- and HDZ1-loaded FDCDs demonstrated prolonged release behavior, with ISDN and HDZ release profiles showing the best fit to the zero-order and Higuchi models, respectively, based primarily on the coefficient of determination (R2), while root mean square error (RMSE) was used as a complementary measure of fitting error. Conclusions: These findings suggest that the developed dual-drug-loaded FDCD has potential as a dual-drug oral delivery platform for simultaneous delivery of ISDN and HDZ with prolonged drug release characteristics and further development of oral combination drug delivery systems.

articles.title: Development of Pectin-Coated Cationic Liposomes for Sustained Drug Release, Enhanced Serum Stability and Reduced Macrophage Uptake.
articles.abstract: Background: Cationic liposomes are promising carriers for anticancer agents but are often limited by rapid clearance by the mononuclear phagocyte system, poor serum stability, and insufficient control of drug release. This study aimed to develop and characterize pectin-coated, Ca2+-crosslinked cationic liposomes as a multifunctional delivery platform providing sustained release, enhanced serum stability, and reduced macrophage uptake while preserving the biological activity of an encapsulated anticancer compound. Methods: The optimal polysaccharide-to-liposome ratio was established by ζ-potential polyelectrolyte titration, and coating parameters were optimized using a Taguchi experimental design. Physicochemical characterization included dynamic light scattering (DLS), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). The optimized formulations were further evaluated for drug release, serum stability, cellular uptake and cytotoxicity against A549 and HeLa cells using MTT and Neutral Red assays. Results: Polyelectrolyte titration identified a pectin-to-liposome saturation ratio of 3:1, and Taguchi optimization yielded a formulation with a drug retention efficiency of 99.34%. Pectin coating significantly reduced the initial burst release (37.9% at 1 h) and decreased cumulative drug release after 48 h (66.3%), consistent with a polymer relaxation-controlled release mechanism. The coated liposomes also exhibited enhanced serum stability and reduced macrophage uptake (up to ~73% lower in RAW264.7 cells), while maintaining uptake by non-phagocytic cells. The biological activity of the encapsulated model compound was preserved, with enhanced cancer-cell selectivity against A549 and HeLa cells demonstrated by both MTT and Neutral Red assays. Conclusions: Pectin-Ca2+ surface functionalization transforms cationic liposomes into a stable sustained-release delivery platform with reduced macrophage recognition and enhanced serum stability. These findings support the further development of this carrier as a versatile platform for the systemic delivery of anticancer agents.

articles.title: Integrated Analysis of Microbiome and Serum Metabolomics to Understand How Rauvolfia vomitoria Alkaloids Inhibit Colorectal Cancer Growth.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Rauvolfia vomitoria alkaloids (RVA) exhibited excellent activity against colorectal cancer (CRC) growth in the heterotopic model. However, their antitumor effects in the orthotopic models, as well as the underlying mechanisms related to gut microbiota and serum metabolomics, remain poorly understood. Methods: We performed 16S rRNA sequencing and serum metabolomics analysis in orthotopic CRC-bearing mice following different treatments. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were used to screen key gut microbes and metabolites associated with RVA treatments. KEGG enrichment analysis was conducted to identify the metabolic pathways modulated by RVAs in vivo. Results: RVA, either alone or in combination with 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU), exhibited a potent inhibitory effect on CRC growth, comparable to intraperitoneally administered 5-FU. In terms of body weight and organ indices, RVA showed lower toxicity compared to 5-FU. Both treatments induced measurable shifts in the gut microbial profiles of CRC mice. Increased abundance of Akkermansia and Lactobacillus and decreased abundance of Enterococcus were found to be associated with RVA monotherapy. The enrichment of Acinetobacter and Mucispirillum in CRC mice was suppressed by the combination treatment. A serum metabolomics study revealed that linoleic acid metabolism and β-oxidation of long-chain fatty acids were modulated by both RVA-containing regimens. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate that oral administration of RVA, either alone or combined with current clinical therapeutic methods, may represent a promising strategy for CRC treatment. Targeted modulation of gut microbiota and fatty acid metabolism may provide promising approaches to hinder CRC progression.

articles.title: Oxaprozin-Based Amide Derivatives as Multifunctional Agents: Synthesis, Characterization, and Comprehensive Biological Profiling.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Inflammation plays a role at multiple levels, contributing to tumorigenesis, cellular proliferation, cell survival, and metastasis. The established link between chronic inflammation and tumor development has shifted the therapeutic focus toward nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, which exert their effects primarily through cyclooxygenase inhibition. Methods: In the present study, the antitumor potential of novel synthesized oxaprozin derivatives was evaluated using the MTT assay. The immunomodulatory effects of the selected derivative were determined in vitro by measuring cytokine concentrations and performing flow cytometry. To investigate the inhibitory capacity of these derivatives against cyclooxygenase enzymes, an in vitro inhibition assay was conducted using fluorometric screening kits, followed by in silico validation. Results: All tested tumor cell lines exhibited sensitivity to compound 1, which demonstrated the lowest cytotoxic effect against non-cancerous mMSCs and MRC-5 cells. This compound can effectively target tumor cells, inducing potent apoptosis in 4T1 breast cancer cells through a strategic shift in the Bax/Bcl-2 balance and the downregulation of the oncogenic driver Bcl-6. Although the synthesized oxaprozin derivatives showed moderate affinity for COX-1, none of the newly synthesized compounds achieved more than 50% inhibition against COX-2 at a concentration of 100 μM. Consistently, in silico procedures validated the results of the in vitro COX inhibition assay. Conclusions: The findings of this study indicate that compound 1 has the ability to modulate immune responses under stimulated conditions, and its potent antitumor activity may not be directly related to cyclooxygenase inhibition, suggesting the involvement of COX-independent pathways.

articles.title: Development and Characterization of Shikonin-Loaded NLC with Enhanced Photostability in Hydrogel-Based Dermal Patch.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Shikonin is a bioactive compound with promising pharmaceutical potential, particularly for anti-inflammation and ability to inhibit proliferative scar formation. However, its applications are limited by poor photostability. Therefore, this research aimed to develop and optimize shikonin-loaded NLC to improve the photostability of shikonin. The optimized NLC formulation was subsequently incorporated into a hydrogel matrix to fabricate a dermal patch, providing a potential alternative for topical scar treatment and self-care application. Methods: Shikonin-loaded NLCs were developed, optimized, and evaluated for physicochemical properties, entrapment efficiency, photostability, and in vitro release. The optimized NLC was incorporated into a hyaluronic acid-carboxymethyl cellulose hydrogel matrix to fabricate and evaluate an NLC-based dermal patch. Results: The optimized shikonin-loaded NLC exhibited a particle size of 104.94 nm with a narrow polydispersity index of 0.15, and a zeta potential of -34.34 ± 0.02 mV. The NLC achieved high entrapment efficiency (>90%). The NLC significantly enhanced the photostability of shikonin, by increasing the percentage of shikonin remaining after light exposure from 37.36 to 64.55% (p < 0.05). In addition, the cumulative shikonin release over 12 h was 15.61 ± 4.18%, following Korsmeyer-Peppas model. A combination of hyaluronic acid and carboxymethyl cellulose (1% w/w) was employed as the biopolymer for the hydrogel dermal patch. The shikonin-loaded NLC-based dermal patch exhibited favorable physicochemical characteristics. Conclusions: The NLC demonstrated enhanced photostability and release properties, which are preserved upon their integration into the hydrogel. The incorporation of shikonin-loaded NLC into a hydrogel matrix provides a viable strategy for stabilizing this light-sensitive bioactive compound. Consequently, this NLC-loaded hydrogel system represents a promising platform for future topical dermal delivery in pharmaceutical and cosmetic applications.

articles.title: Tislelizumab-induced immune-mediated hepatotoxicity combined with two episodes of hepatitis B virus reactivation: a case report.
articles.abstract: Immune-mediated hepatotoxicity (IMH) is a typical immune-related adverse event associated with the use of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), while hepatitis B virus reactivation (HBVr) is an infectious complication that may also occur during ICI therapy. However, these two conditions are usually independent and rarely co-occur in the same individual. Herein, we describe a patient with lung squamous cell carcinoma who developed HBVr and IMH simultaneously after receiving tislelizumab, and the co-existence of two episodes of HBVr brings challenges to the diagnosis and treatment of IMH. In the diagnosis of IMH, the co-existence of HBVr masked the underlying IMH, resulting in a delay in IMH treatment. In the treatment of IMH, the re-occurrence of HBVr led to a dilemma of continuing to use glucocorticoids (GCs) or stopping them. In such a clinical scenario, the multidisciplinary approach, close monitoring of liver function and HBV-DNA, and a carefully balanced treatment strategy combining GCs with intensified antiviral therapy are essential to realize the optimal management for IMH. In conclusion, medical staff should be alert to the coexistence of HBVr and IMH in patients receiving ICIs, so as to avoid missed diagnosis and treatment delay.

articles.title: Next-Generation Bioinspired Microneedle Systems for Peptide Delivery: Bridging Design and Translational Medicine.
articles.abstract: Peptide-based therapies have transformed the management of chronic illnesses such as diabetes, cancer, and cardiovascular problems, owing to their remarkable specificity, effectiveness, and low toxicity. Nonetheless, their therapeutic efficacy is frequently impeded by obstacles such as inadequate bioavailability, fast enzymatic breakdown, and restricted systemic stability. Conventional delivery strategies, such as oral and intravenous injection, have considerable constraints in efficiently transporting peptides to target locations. Transdermal drug delivery systems, especially microneedles (MNs) and bioinspired microneedles (BMNs), have garnered considerable interest as a less invasive and effective option to surmount these obstacles. MNs form microchannels in the epidermis and dermis, facilitating the direct administration of peptides into systemic circulation, hence dramatically improving peptide delivery across the skin. Recent improvements in BMNs technology have enhanced peptide delivery through better mechanical strength, skin contact, and controlled release. This paper mainly focuses on the importance of peptide drugs, the obstacles related to their administration, and the potential of BMNs for effective transdermal delivery. We emphasize current advancements in BMNs that improve peptide stability, permeability, and therapeutic effectiveness, facilitating their practical use in the treatment of chronic and acute disorders.

articles.title: NanoMiLens (Nano-Micelle Loaded Hydrogel Contact Lenses) of Tofacitinib Citrate: Amalgamation, Development, Optimization and Characterization.
articles.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a multifactorial inflammatory eye disease caused mainly by immune dysregulation through JAK/STAT, which leads to a turbulent tear film, damage to the corneal epithelia, and poor visualization. Topical therapies of the conventional type show less ocular bioavailability with quick precorneal excretion. This research was done to design and test a new NanoMiLens system loaded with Tofacitinib Citrate (TFC), which is a selective JAK inhibitor, in order to have a controlled and prolonged contact lens delivery manageable with DED. TFC Polymeric Nano-Micelles (PoT-PNMs) were prepared using a thin-film hydration method employing Poloxamer 407 as the amphiphilic polymer and Tween 80 as the stabilizing surfactant in acetone, then rehydrated with simulated tear fluid. PBD ANOVA confirmed polymer concentration and surfactant concentration as dominant factors for EE%. CCD quadratic modelling yielded R2 = 0.9904 for EE%, 0.9789 for CDR%, and 0.9408 for particle size, with model validation errors < 1%. The optimized PoT-PNMs (200 mg Poloxamer 407, 0.30 mL Tween 80) achieved particle size 92 ± 2.6 nm, PDI 0.246, EE% 90.60 ± 0.44%, and CDR% 93.10 ± 1.2% over 12 h. FTIR, DSC, and XRD confirmed drug amorphization and drug-excipient compatibility. The optimized PoT-PNMs were loaded into freeze-thaw-crosslinked PVA/pHEMA hydrogel contact lenses via soak-loading. The optimized PoT-PNMs -loaded contact lens (NMCL12) showed % transmittance 96.11 ± 0.22%, swelling index 96.48 ± 0.24%, drug content 90.60 ± 0.44%, in-vitro CDR% 96.50 ± 0.30% over 12 h, and mechanical strength 142 ± 6 folds. This system is an effective, scalable method of topical immunomodulatory treatment of inflammatory dry eye disease.

articles.title: Design, Characterization and In Vivo Evaluation of Rifaximin-Loaded Chitosan Nanoparticles for Potential Colonic Drug Delivery in Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to develop rifaximin (RFX) loaded chitosan (CS)-tripolyphosphate (TPP) nanoparticles for potential colonic delivery as a drug delivery system for the management of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). Nanoparticles were prepared using the ionotropic gelation method and optimized by varying stirring speed, TPP concentration, and polymer-to-drug ratio. The optimized formulation (F41) exhibited a particle size of 262.4 ± 24.3 nm, a polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.389 ± 0.033, a zeta potential of + 9.91 ± 0.94 mV, and an encapsulation efficiency (EE%) of 94.75 ± 0.04%. In vitro release studies demonstrated nearly complete drug release within 36 h, which was faster compared to other formulations (52-64 h). Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) confirmed spherical morphology, while differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) analyses indicated successful drug encapsulation without chemical interaction. In vivo evaluation using a chronic restraint stress (CRS) induced IBS model showed that F41 significantly improved physiological parameters, including reduced fecal water content (20.655 ± 23.494%), increased body weight gain (22.716 ± 3.903%), and a decreased disease activity index (p < 0.05). These findings indicate that, the optimized nanoparticle system demonstrated favorable physicochemical properties, sustained drug release, and improved therapeutic outcomes. Owing to the cationic nature of CS, the system may also provide enhanced interaction with colonic mucus, potentially contributing to prolonged local residence. These findings suggest that the developed formulation represents promising approach for potential colonic delivery of RFX in IBS management; however, further studies are required to directly evaluate its mucoadhesive properties and underlying mechanisms.

articles.title: Colorimetric Microplate Assay Coupled with Nonlinear Mixed-Effects Modeling for High-Throughput Evaluation of Ophthalmic Preservatives.
articles.abstract: Conventional preservative efficacy tests for ophthalmic formulations rely on discrete colony counts and therefore provide limited insight into the dynamic processes of microbial inactivation and recovery. Such endpoint-based evaluations can obscure formulation-dependent differences in antimicrobial performance and hinder rational optimization of preservative systems. In this study, we developed a quantitative framework that integrates a high-throughput WST-8-based colorimetric microplate assay with nonlinear mixed-effects (NLME) modeling to characterize bacterial killing and regrowth dynamics in borate-buffered systems. Escherichia coli responses were analyzed across 43 formulations using L27 orthogonal and Box-Behnken experimental designs. Bacterial inactivation was described by first-order kinetics, while post-exposure regrowth was modeled using a damage-dependent suppression term. The resulting hierarchical NLME model adequately described bacterial growth trajectories across all formulations, as confirmed by goodness-of-fit diagnostics, visual predictive checks, and bootstrap analyses. Multivariate covariate analysis suggested that borax and pH-related physicochemical conditions contributed to variability in bacterial inactivation rate constants, indicating that antimicrobial activity in borate systems is influenced by buffer composition and the associated physicochemical environment rather than by total borate concentration alone. By coupling structured experimental design with hierarchical population modeling, the proposed framework enables dynamic and mechanism-informed evaluation of preservative efficacy. This approach extends conventional endpoint-based testing and provides a quantitative platform for data-driven optimization and risk assessment of ophthalmic formulations.

articles.title: Assessment of the Mucoadhesion and Mucopermeation of Emulsifying Systems Containing Copaiba Oil on the Intestinal Mucosa.
articles.abstract: Mucopenetrating systems are drug delivery platforms designed to overcome the intestinal mucus barrier, facilitating access to epithelium and enhancing the bioavailability of lipophilic compounds. Copaiba oil (CO) is a compound displaying broad therapeutic potential but low aqueous solubility, which limits its bioavailability. This study aimed to assess how two CO-loaded delivery systems, an emulsion (EM) and a self-emulsifying system (SE), interact with the intestinal mucus layer and how effectively they permeate it. Thus, interactions with mucin and porcine intestinal mucosa were evaluated via oscillatory rheometry, by determining rheological synergism, and the in vitro and ex vivo mucoadhesion assays. The retention of the emulsion systems on the intestinal mucosa was also assessed, along with mucopermeation, using Transwell inserts coated with porcine intestinal mucus and mucin solution. Rheological analysis demonstrated a significant interaction between SE and mucin, evidenced by positive rheological synergism, whereas EM showed limited interaction. In mucoadhesion studies, EM behavior was primarily associated with its higher consistency, while SE exhibited more specific interactions with mucin. Ex vivo retention studies demonstrated greater retention of EM on the intestinal mucosa. In contrast, SE showed superior permeation through the mucus layer in mucopermeation assays, a behavior attributed to the presence of PEG 400. Overall, SE exhibited a more favorable balance between mucoadhesion and mucus penetration than EM. The SE demonstrated enhanced mucopermeation while maintaining adequate interaction with intestinal mucus, suggesting its potential as a promising oral delivery platform for improving the intestinal transport and bioavailability of copaiba oil.

articles.title: Integration of In Silico Degradation Prediction, Mechanistic Stress Testing, and Accelerated Stability Modeling for Olaparib Drug Substance and Prototype Formulation.
articles.abstract: A stability-assessment framework integrating Zeneth in silico degradation prediction, AIBN-mediated radical autoxidation, and ASAPprime® accelerated kinetic modeling was developed for olaparib drug substance and a prototype immediate-release tablet. Zeneth predicted benzylic oxidation as the dominant degradation pathway (pathway score 912). Under AIBN stress, Impurity 6 formed at 2.15%, with radical-initiator dependence confirmed by an AIBN-free control (< 0.1% total impurity); aqueous hydrogen peroxide (1.0%) provided degradant mass for LC-MS/MS characterization. Impurity 6 was confirmed as the benzylic ketone (C₂₄H₂₁FN₄O₄) against an authenticated reference standard (Schymanski Level 1; mass error + 0.7 ppm); the reprocessed HRMS/MS fragmentation ladder was fully reconciled with this assignment, and Impurity 6 was chromatographically resolved from its isomeric Impurity 4 (relative retention times 1.45 versus 1.02). Isoconversion ASAPprime® studies (drug substance: 50-80 °C/11-75% RH; formulation: 40-70°C/11-75% RH) were validated against 12-month real-time data. The drug substance followed first-order kinetics (Ea = 91.2 ± 6.7 kJ·mol⁻1) with negligible humidity sensitivity (B = 0.004 ± 0.003; p > 0.05), yielding a model-derived 95% confidence shelf-life estimate of 3.4 years (MAPD = 5.3%; Q2 = 0.96). The formulation showed accelerated kinetics (Ea = 85.4 ± 5.9 kJ·mol⁻1; B = 0.014 ± 0.005; p < 0.05) and a shelf-life estimate of 2.6 years (MAPD = 5.2%; Q2 = 0.93). These projections require confirmation by longer-term real-time data. The workflow provides a development stage stability risk assessment tool; Impurity 6 was structurally confirmed at Level 1 against an authenticated reference standard, and the formulation was single batch and unoptimized.

articles.title: Overcoming Biopharmaceutical Challenges in the Development of Amorphous Nanosuspension: A Case Study of Atazanavir.
articles.abstract: Amorphous nanosuspensions can generate supersaturated drug concentrations far above crystalline solubility, but their performance depends on stabilizing both the metastable amorphous phase and the high interfacial energy of nanosized particles against recrystallization and Ostwald ripening. ATZ was selected as a model weakly basic drug because its poor dissolution and rapid desupersaturation at intestinal pH provide a rational formulation space for probing the biopharmaceutical relevance of amorphous nanosuspensions. The present study addressed these limitations through the development of ATZ amorphous nanosuspension using acid-base neutralization method. Polymer-surfactant screening was performed through desupersaturation assay and drug-rich droplet size analysis which identified HPMCAS-MG and Soluplus as optimal precipitation inhibitors. Box-Behnken design optimization yielded nanosuspension with a mean particle size of 146.7 ± 5.56 nm and polydispersity index of 0.261 ± 0.05, and a zeta potential of - 4.54 ± 0.78 mV. Solid-state and spectroscopic analyses confirmed successful amorphization of ATZ and the presence of hydrogen-bonding and hydrophobic interactions in ATZ-ANS. Further, non-sink in vitro dissolution testing revealed that ATZ-ANS effectively sustained supersaturation with limited precipitation. The formulation retained its nanoscale characteristics and did not show evidence of recrystallization during six months of accelerated stability testing at 40 °C/75% relative humidity (RH). The in vivo pharmacokinetic evaluation in Sprague Dawley rats demonstrated that ATZ-ANS achieved 16.59-fold higher Cmax (ng/mL) and 6.31-fold higher AUC0-t (ng-h/mL) than crystalline ATZ, and a 2.08-fold and 3.22-fold increase over the marketed formulation (Reyataz®), respectively. Our findings highlighted amorphous nanosuspension as a pragmatic approach for difficult to deliver drugs.
